Poison Spell.name: Poison Spell
notes: The Poison Spell is the first Dark Spell unlocked in the Dark Spell Factory and is automatically unlocked once the Dark Spell Factory has finished being built, requiring the Town Hall to be at level 8. It slows down all enemy Clan Castle Troops , Heroes , and Skeletons inside its area of effect (and causes them to take damage over time). However, buildings remain unaffected by Poison Spells.
The Poison Spell slowly ramps up in damage the longer a unit stays poisoned. The effect lasts for an additional 6 seconds after the unit leaves the poison radius.

A Poison Spell has a circular area of effect for scaling damage, whereas a Lightning Spell strikes a small radius, dealing instantaneous damage. Making effectiveness of both spells depend on the defending base's layout, as well as what and where the Clan Castle Troops are, and the player's army composition.

As of September 18, 2015, Poison Spells do scaling damage in a similar manner to a single-target Inferno Tower , just to a lesser extent. This scaling effect dramatically affects high-hitpoint units but deals much less damage against Heroes for balancing reasons. The Poison Spell is still useful to slow defending Heroes down; however, a Freeze Spell can also be a good alternative, which can also affect defenses around them. It can also be used to slow the movement and attack speed of the opposing heroes down.

The Poison Spell is still useful to slow defending Heroes down; however, a Freeze Spell can also be a good alternative, which can also affect defenses around them. It can also be used to slow the movement and attack speed of the opposing heroes down.
It can also be used to slow the movement and attack speed of the opposing heroes down.

If you see a Dragon , Baby Dragon , Balloons , or Valkyries on defense, it is good to use a Poison Spell on them, as the scaling effect is deadly against high-hitpoint units. It also decreases their speed, which makes them slower to reach the target. Although a single Poison Spell will not fully wipe off very high hitpoint troops like Dragons, Electro Dragons , Golems , and P.E.K.K.As , its slowing effect makes them highly vulnerable to other troops while active.

Although a single Poison Spell will not fully wipe off very high hitpoint troops like Dragons, Electro Dragons , Golems , and P.E.K.K.As , its slowing effect makes them highly vulnerable to other troops while active.
Multiple stacked Poisons Spells will speed up the scaling process but will not increase the maximum damage per second, so typically it is a waste if you place many at once.

As of the March 2016 update, defending troops will automatically attempt to escape the Poison Spell's AOE if they are currently not targeting any troop, in which case they will ignore the spell entirely. Healers and Heroes are not affected, as Healers cannot attack enemy troops and defending Heroes have a limited targeting range already. However, it is currently unknown whether the Druids will run away from the Poison Spell, but the Bears will always attempt to escape from it.

A good offensive strategy is to lure the Clan Castle troops to the corner and then attack them with high-damage troops like the Wizard or a high number of Archers . Usually, when the Poison Spell is dropped on any defending troops, and if they do not have any target, then the defending troops will walk out of the radius. So, it is best to attack them with troops while the defending troops are inside the Poison Spell to get its full potential. Alternatively, you can use a Freeze Spell to make the Clan Castle troops unable to move, allowing the Poison Spell to ramp up in damage.
Alternatively, you can use a Freeze Spell to make the Clan Castle troops unable to move, allowing the Poison Spell to ramp up in damage.

As the Loading Screen Hints would say, it is a very effective answer to Skeletons spawned by Skeleton Traps . You can use another expendable troop to activate them, then deploy your Poison Spell to wipe them out.

More than one Poison Spell is normally not good. If you have a good idea of where an attacker may start a Queen or Warden Walk, then place a Hero such that their trigger radius is at or behind the Clan Castle trigger radius in that direction, so an attacker will have to fight a hero and the Clan Castle troops at the same time, potentially forcing more Poison Spells to be brought.

Earthquake Spell.name: Earthquake Spell
notes: "Weaken Walls and buildings with crippling earthquakes! Earthquake Spells damage structures based on their maximum hitpoints. Repeated Earthquakes deal decreasing damage to the same buildings, but increasing damage to the same Walls. No Wall can withstand the might of four Earthquake Spells!"

The Earthquake Boots ability counts as one Earthquake use, so using it will reduce the damage of future Earthquake Spells against the same target. The inverse is true: Earthquake Boots will do less damage against targets already affected by Earthquake Spells.

Four Earthquake Spells will destroy Walls of any level under all conditions. However, 3 Earthquake Spells of any level cannot destroy a Wall of any level. This is caused by the nature of the Earthquake Spell, which only deals percentage damage and no absolute amount of damage at all. The Earthquake's damage formula is slightly different on Walls: the n {\displaystyle n} th quake will do 1 / n {\displaystyle 1/n} as much damage, but every quake after the first also does additional damage equal to 5 ( n − 1 ) 2 {\displaystyle 5(n-1)^2} % of the Wall's maximum health (i.e. 5, 20 and 45% extra for the second through fourth Earthquake Spells respectively).

They are great to use as an alternative to Wall Breakers . As Earthquake Spells deal increasing damage to Walls , they are much more effective than using its counterpart, Lightning Spell, against Walls. They are therefore very useful for ground attacks if Walls might get in the way.

Unlike the Lightning Spell, Earthquake Spells can damage Town Halls and Clan Castles. Both have high health, and Clan Castle being taken out prematurely can prevent Clan Castle troops from spawning. Versus Town Halls of level 12 up to 16, if using defense-targeting troops, consider purposely triggering the Town Hall's defense by using an Earthquake spell so these troops will begin to target the Town Hall.

Against buildings that are close to a weaponized Builder's Hut, note that the Builder will be able to slowly repair all affected buildings in the radius. It is thus not advised to use four Earthquake Spells to open a compartment and/or damage the target buildings until your troops are nearing the compartment to be opened, to minimize the effects of the defending Builders. However, do not leave it too late either, as not doing so in time might mean your troops may be unnecessarily stuck on Walls or move away from the unopened compartments.

On the flipside, it could be advisable to instead use a Jump Spell to bypass a single compartment of Walls to optimize spell capacity in your army. Using 4 Earthquake Spells for a single compartment of Walls would often be inefficient and unnecessary in most cases.

Against opponents with Town Hall 14 or higher, Builder's Huts should be watched out for if attempting a Zapquake attack, as the Builders can repair buildings while the spells are doing damage. To prevent the Zapquake from failing, one should drop all of the spells involved as quickly as possible. It is advised to also bring more damage than is needed to destroy the target defenses, such that the Builder's repair fails to save the target defenses.

Using the Fireball alongside the Earthquake Spell will destroy a huge area of the base, provided that if both of them are sufficiently leveled to destroy main defenses. Otherwise, they will be severely damaged, and said defenses will eventually take out most of your army, if not all. Using the second Earthquake Spell can also allow it to increase the chances of destroying major defenses.
Using the second Earthquake Spell can also allow it to increase the chances of destroying major defenses.

The Seeking Shield can heavily damage defenses if they survive, which the Earthquake Spell can then be used to destroy them. It can serve as an alternative to the Rocket Spear if the defenses do survive, provided that if they have low enough health to be destroyed.

The Spiky Ball will damage buildings, and the Earthquake Spell can be used to take them down, especially if they are defensive buildings. Take note that resource storages are immune to damage by Earthquake Spells, so keep that in mind.
Take note that resource storages are immune to damage by Earthquake Spells, so keep that in mind.
The Giant Arrow can be used to damage buildings and pairing with the Earthquake Spell will help finish them off, provided if they do not have enough health to survive.
Earthquake Spells are only effective in destroying Walls in large numbers. Consider not allowing much value by either having very large or very small compartments.

Haste Spell.name: Haste Spell
notes: The Haste Spell is the 3rd Dark Elixir Spell unlocked at Dark Spell Factory level 3 that requires the Town Hall to be at level 9. Similar to a Rage Spell , it boosts the movement speed of troops in its area of effect, but to a greater effect; however, the Haste Spell does not increase their damage. The Haste Spell is half the housing space and also has a slightly smaller radius than the Rage Spell.
Like with Healing Spells and Rage Spells, the Haste Spell has a reduced effect on Heroes , only granting 50% of its speed boost to them.

Haste Spells may be used to counteract the effect of Air Sweepers . Deploy the spell on slow air troops such as Electro Dragons and Balloons , and it will counteract the effect of the Air Sweeper by putting them back into where they were faster. However, if you can destroy Air Sweepers, it is better to destroy them directly, as it is not the most consistent.

The Haste Spell is most effective in aiding slower but more powerful troops, such as Balloons , Electro Dragons , Root Riders , Golems and Ice Golems . It is also effective on troops with abilities that last only temporarily, such as the Rocket Balloon , so that they can make use of the ability against their targets for longer. However, troops with fast movement speed would not benefit much from this, as there is no damage increase. It also does not boost attack speed, unlike the Haste Vial .
This spell, when paired with the Invisibility Spell or Overgrowth Spell , can help to facilitate funneling, since the Haste guides the troops to the funneled area faster.

In Zap attacks, where the attacker brings lots of Lightning Spells , the Haste Spell is very important if the troops are slow but strong since the spell is much more efficient at moving troops than other spells.

You can also use the Haste Spell at the last seconds of the battle in which your slow troops are away of non-defensive buildings like a Builder's Hut , so that they are able to destroy it and get 3 stars. You can also drop the spell before the Giga Bomb explodes, avoiding the death damage, especially if the bomb leaves poison behind.
You can also drop the spell before the Giga Bomb explodes, avoiding the death damage, especially if the bomb leaves poison behind.

Clone Spell.name: Clone Spell
notes: "Turn this Spell into a pop-up army ! Clone Spells create a circle of spawning that creates limited-lifetime copies of troops that enter it. It will only spawn up to a maximum housing space of troops."

The Clone Spell is the 6th Elixir Spell unlocked at level 5 Spell Factory , requiring the Town Hall to be at level 10. As the name of this spell implies, it clones troops that enter the spell's radius.
The copied troops are equal in level to the original troop, and appear with full health. However, they only last a limited amount of time, and can be destroyed prematurely by defenses .

A Clone Spell can clone any troop type, including Super Troops , provided there is enough housing space for it (some temporary troops, such as Giant Giant , take up too much housing space and cannot be cloned). Heroes , Pets and Siege Machines cannot be cloned. It can also clone sub troops as well as troops spawned by Hero Equipment . Each subtroop has its own housing space value for this purpose. For example, each Skeleton (no matter how it is spawned), Bat or Frostmite has a housing space of 1, each Lava Pup , Ice Pup and Yetimite has a housing space of 2, each Golemite has 6, and each Big Boy has 10. Cloned troops are also able to be cloned by a Clone Spell as if they were normal troops.

It can also clone sub troops as well as troops spawned by Hero Equipment . Each subtroop has its own housing space value for this purpose. For example, each Skeleton (no matter how it is spawned), Bat or Frostmite has a housing space of 1, each Lava Pup , Ice Pup and Yetimite has a housing space of 2, each Golemite has 6, and each Big Boy has 10.
Cloned troops that spawn subtroops, such as Golems or Witches , will spawn these subtroops in a cloned state.
If more than one troop is inside the deployed Clone Spell, the troop spawned first will be cloned first.
For troops with death effects (such as Balloons or Ice Golems ), cloned troops that expire by overstepping their time limit will not exhibit any effects on death.

Cloning a Golem / Lava Hound at low health will create a new Golem/Lava Hound with full health. Use this to your advantage, as the cloned troop will be able to tank lots of damage, and for Lava Hounds, it will spawn more Lava Pups, which can distract the enemy and deal massive damage.

As the Clone Spell spawns clones randomly within its radius, you can place a Clone Spell partly over a layer of Walls to get some cloned troops behind them. This can be useful if you do not have Wall Breakers , Jump Spells or any other means of easily getting past the Walls. However, this should only be used in a pinch and if you do not have other solutions or if you are desparate.

Clone Spells can be used similarly to clone other Clan Castle complements, such as Super Wizards or Super Archers cloaked under Invisibility Spells . The additional clones can greatly amplify the power of such squads.

If a cloned troop with an effect on death expires by lasting its maximum duration, it does not inflict damage or any other effects that would normally occur if it is destroyed. This is important to note if the cloned troop has a significant effect on death (such as cloned Ice Golems or Super Valkyries ), as these beneficial effects will not occur then.

The behavior of the Clone Spell on Super Troops with temporary abilities is not consistent and differs between different Super Troops : Cloned Super Barbarians will not have their ability active when created, even if the original still has its ability active. Cloned Rocket Balloons and Sneaky Goblins will spawn with their respective abilities at full duration, even if the haste or cloak has already expired on the troop being cloned. Cloned Super Minions will spawn with all of its long shots available, even if the original Super Minion has already used some or all of its long shots.
Cloned Rocket Balloons and Sneaky Goblins will spawn with their respective abilities at full duration, even if the haste or cloak has already expired on the troop being cloned.
Cloned Super Minions will spawn with all of its long shots available, even if the original Super Minion has already used some or all of its long shots.

Cloned units only last for a limited time. Use Tornado Traps to stall them and limit their effectiveness. Multiple Wall layers can be useful too, unless if they can jump over, mine under, or blow them up by either walking or dying (in the case of Wall Breakers ).

The Clone Spell multiplies the troop with the lowest housing space, which is commonly low-hitpoint troops like the Miner , the Balloon , the Hog Rider , the Bowler , the Giant or the Wizard . Use splash damage defenses and protect them so they can help destroy the cloned troops.

Skeleton Spell.name: Skeleton Spell
notes: "Summon an army of Skeletons anywhere on the battlefield! Put a few extra swords when and where you need them most. Skeletons do not trigger traps ."

The Skeleton Spell is the 4th Dark Spell unlocked at level 4 Dark Spell Factory that requires the Town Hall to be at level 9. When casting this spell, it summons several Skeletons on the battlefield. These Skeletons are very weak, but can provide a good distraction.
Like Skeletons summoned by Witches , they do not trigger Traps or Clan Castle troops.

In Balloon raids, if your Balloons usually clump up and your Lava Hounds don’t burst, it will take a lot of time to finish off non-defensive buildings. Dropping a Skeleton Spell or two will help you clean up the base. If you decided to leave the defending Archer Queen for something else during your opening phase, a good idea is to wait for the Balloons and Lava Hounds to come around, rage them and drop a Skeleton Spell. The spell will distract and take out the Queen and possible other buildings, and with the added bonus of raging your main army. However, beware of splash surrounding the Queen. If there is a Bomb Tower nearby, consider taking the Queen out during the opening phase.

If you decided to leave the defending Archer Queen for something else during your opening phase, a good idea is to wait for the Balloons and Lava Hounds to come around, rage them and drop a Skeleton Spell. The spell will distract and take out the Queen and possible other buildings, and with the added bonus of raging your main army. However, beware of splash surrounding the Queen. If there is a Bomb Tower nearby, consider taking the Queen out during the opening phase.

In GoHo ( Golem + Hog Rider ) attacks, you may encounter Skeleton Traps which spawn a few Skeletons to follow and damage your Hog Riders. Dropping a single Skeleton Spell will help get rid of the Skeletons chipping away at your Hogs' health. Wait until your Hogs run into a Healing Spell , then drop your Skeleton Spell.

Skeleton Spells could be very effective against single-target Inferno Towers . The Skeletons will be able to distract the Inferno Tower while other troops finish it off. However, multiple-target Inferno Towers will negate this spell very quickly. More generally, the Skeleton Spells are effective against compartments containing only single-target defenses and slow-firing defenses (which includes the Mortar and Scattershot ). They can be used to cover troops as they advance through this compartment; in particular, the Royal Champion on her own can be used in conjunction with Skeleton Spells in this manner to clear such a compartment without taking significant damage.

Bat Spell.name: Bat Spell
notes: The Bat Spell is the 5th Dark Spell unlocked at level 5 Dark Spell Factory that requires the Town Hall to be at level 10. When casting this spell, it summons several Bats on the battlefield over time (its method of spawning is similar to a Skeleton Spell ). These Bats are low on health and target defenses.
Like Skeletons , Bats do not trigger traps or Clan Castle troops .

Bats spawned from the Bat Spell deal less damage to resource storages; in particular, this applies to the Town Hall's Giga Tesla , and Giga Inferno , as it is classified as both a defense and a resource storage.
The Bats also relate to the Builder Base troop also known as the Night Witch . The Night Witch spawns Bats that relate to the Bats in the Bat Spell. However, the Night Witch's Bats attack any target.
Bats can destroy most single-target exposed defenses relatively easily.

Bats can be very effective in distracting single-target Inferno Towers from targeting your tanks ( Golems , Lava Hounds, etc.). But, against defenses which target multiple targets such as multi-target Inferno Towers, the Bats will get killed quickly.

Wizard Towers are excellent in countering Bat-based attacks. Consider their placements carefully when planning such an attack. Either distract them with another troop like a Giant or Ice Golem or use a Freeze Spell to stop them.

It can be viable to use Bat Spells in masses with Lava Hounds. The Lava Hounds will be able to tank well for the Bats (as well as shield them from Inferno Towers) while the Bats do damage. However, if the Lava Hound gets targeted by an Air Bomb, the resulting explosion from the traps will destroy the bats if nearby said troop afterwards.
However, if the Lava Hound gets targeted by an Air Bomb, the resulting explosion from the traps will destroy the bats if nearby said troop afterwards.

If defenses are targeting your tanks, place a few Bat Spells on the defenses to destroy them. However, Make sure that there isn't much defenses that are free, since they should be able to take out the bats easily.

A good strategy for Bat Spells would be to place a lot of them down near the center of the base, along with a Rage Spell and a Freeze Spell, aiming to destroy single-target Inferno Towers, Air Defenses, and the Eagle Artillery at the beginning of an attack. Anything else would be a bonus. Then use the rest of your attack to maul the rest of the base. The Battle Blimp used with the Super Wizards paired with Invisibility Spells (Blizzard) or the Electrone (Balloons and Electro Dragons with Clone and Rage) strategy is still more effective at decimating the core.

With a similar thought process, use something else that does not require more than one or two Rage Spells to take out a portion of the base, along with the Town Hall and Splash defenses to create a clear path and make the job much easier for the Bats to breeze through the rest of the base.

Another strategy is to use a horde of bats to take down a whole area of single-targeting defenses. The Invisibility Spell will be useful for them, as well as the Freeze Spell to freeze splash defenses as necessary.

A hit from a Scattershot can take out a horde of Bats quickly. However, due to the Scattershot's slow attack and the Bats' speed as well as the Scattershot's blind spot, a Scattershot may be swarmed before proving to be useful. Make sure to surround your Scattershot with several defenses in order to stall the Bats. However, if it and other defenses are too close to each other, especially to those which target ground and air units and doing multi-target, fast attacking or splash damage, a Freeze Spell will be able to stop them from attacking altogether, and the Bats may will be able to destroy these defenses before the Freeze Spell expires.

However, if it and other defenses are too close to each other, especially to those which target ground and air units and doing multi-target, fast attacking or splash damage, a Freeze Spell will be able to stop them from attacking altogether, and the Bats may will be able to destroy these defenses before the Freeze Spell expires.

If multi-target Inferno Towers are unavailable (due to being upgraded, for example), rapid-firing defenses such as X-Bows set to ground and air mode can also destroy Bats quickly. Archer Towers set to fast attack can also prove viable, as well as the Multi-Archer Tower .
Air Bombs can be helpful to sweep up Bats that are following closely behind other air troops, but as the Bats cannot trigger the Air Bomb themselves, it may not be a reliable option.

Resource storages, which also includes the Town Hall itself are a good way to soak up damage from the Bats, since they deal 15% of the damage when attacking these types of buildings, either causing the attacker to likely time fail, or to possibly get a 1-star, provided if the Town Hall is not destroyed.

Having a defensive Archer Queen and other Clan Castle troops that can target air can also be useful to defend against Bats. The Bats will not attack these units; however, they may be too fast to tackle. It may also be possible these defensive units target other air troops instead. The defending Electro Titan is able to wipe out Bats instantly due to her passive damaging aura, even if you apply the Invisibility Spell on them. Her aura can neither be stopped by Freeze Spells nor Poison Spells, so the only way to deal with the aura is to lure the Electro Titan away from the area you want to deploy your Bats.

Her aura can neither be stopped by Freeze Spells nor Poison Spells, so the only way to deal with the aura is to lure the Electro Titan away from the area you want to deploy your Bats.

A massive swarm of Bats may be terrifying but can easily be stopped by Wizard Towers , so place them carefully, and multi-target Inferno Towers. The Giga Tesla and Giga Inferno also can mow down Bats quickly. Another thing to note is that while Bats cannot trigger traps by themselves, other nearby air troops such as Balloons and Dragons may trigger Air Bombs and the Tornado Trap . These traps can wipe out hordes of bats very easily if the bats are caught in the blast.

If the Bats are very close to each other, one shot of the Eagle Artillery could take them all out, but this is not a reliable option, because if other troops are on the battlefield, it is unlikely the Eagle Artillery will target Bats due to their low hitpoints.

Invisibility Spell.name: Invisibility Spell
notes: https://clashofclans.fandom.com/wiki/Invisibility_Spell
"Invisibility Spell makes EVERYTHING except for Walls and Siege Machines invisible and untargetable within its radius."

The Invisibility Spell is the seventh Elixir Spell available for Town Hall 11, unlocked by upgrading the Spell Factory to level 6. It allows any offensive or defensive unit (with the exception of Walls and Siege Machines ) in its radius to turn invisible and be unable to be targeted by anything until they step out of the radius or the duration runs out. If the spell hits a building that the Troops were originally targeting, they will leave their previous target and engage to another one that's close to them.
If the spell hits a building that the Troops were originally targeting, they will leave their previous target and engage to another one that's close to them.
Invisible units can still be affected by other spells and can also be hit indirectly through splash-damaging attacks or otherwise.
Damaging projectiles will still hit any troops they targeted if they are sent before the spell has affected the targeted troop.
The Invisibility Spell can be used to buy time for slow troops such as Electro Dragons or Balloons under high DPS areas in order to survive longer.
It can be preferred over the Freeze Spell since instead of stopping one area from attacking any troops , it protects one group of troops from being attacked at all.

This is also useful for funnelling the Royal Champion , as the player can use the Invisibility Spell on the Royal Champion and some other defense such as Mortar , Cannon or Archer Tower and lead her to a more valuable defense, such as Inferno Tower , X-Bow or a Multi-Gear Tower .

The Invisibility Spell synergizes very well with the Electro Dragon. It can protect the Electro Dragon, make it skip less important buildings, and also allow it to chain back to said less important buildings before targeting them again.

Making a defense invisible will not prevent it from firing at any visible targets in its range. However, doing so may still be useful if only to guide defense-targeting troops to attack a more valuable defense.
Once the Eagle Artillery has locked on, it will fire, even if its targets later become invisible. Be sure to place your spell before it locks on or else it will be a waste.
Attacking Troops will always see each other. As such, Healers will heal a troop even after it becomes invisible.

Since Walls are not made invisible, a Jump Spell will be necessary to do this if the Clan Castle is surrounded by Walls, as the Skeleton Spell will not be able to spawn its Skeletons easily inside the Clan Castle compartment without making the Clan Castle invisible as well.
Clone Spells can be added to increase the number of troops spawned, amplifying the damage of the strategy.

Super Archers can be used to a similar effect, since their attacks can pierce through buildings from a very long range. If the player has problems in using Super Archer Blimps, the Throwers can also be used to do a similar thing, except they only deal damage to a target but has much more hitpoints, allowing them to survive Giant Bombs .

If the player has problems in using Super Archer Blimps, the Throwers can also be used to do a similar thing, except they only deal damage to a target but has much more hitpoints, allowing them to survive Giant Bombs .

Sometimes, a player can use an Invisibility Spell paired with about 8 Sneaky Goblins to take out a Town Hall . This works well when trying to snipe a Town Hall, especially at Town Halls 12 and above so its weapon or bomb at the end does not take out any offensive units. Care must be taken not to make the Town Hall invisible, as it will prevent the goblins from targeting it.

Traps are not affected by this spell. An invisible troop walking over a trap will trigger as normal. This also applies to Hidden Teslas . Buildings such as the Giga Tesla , Giga Inferno and Bomb Tower 's death bombs will still do damage to troops after being destroyed.
AOE Defenses can still attack troops that are invisible if they hit a non-invisible troop near the invisible troops.
The defending Electro Titan's aura is still able to damage invisible units.
Try to make it so that certain spots that would be good spots for an Invisibility Spell houses an important Defense , as then the troops will skip over said important defense.

Since Invisibility Spells are commonly used near an important defense surrounded by other defenses or buildings, consider using Skeleton Traps as they will remain invisible while still triggering if the enemy troop steps out of the ring. Near an Air Defense use a Seeking Air Mine since troops that use an Invisibility Spell to skip to the Air Defense will probably be troops like the Electro Dragon or the Dragon .

Recall Spell.name: Recall Spell
notes: " Attack going badly? Need to come in from another direction? The Recall Spell summons back Troops , Heroes and Pets to the deployment bar. You can then send the recalled units back out for a second strike."
Note that the Hero priority does not extend to Pets, which may be separated from the Hero if other high-housing space troops are recalled.

Units that are recalled will retain their current hitpoints and status effects that were afflicted on them when they are recalled, but spell effects will generally wear off since they may be redeployed outside the spell radius, and most status timers will count down while the unit is pending redeployment. The only status timers that are paused while pending redeployment are the clone lifetimes (for clones from the Clone Spell ), the Angry effect from the Angry Spell , active Hero Equipment effect timers (such as Rage Vial and Eternal Tome ), and revival timers (for Heroes being temporarily revived by Phoenix). This is to ensure they cannot be lost between their recalling and redeployment.

The Recall Spell can be used to forcibly call back units from the Town Hall weapon's explosion upon its destruction. This can save lower-health units from being otherwise obliterated, and can prevent significant HP loss on Heroes , and is especially useful against Town Halls 14 and above, since the Giga Inferno Poison Bomb's and the Inferno Artillery 's damage over time effects can prove devastating.

If two Heroes are being used for the same walk, both Heroes and their Pets will be prioritized, preventing any Healers from being recalled if both Heroes have Pets other than the Phoenix. If the Phoenix is assigned to one of them, with the other having a Pet, a level 2 Recall Spell is required to recall any Healers at all, with level 4 allowing the recalling of two Healers.

Having spawn holes (3x3 or larger areas that are completely empty, allowing attacking troops to be spawned) in the middle of a base will enable attackers to deploy troops with some sort of safety net (usually one or more Invisibility Spells to prevent being targeted) before using a Recall Spell to carry them to safety. This can be easily avoided by ensuring that no such holes exist in the base, keeping in mind that Traps and Hidden Teslas do not create their own no-spawn zones.

To prevent a Recall Spell from enabling Hero walks on multiple sides, you can try to defend against the Hero walk itself. For example, ground-mode X-Bows can create long-range pressure which may have to be responded to by a Rage Spell , while single-target Inferno Towers or Monoliths will force attackers to use a Freeze Spell or Invisibility Spell. Clan Castle troop complements built to shut down or stall Hero walks can render the strategy ineffective as well.

Overgrowth Spell.name: Overgrowth Spell
notes: "Ever wish you could ignore a whole chunk of that enemy base ? The Overgrowth Spell traps nearby Buildings in tough roots, stopping Defenses attacking. Troops ignore trapped Buildings."

The Overgrowth Spell is the 6th Dark Spell unlocked at level 6 Dark Spell Factory , which requires Town Hall level 12. It temporarily disables defenses and turns all the buildings invisible and invulnerable within a 13-tile diameter, or a 6-tile radius centered where the spell is placed. If the spell hits a building that the Troops were originally targeting, they will leave their previous target and engage to another one that is close to them. Unlike the Invisibility Spell , it does not make attacking units invisible, thus making them vulnerable to fire.
If the spell hits a building that the Troops were originally targeting, they will leave their previous target and engage to another one that is close to them.
Unlike the Invisibility Spell , it does not make attacking units invisible, thus making them vulnerable to fire.

The spell has no effect on Walls and Traps , which retain their original functionality for the duration of the spell. Defending Troops , Heroes and Builders are also unaffected and can continue to defend normally. If the Clan Castle is affected by the spell, it can still be triggered and summon defensive reinforcements that it houses.

Buildings that are affected by the spell cannot be harmed by any form of damage, including spell damage and indirect damage from units with area-of-effect attacks. Although they cannot be targeted directly, they can still absorb lightning chains from Electro Dragons , Super Wizards and the Electro Owl if a nearby building is struck (they do not take any damage from this). The Wall Wrecker and Log Launcher both continue to attack overgrown buildings if they are in their path, again dealing no damage (in the case of Log Launcher, overgrown buildings also consume the log's pierce). As a result, they will get stuck if they encounter an overgrown building in their path.

The Wall Wrecker and Log Launcher both continue to attack overgrown buildings if they are in their path, again dealing no damage (in the case of Log Launcher, overgrown buildings also consume the log's pierce). As a result, they will get stuck if they encounter an overgrown building in their path.

Consider this spell to be a combination of the Freeze Spell and the Invisibility Spell , but lasts longer and having a much greater range at the cost of 2 spell housing space, while buildings under this effect cannot be damaged in any way, and Siege Machines can indeed get stuck.

Upgrading it only increases the spell duration, and it is not the most significant, so you can save up your Dark Elixir to upgrade other troops and spells instead. This might even be a double-edged sword, as more time also means that if all buildings outside the radius is destroyed, it will likely take a while for the troops to attack said buildings inside, which could make you run out of time.

This might even be a double-edged sword, as more time also means that if all buildings outside the radius is destroyed, it will likely take a while for the troops to attack said buildings inside, which could make you run out of time.

This might even be good to cover major defenses, considering its massive radius, leaving the troops to tackle the most powerful part of the village later, meaning that the troops might have more health and Heroes might still have abilities (and also if the player has spells left to use), increasing the odds of the attack succeeding.

Utilizing this strategy could effectively address significant defenses due to its extensive range, allowing troops to focus on the most powerful section of the village at a later stage. This approach may result in troops retaining more health and Heroes preserving their abilities, provided the player has any remaining spells to use, thereby increasing the likelihood of a successful attack.

It can also be used to put defenses which can be destroyed later or you can use it to prevent troops from attacking the Town Hall early, thus making it not just a versatile spell but one that also is very impactful due to its long range. However, do note that troops will not attack defenses under the effect of the Overgrowth Spell, nor will they retaliate against them. Take note that sometimes that the Town Hall and other defenses are left strangled by the Overgrowth Spell, and when your army is low on health when the spell duration expires, they may not be able to destroy the Town Hall before they do so.

Take note that sometimes that the Town Hall and other defenses are left strangled by the Overgrowth Spell, and when your army is low on health when the spell duration expires, they may not be able to destroy the Town Hall before they do so.

Timing is also vital, since you might have, say an Archer Queen , in the middle of the Overgrowth Spell's radius and the spell wears off, this can allow the Queen to take a lot of damage, so always carry an extra Freeze or Invisibility Spell to avoid this sort of scenario.

It is advisable to avoid carrying an Overgrowth Spell when deploying Electro Dragons or Super Wizards . These units can absorb chain damage without sustaining any harm, which is particularly disadvantageous for Electro Dragons. Their effectiveness relies on their chain attack, which is a primary source of damage. Consequently, utilizing the Overgrowth Spell in this context would waste both the spell capacity and the damage potential of said troops.

Its long range and duration makes it quite hard to defend against, however traps around the area and the Clan Castle's defending troops in areas where the Overgrowth Spell might pull troops into an area used by the Overgrowth Spell and when the spell wears off, it will create a high-DPS area which will cripple the health of units inside its range.

Bag of Frostmites.name: Bag of Frostmites
notes: When cast, the Bag of Frostmites freezes the area of impact, similar to a Freeze Spell . Frostmites then spawn over time within the radius of the spell, which provides distractions and slows down defenses they hit.

The Bag of Frostmites can be used to suppress strong defenses, making them somewhat less threatening. It should be kept in mind that the Bag of Frostmites is not a replacement of the Freeze Spell in the Home Village and will not stop such defenses completely, but can prove to be a viable distraction against high-damage defenses by spawning Frostmites. Thus, it is also useful against single-target Inferno Towers and Monoliths , which means they will be distracted by the Frostmites.
Thus, it is also useful against single-target Inferno Towers and Monoliths , which means they will be distracted by the Frostmites.

Consider how you use this spell as a Skeleton Spell or a Bat Spell: use this to freeze, distract, deal slight damage and slowing them down using this versatile spell. However, the Freeze effect does not last as long as a Freeze Spell, and certainly spawns less distractions than the Skeleton Spell and the Bat Spell .

Do not clump Inferno Towers and other slow-attacking defenses together: This will give a lot of frost-spell value, and the Frostmites will be able to distract them. However, any nearby splash or multi-targeting defenses will destroy the Frostmites, provided that if they do enough damage to prevent them from slowing down defenses.
However, any nearby splash or multi-targeting defenses will destroy the Frostmites, provided that if they do enough damage to prevent them from slowing down defenses.

Revive Spell.name: Revive Spell
notes: "The Healer's own special recipe! The Revive Spell brings a defeated Hero in its range back into the fight with some health. Bring this Spell into battle, and a floating golden heart will appear above any defeated Hero that can be revived. Upgrade the Revive Spell to increase the amount of health Heroes regain."
If there are no eligible Heroes in range if selected, the spell will disappear without taking effect, wasting the spell.
If there are multiple Heroes in range, the effect will only apply to the closest Hero to where the Spell was deployed.

If the Hero is knocked out during a timed ability, such as that provided by the Rage Vial or Invisibility Vial , the ability timer will tick down while the Hero is knocked out. The ability can be resumed if the Hero is revived while the timer is ongoing.

The Barbarian King is also an excellent choice, as he also has a lot of hitpoints. Additionally, if an ability is still active, such as the Giant Gauntlet , Stick Horse , or Rage Vial , the Revive Spell can allow the King to continue wrecking havoc. However, the King cannot jump over Walls, so his usefulness may be situational.
However, the King cannot jump over Walls, so his usefulness may be situational.
The Royal Champion can also be beneficial, as she can jump over Walls whilst the Barbarian King and the Archer Queen cannot.

If the Grand Warden wields the Fireball in a Warden Charge while being grabbed by the Hook Tower, you can let the Warden get knocked out in an area. Afterwards, turn the defeated Hero invisible and revive them before activating their ability and recalling them. Paired with Earthquake Spells , this can prove to be a deadly combo if used correctly.

Ice Block Spell.name: Ice Block Spell
notes: "Cast this cool concoction to encase your ground and air Troops in ice that blocks almost all damage but Freezes their movement and attack!"

The Ice Block Spell appears to be a vial filled with cornflower-colored liquid, surrounded by ice crystals of its respective color. When deployed, it affects all friendly units in its radius to be immobilized and unable to attack, but take significantly reduced damage. This spell does not affect enemy buildings. Only units that are in the area of effect when the spell is deployed will be affected by the spell. Units that move into or are spawned in the radius of the spell will be unaffected. Siege Machines are immune to the spell effect. Units that are underground (e.g. Miners and Super Miners ) are also unaffected but will be affected if they are on the surface when the spell is deployed.
Only units that are in the area of effect when the spell is deployed will be affected by the spell. Units that move into or are spawned in the radius of the spell will be unaffected.

Siege Machines are immune to the spell effect. Units that are underground (e.g. Miners and Super Miners ) are also unaffected but will be affected if they are on the surface when the spell is deployed.

The Ice Block Spell does not stack with other damage reduction effects such as those from the Giant Gauntlet or Eternal Tome . When multiple damage-reducing effects are active on a single unit, the one with the best damage reduction is used. (Eternal Tome's invincibility is treated as having a 100% damage reduction).
Spawned troops, like those from the Golem , Lava Hound , or Yeti will not be frozen when spawned.
Troops spawned from the Bat and Skeleton Spell will be frozen even if they have not spawned yet.
The Furnace will continue to spawn Firemites when frozen.

The Ice Block Spell can be useful when combined with Invisibility Spells and the Fireball . By using Invisibility Spells on nearby defenses on the outside of the base, the fireball can be launched into the center of the base for massive damage. The Ice Block Spell can prevent the Grand Warden from moving when using this strategy, reducing the chance of targeting the wrong defense.

The Ice Block Spell can save your troops from the Town Hall death explosion and reduce the amount of damage taken from the ensuing poison, should you not have the Grand Warden's Eternal Tome available.

This spell has a very good synergy with medium-sized tanks, such as an Ice Golem or a Giant . The effect of the spell would make your Ice Golem/Giant tank for longer, which can make them very effective if you are starting a push, or to tank for funnelling troops, and allowing them to survive for longer. The Freeze effect after the Ice Golem dies can also be used to start your main push after the spell wears out.
The Freeze effect after the Ice Golem dies can also be used to start your main push after the spell wears out.

Inferno Towers and Monoliths are probably your best bet as they are tank shredders and can deal some damage to them. However, this only really works if the troops are already at low health before being put under this spell.

Totem Spell.name: Totem Spell
notes: The Totem Spell summons a Totem with very high hitpoints. When deployed, the totem crashes down onto the deployment location, briefly stunning buildings and troops in a large radius. The stun causes nearby defenders to retarget. The retargeting does not force defenses to target the Totem. Defenses can attack a different target, if that unit is closer to the defense than the Totem is.
The retargeting does not force defenses to target the Totem. Defenses can attack a different target, if that unit is closer to the defense than the Totem is.

The Totem is considered both a ground and air troop for the purposes of being targeted by defenses; it can be hit by both ground-only and air-only defenses (in addition to defenses that can target both). The Totem is not considered an air troop for the purposes of determining if the Baby Dragon or Dragon Duke enrages or not; in other words, these units can trigger their enraged state near a Totem.
The Totem is not considered an air troop for the purposes of determining if the Baby Dragon or Dragon Duke enrages or not; in other words, these units can trigger their enraged state near a Totem.

The Totem is unable to trigger Traps or Clan Castle troops, nor will it trigger Spell Towers . The Totem also is unable to be affected by Clone Spells , Recall Spells , Ice Block Spells , or the auras of Life Gem or Apprentice Wardens . Although the Totem can be healed with a Healing Spell , it will not be targeted by Healers or Druids . The Totem can still be affected by Traps if other troops trigger them. However, the Totem is immune to displacement effects (e.g. from the Tornado Trap ).
The Totem can still be affected by Traps if other troops trigger them. However, the Totem is immune to displacement effects (e.g. from the Tornado Trap ).

The Totem is considered to take up 20 housing space. This is used when interacting with the Dark Crown , and is sufficient to withstand being ejected immediately by a Spring Trap (note that it can only be affected as such if other troops trigger the Trap). However, for the purposes of Eagle Artillery activation, the Totem Spell only counts as 5 housing space, the same as any 1-housing space spell.

Totem Spells are useful for distracting defending units to the summoned Totem, preventing important units like the Grand Warden in a Warden Charge or a Flame Flinger creating a funnel for the main army from being defeated prematurely. As one of the most used spells in most strategies at higher Town Hall levels and only requiring 1 spell housing space, they allow the attacking army to deal with the defending force and obliterate the base, provided that the attack is executed successfully.

However, since it stuns, it does not always redirect to the Totem, and will instead target the nearest unit if the defense's target is closer than the Totem, and can become worse if the defense deals splash damage, like Mortars and Scattershots , since small troops would get wiped out easily, and multi-targeting defenses like Multi-Archer Towers and multi-targeting Inferno Towers can still fire over troops.
On the other hand, Freeze Spells work better as it stops defending targets within its range, including Heroes, troops and buildings alike.

Totems have very high hitpoints, and are very useful for taking heavy fire in just one housing space, acting as both ground and air units that allows all defenses (including those that target air) to attack them. However, Totems are prone to single-target damage, so defenses like single-target Inferno Towers, Monoliths and fully powered Revenge Towers can easily take them out. In addition, they also have a limited time, which can be shortened if they take any form of damage, and will be destroyed if their hitpoints are depleted, and cannot trigger traps (including the Giga Bomb ).

In addition, they also have a limited time, which can be shortened if they take any form of damage, and will be destroyed if their hitpoints are depleted, and cannot trigger traps (including the Giga Bomb ).

The Eternal Tome cannot make the Totem immune to damage for the entire duration, because it is considered to be a stationary troop that acts like a building, unlike immovable Siege Machines and Furnaces .

When any units equal to or less than 18 housing space trigger the Spring Trap while the Totem is active, the Totem takes the damage instead of the troop, otherwise it would target them instead. This can be useful for Headhunters who are traveling to a defending Hero, allowing them to survive and eventually take them out.

Totems can lure ground troops to the Totem, especially in air attacks where the defending troops (like the Ice Golem or Skeletons that spawn from Witches) which could otherwise potentially make the difference between a 99% two-star time fail and a triple.
Totem Spells are particularly annoying for defending, especially due to its ability to stun everything in a large area.

However, since the Totem is spawned behind where the attacking force is, defending units and buildings must try their best to destroy the Totems as fast as possible, otherwise they may be destroyed easily, depending on the attacker's strategy.

Similarly, defending Heroes like the Archer Queen can take down Totems in several seconds due to her massive damage output, although the main attacking force can have problems, especially if they are entering the base.
Since Totems cannot trigger Traps, it is useful to place Traps to protect main defenses as they will deal with the attacking force, and separate major defenses from each other.

Angry Spell.name: Angry Spell
notes: When deployed, the Angry Spell will make any units that are in its radius temporarily target the defenses, although those that specifically target defenses do not have an effect on them, like the Royal Champion , lasting for a limited amount of time before they return to normal.

When a unit is within the Angry Spell's range, it makes it target defenses for a while, before returning back to normal. Units that target defenses like Balloons , Giants , Golems , Hog Riders , Root Riders , Dragon Riders , Ice Golems , Bears , and the Royal Champion are not affected and will function as normal. Units that target specific defenses ( Lava Hound and Ice Hound ) will target any defense instead of their specific defense. Additionally, the Angry Spell has no effect on Healers , Druids , and Ruin Witch who cannot deal damage.

Units that target defenses like Balloons , Giants , Golems , Hog Riders , Root Riders , Dragon Riders , Ice Golems , Bears , and the Royal Champion are not affected and will function as normal. Units that target specific defenses ( Lava Hound and Ice Hound ) will target any defense instead of their specific defense.
Additionally, the Angry Spell has no effect on Healers , Druids , and Ruin Witch who cannot deal damage.
After the spell effect ends, the affected troops return back to their normal targeting priority.
The Angry Spell will continue to take effect for the entire duration, and if any units are deployed within this time span, they will still be affected and thus, will target defenses.

The Angry Spell is a unique spell, capable of turning regular units that target anything into defense-targeting ones. For example, Dragons would struggle against a defense that is too far away, or in the case of the Grand Warden , it allows him to target the nearest defense in a Fireball attack, which is useful for those that are lower than Th16 as a substitute for the Angry Jelly itself.
Healers, Druids, and defense-targeting units as mentioned above are not affected, so using the Angry Jelly on them will not be effective.

The Angry Spell is a very tricky spell to defend against, as it allows the units to take on major defenses with the use of Hero abilities. Try designing a ring base with the Town Hall and major defenses at the center, while the rest would be on the outer rings. This is most effective in Invisibility Spell Tower bases, where it can annoy the attacker.

Barbarian King.name: Barbarian King
notes: The Barbarian King has very high health and a high damage output so he is best used as a tank and a brute force. Deploy him first to distract the defenses then deploy lower health units (like the Archer Queen ) to do the damage behind walls. However, at lower levels, like Town Halls 4 to 9, it is most likely that players might want him inside the base since Heroes are good damage dealers. Another way to use him is for funneling, as is very clear where to funnel, which can be easier depending on his Equipment.

When unlocked, he starts with the Barbarian Puppet and Rage Vial. The Barbarian Puppet allows the Barbarian King to summon a large number of raged Barbarians and an increased health recovery. The level of the Barbarians matches the level researched by the player, while the rage increases their damage and movement speed. It gives a passive increase to max health. The Rage Vial enrages the Barbarian King with his ability, increasing his damage and movement speed, and grants a vastly increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage.

The Barbarian Puppet allows the Barbarian King to summon a large number of raged Barbarians and an increased health recovery. The level of the Barbarians matches the level researched by the player, while the rage increases their damage and movement speed. It gives a passive increase to max health.
The Rage Vial enrages the Barbarian King with his ability, increasing his damage and movement speed, and grants a vastly increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage.

When the Blacksmith is constructed and is upgraded to level 3, it unlocks the Earthquake Boots and Vampstache respectively. The Earthquake Boots deals damage similar to an Earthquake Spell , except that it destroys walls instantly and damages all ground units in its radius. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health. The Vampstache passively restores a small fraction of the King's health every time he lands an attack. It gives a passive increase to damage and attack speed.

The Earthquake Boots deals damage similar to an Earthquake Spell , except that it destroys walls instantly and damages all ground units in its radius. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.
The Vampstache passively restores a small fraction of the King's health every time he lands an attack. It gives a passive increase to damage and attack speed.

The Giant Gauntlet makes the King grow gigantic, allowing him to deal splash damage, hit buildings behind Walls , and reduces damage taken for a period of time. It gives a passive increase to damage and grants self healing.
The Spiky Ball makes the King kick a ricocheting ball which bounces to a number of buildings, dealing massive damage. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.
The Snake Bracelet passively generates Snakes whenever the King takes damage up to a limit, which can jump over Walls. It gives a passive increase to max health and attack speed.
The Stick Horse allows the King the jump over Walls, and attack and move faster for a while when deployed. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.

At Town Halls 4 through 6, the Barbarian King is available at a limited capacity. He cannot be upgraded, his equipment cannot be configured, and he cannot defend the village as there is no Hero Banner to place. However, his key stats (damage per second, hitpoints and health recovery), and that of his default equipment, will scale by Town Hall level based on the level 1 stats. Town Hall 4 has 50% of the stats, Town Hall 5 has 75%, and Town Hall 6 has the full stats. The ability attributes (speed increases, damage increases, etc.) of his default equipment are unaffected by this scaling, only its passive stats.

The Barbarian King can often be used to create funnels; if there are no gaps in nearby Walls , he will stay outside the Walls and clear out buildings placed outside. As he is able to tank a lot of damage, he can be used to clear areas covered by high-DPS defenses, like a Hidden Tesla , Scattershot , Firespitter , or an X-Bow farm (where multiple of the same defense type is grouped to provide concentrated damage). However, air troops may be better suited for the funnel if anti-air DPS is lacking in such areas, and one should still be wary of single-target Inferno Towers and Monoliths , which can quickly defeat him and end the funnel. This can also be commonly referred to as a King Walk.

He is best used with support from ranged troops, such as the Archer , Wizard , Witch , and the Headhunter to kill air troops and to deal damage behind. However, make sure that the ranged troops are protected from strong splash defenses such as the Scattershot , Mortar , and the Eagle Artillery , otherwise they will be taken out quickly.
However, make sure that the ranged troops are protected from strong splash defenses such as the Scattershot , Mortar , and the Eagle Artillery , otherwise they will be taken out quickly.

He is also good for helping to destroy the remaining buildings of a village, after most or all defenses have been destroyed. However, he has a slow movement speed, so you might have to speed him up if you want an effective cleanup procedure, either with his ability or other spells.
However, he has a slow movement speed, so you might have to speed him up if you want an effective cleanup procedure, either with his ability or other spells.

The Barbarian King can be easily swarmed by a group of Archers or Barbarians , as he only attacks one target at a time and has a somewhat slow attack speed against swarms. However, the Giant Gauntlet ability can negate this, since it allows the King to do splash damage and take less damage by himself.
However, the Giant Gauntlet ability can negate this, since it allows the King to do splash damage and take less damage by himself.

As his ability recovers some health, you should let your Barbarian King take some damage before activating this ability to maximize the recovered health provided by activating the ability. The exception is at the end of a successful battle where the Barbarian King survives with taking very little or no damage, because if the ability is not activated after battle he will automatically activate it, recovering his health. Depending on Hero Equipment, his ability can be used to speed up the process of clearing the base, when paired with other Hero Equipment.

The Barbarian King can be healed by Healing Spells , Healers , Druids , the Unicorn , and the Healing Tome of the Grand Warden . However, since he is a Hero, he receives a different healing rate from some of these sources of healing compared to troops: Healing Spells only heal 55% as much as with troops. Healers at lower levels only heal about 55% compared to troops, but this percentage increases at mid-levels, eventually surpassing troop healing at level 11. Druids heal more effectively (between 5% and 15%) compared to troops, depending on the level. The Unicorn and Healing Tome do not have different healing rates on Heroes when compared to troops.
