Avoid using the ability when the King approaches a Bomb Tower or an area where a Giant Bomb or Giga Bomb will be, unless when desperately needing to recover health. If done, the summoned Barbarians will most likely be wiped out by the resulting explosion. However, this becomes much less of an issue with the higher level Barbarian King because when the Bomb explodes, it is likely not all of the Barbarians have spawned in yet so only a few of them blow up. This is only a problem only if using either the Barbarian Puppet or if the King is too close to damage dealers, since the Giant Bomb can cripple, or possibly even wipe out the player's whole line of damage-dealing units.

When you are facing a single-target Inferno Tower , activate the Barbarian King's ability before he is locked on to the Inferno Tower, when using the Barbarian Puppet. This way the spawned Barbarians can distract the Inferno Tower and keep the King alive for longer. When not using this equipment, the Earthquake Boots allow the King to access the Inferno Tower, or the Giant Gauntlet can allow him to reduce its damage, and to help destroy it quickly with the help of the other Equipment slot.

Enable "Automatically use Hero Abilities on KO" in the settings, as there is no real downside to doing so; his Hero ability enhances his sustainability and boosts his damage output, and it might also reduces the time of healing for the hero to be used again, which is noticeable in higher Town Halls.

When using Barbarian Puppet, since that ability will summon Barbarians which is the current level inside the Laboratory , it is highly recommended to do so when using this ability often, as they will become stronger and destroy buildings faster, as well as being a greater distraction. However, this equipment is quite weak, so it is not recommended, due to traps that will destroy the spawned Barbarians.
However, this equipment is quite weak, so it is not recommended, due to traps that will destroy the spawned Barbarians.

The Mighty Yak specializes in wall-breaking, which is useful to the Barbarian King as he is the only Hero unable to attack over Walls; the Yak can break open walls enabling the King access to buildings inside, and also being a mini-tank for the King.

The Phoenix guarantees his survival in battle for a duration, which can be especially useful since the Barbarian King can potentially be defeated mid-ability. Although defenses generally retarget between the King's first defeat and his revival, he is still able to do considerable damage and tank any defenses that happens to target him, allowing the other units to destroy the defenses before they lock onto them.

The Barbarian King generally benefits more from having better levels itself than better equipment levels, so leveling up the Barbarian King should be a priority at all times for a good offensive attack. However, higher level equipment is still necessary for an effective attack.

The Giant Gauntlet and Rage Vial, which allows the King to do massive amounts of damage, take less damage, wreck compartments and to improve his tanking potential. The Spiky Ball is usually an upgrade to Rage Vial in most situations. Spiky Ball give a huge increase in maximum health and damage passively while also crippling nearby defenses and buildings on its way, if not destroy them.

The Spiky Ball is usually an upgrade to Rage Vial in most situations. Spiky Ball give a huge increase in maximum health and damage passively while also crippling nearby defenses and buildings on its way, if not destroy them.
The Rage Vial can also find good synergy with Vampstache, allowing the King to recover health faster and deal more damage at the same time.

The Vampstache paired with Snake Bracelet can improve the sustainability of the King extremely well with massive amount of extra max health, Snakes causing distraction, and both equipment giving passive attack speed increase.
Though he is very strong on offense, he only attacks one target at a time on defense which makes him easy to defeat with multiple units, so protect him with splash-damaging defenses.

The Barbarian King is the only Hero that cannot target aerial units. Despite this, he can still stall air units that do not have a preferred target such as Dragons , because such air units will target him even though he poses no threat to them.

Unlike troops in the Clan Castle , the Barbarian King cannot be lured to the edge of the map and then defeated out of range of the defenses (unless his altar is near the edge). If his target moves out of his patrol area, he will retreat and engage another enemy inside his patrol area. If no enemies remain in his patrol area, he will resume patrolling.

Archer Queen.name: Archer Queen
notes: The Archer Queen is the second Hero unlocked at Hero Hall Level 2, which requires Town Hall Level 8. She is essentially a bigger and much more powerful version of the Archer . In addition to possessing much higher damage and hitpoints, the Archer Queen also shoots 1.5 tiles farther than a normal Archer (5 tiles instead of 3.5 tiles).
The Archer Queen shoots three rapid arrows per shot. However, that is more of a visual feature, because these arrows deal damage to a single target.

When unlocked, she starts with the Archer Puppet and Invisibility Vial. The Archer Puppet allows the Archer Queen to summon a large number of invisible Archers and an increase health recovery. The level of the Archers matches the level researched by the player. It gives a passive increase to damage. The Invisibility Vial turns the Archer Queen invisible and gives her significantly increased damage for the duration. It gives a passive increase to maximum health.

The Archer Puppet allows the Archer Queen to summon a large number of invisible Archers and an increase health recovery. The level of the Archers matches the level researched by the player. It gives a passive increase to damage.
The Invisibility Vial turns the Archer Queen invisible and gives her significantly increased damage for the duration. It gives a passive increase to maximum health.

Upgrading the Blacksmith to level 2 and 5 unlocks the Giant Arrow and Healer Puppet respectively. The Giant Arrow launches a large arrow that travels the whole village, dealing damage on the way. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health. The Healer Puppet summons Healers, with the number of Healers is dependent on the level of this Equipment. It gives a passive increase to her maximum health and grants her self healing.
The Giant Arrow launches a large arrow that travels the whole village, dealing damage on the way. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.
The Healer Puppet summons Healers, with the number of Healers is dependent on the level of this Equipment. It gives a passive increase to her maximum health and grants her self healing.
The Frozen Arrow passively makes her attacks slow down defenses, defending Heroes and troops. It gives a passive increase to damage.
The Magic Mirror summons clone(s) of herself, provides a brief invisibility, and grants an increased health recovery with her ability. It gives a passive increase to max health.
The Action Figure summons a Giant Giant to fight by the Archer Queen's side. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health and grants her self healing.

The Monolith Arrow passively makes her attacks deal bonus damage based off the target's maximum health. This bonus damage decreases the more troops are deployed. it also gives a passive hitpoint increase and grants damage reduction.

She has a better range than an Archer (5 tiles instead of 3.5), so a good strategy is to place a group of Giants , P.E.K.K.As , Golems , or the Barbarian King as a meat shield, then a group of Archers, and finally the Archer Queen. This minimizes the chance of her being defeated or even hit and may allow you to use her many times in a row without waiting for her to regenerate.

A related version of the Queen Walk is the Queen Charge, where instead of being used for funneling, the Queen and Healers target the core of the base, destroying key defenses. This usually involves the use of Wall Breakers , their super form , or Jump Spells in addition to other funneling troops (such as Baby Dragons ) to ensure she enters the base, and then using her abilities to wipe defenses.

An alternate version of the Queen Walk that can be utilized is with Druids instead of Healers. Unlike Healers, Druids do not have a reduced healing rate when healing Heroes, making them slightly more effective. In addition, their healing bounces from one troop or Hero to another, thereby giving you the ability to add supporting troops in a Queen Walk. The downside to using Druids instead of Healers is that they will only remain in their base form for 30 seconds before transforming into their Bear form. Once they have turned into a Bear, they can no longer heal the Queen and/or troops and instead target defenses, which can sometimes be useful to tank the Queen from incoming defenses.

Seeking Air Mines can also counter this. Periodically place some Balloons near the Healers to try and soak them up. These Balloons are often called "coco loons". Try to bring about 3 or 4. Any extra ones may also be used like normal Balloons. However, the Seeking Air Mine strategy does not work on Druids, since they are ground units and will not trigger these aerial traps in any way, at the cost of being vulnerable to defenses and traps that target ground units.

However, the Seeking Air Mine strategy does not work on Druids, since they are ground units and will not trigger these aerial traps in any way, at the cost of being vulnerable to defenses and traps that target ground units.

The Unicorn can be used in place of a Healer or Druid. However, in a lot of strategies, you see them both used at the same time for maximum healing to the Archer Queen, which increases her sustainability.

The activated Invisibility Vial's ability is excellent against single-target Inferno Towers. When used, the Inferno Tower's damage will not only reset, but is often redirected onto a summoned Archer if the Archer Puppet is equipped. The Queen can quickly finish off the Inferno with her damage under the cloak, while the Archers can provide great cover and overwhelm the Inferno if it is not defended well by splash defenses (or other multi-targeting Infernos). Without the Archer Puppet, her sustainability will increased significantly, especially if the Invisibility Vial is paired with either the Giant Arrow or Frozen Arrow.

The Invisibility Vial ability will also not prevent any projectiles (such as Cannon shots) that are targeting the Archer Queen at the time of the ability's activation from hitting her. If the Eagle Artillery has already locked on and fired on the Queen, activating the Invisibility Vial will not prevent the shots from hitting, which will result in great damage against your Queen. Activating the ability just before it fires will stop the Eagle Artillery from firing on your Archer Queen, however, and render the Queen temporarily untargetable by the Eagle Artillery as normal.

Sending the Archer Queen and any other heroes like this with little support (up to about 25 housing space of troops) is known as a Sui Queen. This is best used to destroy outer portions of the base and a few key targets farther in.

Beware of the Barbarian King, as he can knock out the Archer Queen in a 1v1 if they are at the same level or if the Archer Queen is only 5 levels or lower than the King. If you are going to 1v1 the Barbarian King, place Healers/Druids to support the Queen or place Wizards or any other high-damaging troop to quickly defeat the King. Headhunters, if you have access, is also good when going against the King.

The Invisibility Vial ability's mechanism will cause her to be considered as a new target different from the original Archer Queen. Against a defending Electro Dragon , this ability may backfire, as it may cause her to take two hits from the Electro Dragon's Chain Lightning ability.

If you do not need to use her ability during battle, you do not always need to. If the battle ends and she does not use her ability, after battle she will recover health equal to the ability recovery.

The Phoenix can also revive the Archer Queen if she happens to be defeated while under her ability. The subsequent revival allows the Queen to use most of, if not the full duration of her extremely damaging ability if the Invisibility Vial is active.

Other good combos include the Frozen Arrow and Healer Puppet, which allows her more healers for extra health recovery, and also self-heals over time. The Invisibility Vial and Healer Puppet for guaranteed healing, and the Giant Arrow and Invisibility Vial or the Magic Mirror for ZapQuake attacks are all good combinations to a certain extent.

The Magic Mirror is usually an upgrade to the Invisibility Vial in most situations. The Magic Mirror summons clones and turns the Queen invisible briefly so defenses will target them instead, they do more extra damage overall and have some tanking capability, it also provides more maximum health passively and have extra health recovery to make up for not being invisible for longer. Pairing this with the Action Figure allows the Giant Giant to tank for all the cloned Queens, allowing the Queens to deal significant amounts of damage when both abilities are activated.
The Healer Puppet and Giant Arrow/Frozen Arrow/Archer Puppet, as both abilities can be used immediately with little to no conflicts, unlike Invisibility Vial or Magic Mirror.

The Healer Puppet and Invisibility Vial/Magic Mirror are still a valid pairing, as the passive healing already helps the Queen's sustainability in the core, having invisibility time and retargeting available with extra Healers being spawned can be an insurance.

The Archer Queen is more suitable for defense than the Barbarian King because of her higher damage per second, and she is able to attack from a longer range (as well as being able to strike air units ), but she has dramatically lower health than the Barbarian King. The Hero Banner must be placed 3-4 spaces from the nearest wall to prevent the Queen from jumping out and getting targeted by melee troops.
Protect your key defenses by keeping them more than 5 tiles away from the nearest open space, so the Queen cannot snipe them.

Tanking troops can be of some use, but they will not last long against an Archer Queen. For example, a maxed Golem will last only 10-11 seconds against a max-level Archer Queen, not accounting for any other defenses that may be targeting it. If you are using a similar level, using the Barbarian King as a tank and the enemy Archer Queen is not hiding behind a wall, then the Barbarian King himself will be sufficient to defeat the Queen unless nearby defenses or the defending Clan Castle troops or Barbarian King are also attacking him. Activating the King's ability will allow him to defeat the Queen quicker.

If you are using a similar level, using the Barbarian King as a tank and the enemy Archer Queen is not hiding behind a wall, then the Barbarian King himself will be sufficient to defeat the Queen unless nearby defenses or the defending Clan Castle troops or Barbarian King are also attacking him. Activating the King's ability will allow him to defeat the Queen quicker.

Consider bringing a spell or spells to make the takedown process easier, such as a Poison Spell to slow the Queen's attacks, a Skeleton Spell to distract her, or a Freeze Spell to keep her from killing your troops too quickly.

The Grand Warden 's Eternal Tome ability can keep troops alive while they destroy an Archer Queen. Because the Queen's health is so low, the short duration of the Eternal Tome ability is rarely a problem.

Like with the Barbarian King or the Royal Champion, Headhunters are effective at targeting and attacking the Archer Queen, and they are used in small numbers in most high-level strategies such as LavaLoon where the other troops cannot target or damage her effectively. However, if Headhunters are sent in alone without assistance or not being protected by the Grand Warden's Eternal Tome ability, they will likely be picked off and taken out easily by the Queen or nearby defenses. As such, they are best sneaked in, covered by other attacking troops or by the Grand Warden's Eternal Tome ability.

Grand Warden.name: Grand Warden
notes: The Grand Warden is the fourth Hero unlocked at Hero Hall level 5, which requires Town Hall 11. He is a single-target unit with low health and relatively low damage, but he makes up for it with his long range and supporting abilities.

He can be set to Air or Ground mode; he flies in Air Mode and walks in Ground Mode. He can bypass Walls regardless of the mode he is set to; however, he will attack a Wall if the majority of your nearby housing space is doing so as well.
He can bypass Walls regardless of the mode he is set to; however, he will attack a Wall if the majority of your nearby housing space is doing so as well.

When unlocked, he starts with the Eternal Tome and Life Gem. The Eternal Tome lets the Grand Warden make himself and all attacking units in his radius invincible for several seconds. It does not have any passive stat increase. The Life Gem passively increases the health and max health of other attacking units within his radius by a percentage of their max health up to a cap. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.
The Eternal Tome lets the Grand Warden make himself and all attacking units in his radius invincible for several seconds. It does not have any passive stat increase.

The Life Gem passively increases the health and max health of other attacking units within his radius by a percentage of their max health up to a cap. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.

Upgrading the Blacksmith to level 4 and 6 unlocks the Rage Gem and Healing Tome respectively. The Rage Gem passively increases the damage or healing of other attacking units within his radius by a percentage. It gives a passive increase to damage and attack speed. The Healing Tome lets the Grand Warden heal himself and all units within his radius over time. It gives a passive increase to max health.
The Rage Gem passively increases the damage or healing of other attacking units within his radius by a percentage. It gives a passive increase to damage and attack speed.
The Healing Tome lets the Grand Warden heal himself and all units within his radius over time. It gives a passive increase to max health.

Additionally, there are Epic rarity Hero Equipment which can be purchased with event medals during certain events or gems with the Trader . The Fireball has the Grand Warden throw a fireball at the nearest defense, dealing massive damage within a large radius. It gives a passive increase to his damage. The Lavaloon Puppet summons one to two Lavaloons. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health. The Heroic Torch lets the Grand Warden give all units within his radius damage resistance, increased movement speed, and the ability to walk through walls. It gives a passive increase to his damage, max health, and health recovery.
The Fireball has the Grand Warden throw a fireball at the nearest defense, dealing massive damage within a large radius. It gives a passive increase to his damage.
The Lavaloon Puppet summons one to two Lavaloons. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.

The Heroic Torch lets the Grand Warden give all units within his radius damage resistance, increased movement speed, and the ability to walk through walls. It gives a passive increase to his damage, max health, and health recovery.

The Grand Warden has two AI modes during an attack based on a hidden attribute called Warden Weight. If the total Warden Weight is under 20, he remains in regular target mode, where he targets the nearest building to him, ignoring nearby friendly troops. If the total Warden Weight reaches 20 or higher, he instantly switches to group target mode, where the Grand Warden locks onto whichever building is being targeted by the majority or heaviest concentration of nearby troops.
If the total Warden Weight is under 20, he remains in regular target mode, where he targets the nearest building to him, ignoring nearby friendly troops.

If the total Warden Weight reaches 20 or higher, he instantly switches to group target mode, where the Grand Warden locks onto whichever building is being targeted by the majority or heaviest concentration of nearby troops.
The Grand Warden constantly scans a vision radius 13 tiles around himself and calculates the total Warden Weight of all valid friendly troops inside his area.

During battle, when a main group destroys a building, those troops briefly enter a millisecond retargeting delay where they hold no active target. If the Grand Warden evaluates during this exact delay, he may temporarily lock onto a single unit that still has an active target.

Because of the Grand Warden's low health and low damage, he is more suited to support than leading an attack. Have tank units such as Giants , Golems or the Barbarian King to keep him safe from defenses. The Grand Warden can help them in return with his passive abilities.

If using the Air Mode Warden alone (as a niche to evade heavy ground defenses, for example), it is recommended to deploy Balloons near the Warden to distract any Seeking Air Mines and make sure that none of the traps will hit the Warden. Relative level Seeking Air Mines will kill the Grand Warden, unless he is at least level 37 for Town Hall 12 when the Seeking Air Mine is at level 3, or level 49 for Town Hall 13 when the trap is level 4. However, be careful of level 5 or above Seeking Air Mines, as they will defeat him instantly at any level. However, a level 7 Seeking Air Mine leaves the level 48 Grand Warden with the maxed out Life Gem and Healing Tome with only 10 hitpoints remaining.
However, a level 7 Seeking Air Mine leaves the level 48 Grand Warden with the maxed out Life Gem and Healing Tome with only 10 hitpoints remaining.

Use the Eternal Tome ability near the core so your troops can get through the core, where the most damage usually is. Against a level 5 Giga Tesla , Giga Inferno , or the Giga Bomb at Town Hall 17, it may be useful to save the ability specifically for the explosion when the Town Hall is destroyed or when the trap is triggered, as these do severe damage to your army. Alternatively, it can be better to use it early, such as if high damaging defenses are situated nearer the outside of a base, or when your main army is able to split up.

He will follow the troop with the highest housing space or the largest mass of troops, so bunching up troops with the Grand Warden is crucial to getting the most out of his abilities. However, do not bunch them up too tightly, as his aura is large and the troops will take a lot of splash damage from other defenses if they are too bunched up. This also risks them being targeted by the Eagle Artillery . However, this is temporarily nullified with the Eternal Tome ability.

However, do not bunch them up too tightly, as his aura is large and the troops will take a lot of splash damage from other defenses if they are too bunched up. This also risks them being targeted by the Eagle Artillery . However, this is temporarily nullified with the Eternal Tome ability.
This also risks them being targeted by the Eagle Artillery .

When using high-hitpoint troops, it is best to use the Apprentice Warden instead of the Life Gem, since the Apprentice Warden does not have any health limit cap, which can increase bigger troops' health significantly, and the Life Gem will be replaced by either the Rage Gem, Healing Tome or Fireball to help support the attack.

The Grand Warden has the longest range of any troop in the Home Village or all Heroes in the game. He can outrange the Wizard Tower , Bomb Tower , Archer Tower on Fast Attack mode, or the Hidden Tesla . The Super Archer has a projectile range of 12, but her targeting range is only 6. The Mortar Mode Cannon Cart in the Builder's Base has the longest range of any troop in the Builder Base, being 9 tiles. The Flame Flinger has the longest range out of all units in the game, being 10 tiles.
The Super Archer has a projectile range of 12, but her targeting range is only 6.
The Mortar Mode Cannon Cart in the Builder's Base has the longest range of any troop in the Builder Base, being 9 tiles.
The Flame Flinger has the longest range out of all units in the game, being 10 tiles.

If the Grand Warden is positioned correctly, he can defeat an enemy Barbarian King and even an Archer Queen without being attacked. In the case of an Archer Queen, it is substantially harder to pull off, as she has a larger attack radius, has a faster movement and attack speed, and can attack from far away unlike the King.
Druids, unlike Healers, are better to use than Healers due to being a ground unit, and you can bring at least 2 to support him. However, they last for a limited time.
If the Grand Warden has the Rage Gem, he will be able to destroy buildings faster, making Warden Walks faster. This also allows the Healers and/or Druids heal more often.

His AI (which makes him follow troops if they are close enough) can be exploited to help funnel him in a particular direction, which can be useful for the objectives of the Warden Walk. For example, deploying a few Balloons against a defense can coerce him to follow the Balloons in attacking that defense. You can also do this to convert a Warden Walk into a smash-style attack (which will be supported by the Warden and Healers) by simply deploying your main force in the path of the walk.

When set to Air Mode, if you see a Seeking Air Mine coming towards the Grand Warden, activate his Eternal Tome ability if you still have it. If you react quickly enough, he will be able to avoid all damage; failing to do so will mean severe damage, and in most cases automatically trigger the ability anyway (if the "Automatically use Hero Abilities on KO" setting is turned on), but the Warden will be reduced to 1 HP and be extremely vulnerable, leaving you at a disadvantage, especially if he does not have the Eternal Tome equipped.

The Electro Owl is an excellent fit for Grand Warden, especially if using Air Mode. Not only does the Owl provide additional damage that nearly matches his own, the Owl is the only aerial Pet that can accompany the Warden without him being knocked out, thus behaving like an extra troop to protect him. In ground mode, the Owl's additional damage can greatly speed up Warden Walks, and unlike grounded Pets, does not risk pulling the Healers away from the Warden, and can tank for Seeking Air Mines.
The Poison Lizard is an alternative for damage at Town Hall 15, with its DPS being focused on a single target, as opposed to the Owl; it can also assist the Warden against enemy troops.

For additional support utility, Frosty can be paired with the Warden to slow defenses down. The Warden often being in the backline combines with Frosty's targeting AI to keep Frosty himself in the backlines, which enhances his sustainability as compared to pairing him with other Heroes.

The Unicorn can heal the Warden effectively, including during a Warden Walk, due to it being able to keep pace with the Warden easily. Although most often paired with the Archer Queen, the Unicorn's pairing with the Warden can be considered if the Queen should be unavailable or require a different Pet.

Pets like Diggy or Frosty can be used to stun or slow down defenses when the army targets them, increasing the chances of a successful attack, but only if the main army he follows targets the defenses, especially Root Riders .

Royal Champion.name: Royal Champion
notes: "Over the Wall and at them! The Royal Champion is only afraid of four things, and the enemy isn't one of them. Her short range is perfect for stabbing defenses up close and personal."

The Royal Champion is the fifth Hero unlocked once the Hero Hall reaches Level 7, which is available at Town Hall level 13. She has moderately high damage per second, moderate health, and targets defenses . She can also jump over Walls , much like the Hog Rider and Headhunter .

The Royal Champion has moderately high health, but high damage so she is best used as a ranged damage dealer just like the Archer Queen . Most likely, you want to protect your Royal Champion so that she can destroy defenses.

When unlocked, she starts with the Royal Gem and Seeking Shield. The Royal Gem grants the ability a vastly increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health. The Seeking Shield allows her to throw a shield with her ability. It seeks out up to four targets - prioritizing defenses - regardless of distance, dealing a large amount of damage to each. It gives a passive increase to max health.
The Royal Gem grants the ability a vastly increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.

The Seeking Shield allows her to throw a shield with her ability. It seeks out up to four targets - prioritizing defenses - regardless of distance, dealing a large amount of damage to each. It gives a passive increase to max health.

Upgrading the Blacksmith to level 7 and 8 unlocks the Hog Rider Puppet and Haste Vial respectively. The Hog Rider Puppet summons Hog Riders, provides a brief invisibility, and grants an increased health recovery with her ability. It gives a passive increase to max health. The Haste Vial greatly increases her movement speed and attack speed for a short duration with her ability. It gives a passive increase to damage and attack speed.
The Hog Rider Puppet summons Hog Riders, provides a brief invisibility, and grants an increased health recovery with her ability. It gives a passive increase to max health.
The Rocket Spear massively increases her attack range and damage and grants a small splash radius for a few attacks with her ability. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.

The Electro Boots passively create an electric aura similar to that of the Electro Titan's , dealing damage to nearby enemy units and buildings. It gives a passive increase to max health and grant her self healing.
The Frost Flake shoots multiple snow flakes at the closest defense, freezes them for a short while, and deals a small amount of damage. It gives a passive increase to max health.

Similar to the Archer Queen Walk, the Royal Champion can be assisted by multiple Healers in a Royal Champion Walk. However, due to the shorter range of the Royal Champion, the Healers can easily get in range of Air Defenses . As with the Archer Queen, this is useful for taking out outer buildings before the main attack. A variation of this uses Druids instead of Healers, since the former are ground units, but they only heal her for a limited time. Another version of the Royal Champion Walk is to use Invisibility Spells instead of Healers to destroy important defenses, known as the Royal Champion Charge.
A variation of this uses Druids instead of Healers, since the former are ground units, but they only heal her for a limited time.
Another version of the Royal Champion Walk is to use Invisibility Spells instead of Healers to destroy important defenses, known as the Royal Champion Charge.

Send her in with the main pack of a Hybrid ( Hog Riders and Miners ) as they will tank for her and she will deal massive damage to the defenses. She also can attack defending Heroes that are attacking the pack, and then will also follow the pack due to also targeting defenses. She will also protect the pack from defending aerial Clan Castle troops.

Often it is better to send her later in the attack, where the main army is starting to lose power getting to the backend defenses to take out said defenses. Deploy her when some of the defenses are attacking the main army. Sending her in too early may result in her quick death. One way to do this is when you have a Siege Barracks in your army, fill that with Hog Riders and then when they deploy, place the Royal Champion with them.

Her Seeking Shield ability can also get rid of any Hidden Teslas that might appear to protect the Town Hall in such compartments. However, if the ability is used before the Hidden Teslas appear, it will not target them, so time it wisely.

If a single-target Inferno Tower is preventing a great placement, bring one Earthquake Spell and two Lightning Spells . This will allow her ability to one shot the Inferno Tower at not that much of a costly investment if you can use them properly.

Before the Town Hall 16 update, if you allow her hitpoints to deplete in order to automatically activate her ability, be wary that her shield throwing animation takes a few seconds to complete. If she is taking very heavy damage during this animation (which most often occurs when under fire from a single-target Inferno Tower), she will be defeated before being able to throw the shield to do damage, effectively wasting the ability. However, since the Town Hall 16 update, this no longer happens, as the Seeking Shield will be released instantly if she is about to get taken out by defenses.

The Haste Vial and Hog Rider Puppet combo is universally good at most attack strategies, allowing Royal Champion to briefly be invisible while the Hog Riders tank for her, and massively increases the damage she can do in total with the increased attack speed and Hog Riders and charges into the core of the base. However, this combo is weak to traps such as Giant Bombs, as they will be destroyed with the help of splash damage defenses, allowing the Royal Champion to be targeted, and defeat her.

The Seeking Shield and Rocket Spear allows her to pick up a few close by defenses then use her extra range to target defense deep within a base, making her functionally similar to a Flame Flinger for a while.

The Hog Rider Puppet and Royal Gem is useful for the Royal Champion Charge, allowing her to survive for much longer with the Hog Riders tanking for her and the massive health recovery from the ability as both Equipments provide more of it.

The Electro Boots and the Hog Rider Puppet can be a very useful combination because it allows her to deal with swarms, allowing the Hog Riders to tank for her and deal more damage, as well as to recover some health.

The Electro Boots and the Haste Vial can be helpful to destroy defenses quickly in a Royal Charge, supported by the Spirit Fox and Invisibility Spells . However, this leaves the Royal Champion with no extra healing, meaning that she is more vulnerable to major defenses.
Defend possible places where a Champion may be used with lots of high DPS defenses, as she has low health.
Defend your outer defenses with splash defenses and traps, as the Royal Champion is commonly teamed up with Hogs from a Siege Barracks or the Hog Rider Puppet.

That is, unless if the Royal Champion has the Rocket Spear, on which most cases will outrange the Inferno Tower and prevent her from triggering Skeleton Traps. In the case if Skeletons manage to distract the Royal Champion, the explosive spear will destroy all of them, due to its splash damage, if they are too close enough to be caught in the explosion. However, if the defensive Skeletons are well-spread, it will waste two or three Rocket Spears, reducing the Royal Champion's value which in turn increases the chances of a successful defense.

Use several troops or troops with high damage, as she attacks pretty slowly and has low hitpoints compared to relative troops. Dropping a Poison Spell decreases her attack speed further, giving your troops the upper hand.
For defense-targeting troops, trying to speed past a Royal Champion is a very viable strategy but may be risky if you fail or if they slow down while still in the radius of a Royal Champion.

Minion Prince.name: Minion Prince
notes: The Minion Prince is an aerial Hero who attacks all targets from long range that was introduced on November 25, 2024, with the Town Hall 17 update. He is unlocked by upgrading the Hero Hall to level 3, which requires Town Hall 9.

The Minion Prince will defend the village when assigned to a Hero Banner . The Minion Prince only defends his territory around his banner and will retreat if lured too far out. He does not need to be defeated for an attack to end in a 3-star. When defending, the Minion Prince will fly, making him unreachable by units that only target ground such as the Barbarian King.

When unlocked, he starts with the Henchmen Puppet and the Dark Orb. The Henchmen Puppet summons a pair of Henchmen , provides a brief invisibility, and grants an increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage. The Dark Orb launches an ice crystal that travels forward from the Minion Prince and affects all enemy targets in its vicinity as it travels. Affected targets take some damage and are slowed down temporarily. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health.

Upgrading the Blacksmith to level 3 and 5 unlocks the Metal Pants and Noble Iron respectively. The Metal Pants reduces damage taken for a period of time and grants a vastly increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to max health. The Noble Iron allows him to start the battle with several long-ranged attacks that deal extra damage. It gives a passive increases to attack speed.

He should be deployed behind the main army of higher health aerial units like Dragons , Dragon Riders , Electro Dragons, Lava Hounds , and Baby Dragons . They have a shorter range than Minion Prince and can tank for him as he deals massive amount of damage. Placing him together with Electro Dragons is not ideal, as he may take down buildings that allows the chain lightning to keep going. He should be placed to the the side of the main attack to funnel for the Electro Dragons.

Dragon Duke.name: Dragon Duke
notes: The Dragon Duke is the second aerial Hero and the sixth overall in terms of release who attacks all targets from melee range, introduced on March 1, 2026. He is unlocked by upgrading the Hero Hall to level 9, which requires Town Hall 15.

On his default skin, the Dragon Duke otherwise appears similar to a Dragon , except he is larger and bulkier, with a crimson body and a thistle-colored underside. He has orange eyes, thistle eyebrows, three short, thick yellow horns on top of his head (two of them being curved and parallelepiped and the center being shorter and flatter), and yellow rectangular plates on his back. The bottom part of his mouth is thistle-colored, with a similar layout to the Electro Dragon but with spikes on some parts. He also has a pair of handcuffs tied on his wrists and metal chains held by a golden lock in the center.

Like the Minion Prince , the Dragon Duke will defend the village when assigned to a Hero Banner . The Dragon Duke only defends his territory around his banner and will retreat if lured too far out. He does not need to be defeated for an attack to end in a 3-star. When defending, the Dragon Duke will fly, making him unreachable by units that only target ground such as the Barbarian King . He can neither use his passive ability nor use his Hero Equipment during this time.

When defending, the Dragon Duke will fly, making him unreachable by units that only target ground such as the Barbarian King . He can neither use his passive ability nor use his Hero Equipment during this time.

When unlocked, the Dragon Duke starts with the Fire Heart and Flame Blower. The Fire Heart allows the Dragon Duke to create a large death explosion. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health, and grants him self healing. The Flame Blower creates a cone of fire forward from the Dragon Duke and deals significant damage, similar to the Baby Dragon in the Builder Base, and grants an increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to maximum health.
The Fire Heart allows the Dragon Duke to create a large death explosion. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health, and grants him self healing.

Upgrading the Blacksmith to level 9 and 10 unlocks the Stun Blaster and Electro Fangs, respectively. The Stun Blaster creates a stunning shockwave around the Dragon Duke that stuns and damages buildings and defending troops except resource buildings and Walls , and grants an increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage and maximumm health. The Electro Fangs allows the Dragon Duke's regular attacks to gain the chain lightning effect, jumping to additional targets beyond the Duke's original target. It gives a passive increase to maximum health.

This ability is not disabled by the Dragon Duke's Pet if it is flying, like the Angry Jelly , but flying Pets from other Heroes will disable this ability. Summoned units from Pets (like Boogers from Sneezy ) can disable this ability. If the Dragon Duke is defeated while his Pet survives, that Pet will no longer be considered his own for this particular interaction; if the Dragon Duke is revived later by a Revive Spell , his Pet can disable the ability. The Phoenix does not disable the Royal Rampage ability when she hatches and revives the Dragon Duke, but only while her ability is active.
Summoned units from Pets (like Boogers from Sneezy ) can disable this ability.

When alone, the Dragon Duke can prove to be a very powerful Hero, able to destroy a compartment by himself with the help of his Flame Blower or Stun Blaster and Fire Heart , depending on the strategy. He is also resistant to trap damage, allowing him to endure Seeking Air Mines with ease. Be careful, as a single air unit (like Minions and Balloons ) can disable this ability, so keep in mind.
Other aerial Pets can be used, like the Greedy Raven and the Electro Owl , but the former only targets resource buildings while the latter cannot keep up with the Dragon Duke.

In air attacks involving Dragons , Dragon Riders , Electro Dragons , or a combination of these, he is treated as a tank for those units (similar to the Lava Hound ), usually paired with the Minion Prince and the Grand Warden set to Air mode. Their high hitpoints can protect him from taking too much damage, but due to his shorter range, he may be exposed to aerial traps , but he can also protect them in return. He may not use his Royal Rampage ability, but with the Stun Blaster , he can prevent major defenses from dealing damage to the army, especially single-target Inferno Towers , Monoliths , and Revenge Towers from taking them down, provided if used correctly.

Be mindful of the defending Dragon Duke, as he is untargetable by units which target ground. Use Dragons, Baby Dragons, the Archer Queen , the Royal Champion , or other units that target air to knock him out of battle, owing to his extremely high hitpoints.

He can become overwhelmed by swarms like Skeletons from Witches and Skeleton Traps , as he attacks one target at a time, even when using his fiery breath. However, this does not happen if he still has his Ability. The Flame Blower is able to take out all the Skeletons in front of him. The Stun Blaster deals enough damage to take out the Skeletons in a huge radius. And the Rocket Backpack not only takes out the Skeletons, but also causes the Dragon Duke to fly to the other side of the map.

Since the Dragon Duke is a single-target Hero, Witches can summon Skeletons that distract and eventually overwhelm him, buying time for defenses to quickly deal damage to him before he does too much damage to the base. However, if he has the Flame Blower ability still active, the attacker can use it to destroy the Witches and damage any nearby buildings, rendering it useless. It is only when it was already used does the strategy work on him. The Stun Blaster can also work in this regard, because it also stuns the Witches, allowing the Dragon Duke to take them out.

The Barbarian King and the Dragon Duke work together in defending against ground and air units. While the Barbarian King may not target air units, he can tank the damage while the Dragon Duke deals with them. Against ground targets, the Dragon Duke can deal with them without being damaged, unless if units that target air are in the main army, where he would tank the damage.

L.A.S.S.I.name: L.A.S.S.I
notes: L.A.S.S.I prioritizes a target within 2.5 tiles of the Hero that L.A.S.S.I is paired to. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , L.A.S.S.I behaves like a troop with no preferential target; they will attack the nearest building to them regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if they become aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.
L.A.S.S.I is able to jump over Walls to attack buildings and ground troops behind it.
L.A.S.S.I works great with the Royal Champion because they can support each other during an attack and both have the ability to jump over Walls.

She can also assist in funneling with the Barbarian King by taking out buildings behind Walls that the Barbarian King may have trouble reaching. However, this may put her in range of defenses that the Barbarian King may be out of range to tank for, which given her middling hit points, means she will fall rather quickly if this happens. To alleviate this, either use Wall Breakers to get the King in, or use Freeze Spells to stop the defenses .

L.A.S.S.I will not stray very far from her Hero. As a result, you could leave a gap between a layer of Walls and a building that you want to protect from L.A.S.S.I, and if she is paired to the Barbarian King or Archer Queen , L.A.S.S.I will not go for said buildings unless the Hero is attacking the Wall. In the latter case, however, note that the Queen will still be able to attack the building.

Mighty Yak.name: Mighty Yak
notes: The Mighty Yak is the third Pet unlocked from the level 3 Pet House . It has very high health, and does extra damage (x20) to Walls , similar to the Wall Wrecker .

Every time the Mighty Yak moves, once it is in contact with other buildings and it will ram into it and deal a first strike once it stops, then the second attack happens after 1.6 seconds then return to its normal attack rate of 2.1 seconds.

The Mighty Yak prioritizes a target within 7 tiles of the Hero that the Mighty Yak is paired to. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , the Mighty Yak behaves like a troop with no preferential target; they will attack the nearest building to them regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if they become aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.

When the Hero it is assigned to is knocked out, the Mighty Yak will temporarily be raged, doing extra damage and moving faster for 8 seconds. It does not enrage if its Hero is still available to fight but is removed from battle by a Recall Spell. If the Hero was knocked out but later revived by a Revive Spell , the Mighty Yak will not enrage if the Hero gets knocked out again.

The Mighty Yak pairs well with the Archer Queen . Because of its high hitpoints, the Mighty Yak is able to soak up hits for not only the Archer Queen, but also the Archers spawned by the Archer Puppet ability. It will break apart Walls to make Queen Charges much easier to pull off.

The Mighty Yak also pairs well with the Barbarian King . This is because the Barbarian King is the only melee Hero in the game and needs Walls to be broken to enter the base, and the Yak can help break such Walls. Funneling the King is still recommended, however, as the Yak will generally not attack Walls unless both it and the King need to.

Due to its high hitpoints as compared to other pets, the Yak is generally difficult to stop, especially when paired with the Barbarian King (who can tank for it). High-damage defenses such as single-target Inferno Towers , Ricochet Cannons , and Monoliths work very well should the Yak move in front of the Hero and be vulnerable to attack.

Alternatively, one could try to limit the Yak's capability of opening compartments, by designing a base with many compartments to minimize the damage possible should a compartment be opened. Having "island" compartments (where a single building is isolated from other buildings in its own compartment) can also be viable against the Yak when it is paired with the Barbarian King or Archer Queen, since without funneling or opening the compartment directly with Wall Breakers or otherwise, the Hero will likely move to the sides, taking their Yak along with him or her.

* When the Mighty Yak attacks a target, the initial attack speed is 0.5 seconds upon its first attack, when attacking a second time this increases to 1.6s, and every subsequent attack after that, its attack speed will be 2.1s, which is its default attack speed.

Electro Owl.name: Electro Owl
notes: The Electro Owl is the second Pet unlocked from the Pet House , available when the Pet House is upgraded to level 2. He is an air unit that attacks with chain lightning, similar to the Electro Dragon and Electrofire Wizard (if he is on Electro Mode). This chain lightning is only able to hit two targets just like the Mega Tesla , doing 80% of the primary target damage to the second target.

The Electro Owl prioritizes the target that the Hero that Electro Owl is paired to is currently targeting. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , Electro Owl behaves like a troop with no preferential target; they will attack the nearest building to them regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if they become aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.
The Electro Owl is unable to trigger traps , but can be affected by them if a nearby unit triggers them.

You can pair him with the Grand Warden to help destroy buildings, complementing the Warden's relatively low DPS. Although the Owl's DPS does not look impressive when compared to other pets, it is effectively 80% higher if he can consistently land chained lightning to hit two targets.

Generally, shorter-range Heroes will be able to keep the Electro Owl behind them, protecting him from most defenses (bar the aforementioned Air Defense). The air mode Grand Warden is not recommended if you want to keep the Owl alive for as long as possible, as he has a longer range, so will stay behind the owl, and can trigger air traps that can easily knock down the Owl.

Like when defending against Electro Dragons or Super Wizards , it can be helpful to space out buildings, if possible, to minimize chain damage. Buildings spaced 2 tiles apart will stop the Electro Owl from using his chain attack.

Unicorn.name: Unicorn
notes: The Unicorn is the fourth Pet unlocked from the Pet House , when the Pet House is upgraded to level 4. It heals its assigned Hero just like a Healer does. Unlike Healers, however, the Unicorn can target both ground and air units.
Unlike Healers, however, the Unicorn can target both ground and air units.

The Unicorn prioritizes the Hero that the Unicorn is paired to, and while active, Unicorn will follow the Hero and heal them whenever possible. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , Unicorn will target other troops and heal them. If the Unicorn has no target to heal, it will simply remain stationary even if it is taking damage.
Unlike other forms of healing, the Unicorn heals both Heroes and non-Heroes at the same rate; there is no "increased" healing rate for non-Heroes.

The Unicorn is helpful when paired up with the Barbarian King (especially at hybrid attacks) so that the Barbarian King can stay alive for longer, cleaning the non-defensive buildings (e.g. Gold Mines , Elixir Collectors , non-defensive Builder's Huts , etc.). The Barbarian King's slow movement speed also allows the Unicorn to have a maximum healing potential. However, if the Barbarian King is not taking much damage from defenses or is equipped with a sufficiently-leveled Vampstache , it could be advisable to pair him with another Pet . The Barbarian King's already sizeable amount of health allows him to stay alive for longer in the first place.

However, if the Barbarian King is not taking much damage from defenses or is equipped with a sufficiently-leveled Vampstache , it could be advisable to pair him with another Pet . The Barbarian King's already sizeable amount of health allows him to stay alive for longer in the first place.

The Unicorn is, however, more costly than a Healer when it comes to recalling a Hero walk, since the Recall Spell treats the Unicorn as taking up 20 housing space. This is only an issue, however, when using a Recall Spell that is not maxed (the Hero and 4 Healers take up 81 spaces, whereas a Hero, 3 Healers and a Unicorn take up 87), or if additional troops are to be recalled alongside the Hero walk.
The Unicorn has the ability to jump over Walls , even if the hero it is paired to cannot.

The Unicorn has rather low hitpoints compared to other Pets , and so is very vulnerable to defenses . Generally, the assigned Hero should be able to protect it from single-target defenses, but there are defenses that can hit both the Hero and the Unicorn which should be watched out for. If the Unicorn is used to heal the air-mode Grand Warden, this is an even bigger problem, as the Warden will not be able to protect the Unicorn against ground-only defenses.

Its slow movement speed can be an issue when using it with fast-moving Heroes like the Archer Queen or Royal Champion , as they can cause the Unicorn to lag behind over long distances and prevent it from utilizing its full healing potential (although regular Healers have the same problems, they have a longer range to make up for it).

A Scattershot is often a good tool to damage Unicorns hiding behind their assigned Hero , because of its ability to attack units behind the main target. However, this does not work when the Unicorn is healing the Grand Warden in air-mode because Scattershot cannot hit aerial and grounded targets simultaneously.
Other multi-targeting defenses like Inferno Towers , Ricochet Cannons , Multi-Archer Towers , Firespitters , and the Town Hall can also damage both the Unicorn and the Hero.

Phoenix.name: Phoenix
notes: When initially deployed, the Phoenix will start the battle as an egg, which does nothing but is invulnerable and cannot be targeted in this form, however she can trigger aerial traps. Once her Hero is initially knocked out however, she will hatch and revive the Hero, giving them both temporary invincibility for a short period, and then begin attacking as an air unit.

Phoenix prioritizes the target that the Hero that Phoenix is paired to is currently targeting. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , Phoenix behaves like a troop with no preferential target; they will attack the nearest building to them regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if they become aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.

The revived Hero will be immediately knocked out once the invincibility period ends, even if they do not take any damage during this period. They also cannot be healed during this period of invincibility.

If the Hero did not use their ability before being initially knocked out, they can use it while being revived. However, they do not gain any health regeneration if activated during this period, and may be knocked out mid-ability if the invincibility period expires. Similarly, if the Hero was midway through their ability when knocked out, their ability will continue through the revival period. If "Activate Hero Abilities on KO" is turned on in the settings, the Hero ability will be activated first before the Phoenix can attempt to revive them.

The Phoenix can be used to extend the lifetime of the Hero that she is paired to, allowing them to wreak more havoc. Heroes with a low survivability rate like the Royal Champion , or any hero used for Sui strategies, can prove a useful match. Pairing her with the Grand Warden is also a good idea, since it can extend the duration of his Life Aura ability; however, his survivability is generally quite high because of his staying behind other units and as such usually only revives when most other units are already dead. The Phoenix can also be useful for the Minion Prince , since she will revive him in the case if he gets knocked out. His high damage can be used to finish off the Town Hall.

Pairing the Phoenix with the Barbarian King allows it to extend your funnel to help with your main army and allows it to destroy more buildings. Additionally, during King Walks around the base, it will give it that extra hitpoints it needs, and in the middle of a base, it can give a extra few seconds of being a tank before the paired hero is knocked out.

Poison Lizard.name: Poison Lizard
notes: The Poison Lizard attacks quickly at range with poisoned spit, which slows down affected Heroes and Troops , in addition to causing them additional damage over time (as if they were hit by a Poison Spell ). It can also spit at buildings, but this currently causes neither not any slowdown nor no poison damage over time.

The Poison Lizard excels at taking down enemy Heroes, so it can be paired with Heroes that intend to attack other enemy Heroes. It can fare reasonably against enemy Clan Castle troops and Skeleton Traps , though it can only attack one target at a time and is thus prone to being overwhelmed. Pairing it with the Barbarian King or Archer Queen can be useful to back it up against swarms of troops (or against multiple Heroes at a time) since their abilities can spawn additional troops to attack.

To boost its survivability, one can pair it with the Barbarian King, which it will generally be able to stay behind and thus get shielded from most sources of damage. The Grand Warden as an alternative pick is also viable, provided he is himself backing up other troops or Heroes, since he and the Poison Lizard can stay behind other troops to be sufficiently protected. However, the Poison Lizard has lower range than the Warden so it will be exposed to enemy fire when the Warden is alone.

The Poison Lizard has a slow first attacking speed, and cannot deal with large swarms such as the Skeletons from Skeleton Traps, so it is advised to use secondary sources of damage to protect the Poison Lizard.

Diggy.name: Diggy
notes: Diggy burrows underground to attack buildings and troops, just like the Miner and his super counterpart , allowing him to bypass Walls (despite this, he will target Walls if his Hero attacks them). If he surfaces against a defensive building (which includes the Town Hall, if its weapon is activated), he stuns it for a short period of time. He will not stun defending Heroes and troops in the same way if he attacks them.

Diggy prioritizes the target that his paired Hero is currently targeting. If the Hero is knocked out, Diggy will seek out a new Hero, behaving as though he was paired with that Hero. If his paired Hero attacks an aerial unit, he will go towards the nearest building instead. If there are no Heroes for him to pair with, or if his Hero is removed from battle by a Recall Spell , Diggy will behave like a troop with no preferential target; he will attack the nearest building to him regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if he becomes aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.

Diggy obviously works best against defenses, since his stun will prevent them attacking for a period of time. Thus, pairing him with the Royal Champion , the Hero who largely prioritizes defenses, is ideal. Pairing him with the Grand Warden can be a viable option should the Champion be unavailable (or opts to use another Pet), due to the Warden's ability to bypass walls meaning Diggy will not get stuck on a Wall. He could even work for the Archer Queen , assuming you funnel the Archer Queen correctly and Diggy does not move too far.

Compared to the L.A.S.S.I (a popular pairing with the Royal Champion), Diggy has more utility owing to his stun ability, but his burrowing underground exposes the Champion to fire whereas the L.A.S.S.I, who moves in front of the Champion, would take hits for the Champion instead. Thus, to extend the Royal Champion's survivability, L.A.S.S.I may be more useful against large groups of defenses, while Diggy works better against smaller groups.
Diggy's stun effect can be very beneficial in a Hero Dive to get more value out of your Heroes, and to stun important defenses attacking your Heroes.

Diggy is also useful as a small tank, as he has the second-most health of all the pets, behind only the Mighty Yak . However, because he burrows underground to move, he will not be able to tank all the time.

If the Royal Champion activates the Rocket Spear ability, Diggy will go for the nearest defense she targets while she is out of range of other defenses. This can be very helpful if you want to stun a major defense from dealing too much damage in your army, which increases the survivability of your units in an attack. Be careful of longer ranged defenses like X-Bows , Monoliths, and Firespitters , though, as they will outrange her, and possibly cause her to get severely damaged, if not defeat her.

This can be very helpful if you want to stun a major defense from dealing too much damage in your army, which increases the survivability of your units in an attack. Be careful of longer ranged defenses like X-Bows , Monoliths, and Firespitters , though, as they will outrange her, and possibly cause her to get severely damaged, if not defeat her.

Diggy is very effective at reducing the threat of high damage dealing defenses like the Inferno Tower and the Monolith as he can stun buildings when resurfacing. Consider placing these sorts of defenses in range of one another to help take out Diggy and other attacking units.

Since Diggy can burrow underground and bypass Walls like Miners, he can often get to the outside/inside buildings to clean up if the opponent's army will take more time to get there. Therefore, spreading out your base and occupying the most space possible may be the difference between a high 2 star or a 3 star.

Frosty.name: Frosty
notes: Frosty periodically spawns Frostmites , which do a low amount of damage but inflicts the frost effect on targets they hit, causing them to slow down. Frosty himself also inflicts frost effects on defenses and troops he attacks.

Frosty prioritizes a target within 4.5 tiles of the Hero that Frosty is paired to. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , Frosty behaves like a troop with no preferential target; they will attack the nearest building to them regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if they become aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.

Frostmites prioritize defensive structures above all other targets, and will bypass all other types of enemy buildings and troops while any defenses remain on the battlefield. This is true even if they are under attack by enemy Clan Castle troops, heroes or Skeleton Trap skeletons. Note that like all troops that prioritize defenses, Frostmites do not consider the Clan Castle to be a defense regardless of whether it contains enemy troops, but do consider the defending Grand Warden and the activated Town Hall weapon (if any) to be defensive buildings.

Due to Frosty's relatively fragile health, it is recommended to keep him at the back, allowing him to freely summon Frostmites, which will slow down buildings and support the army. Hence, it is preferable to pair him with the Grand Warden , since they both support other troops. The Barbarian King is a good alternative choice since he can serve as a straightforward tank for Frosty.
Frosty's frost effect can help your army against buildings with high damage but with a slow rate of fire, such as the Monolith and the Eagle Artillery .

Frosty and his Frostmites' frost effect work similarly to an Ice Golem slowing the building he is attacking, hence, he is not able to reset a single-target Inferno Tower . So a Lightning Spell or Freeze Spell will help.

If using Frosty for a Warden Walk, you have to be careful since he will be standing in front of him rendering him vulnerable. As such, he can be great for smash style attacks, as he will be continuously staying behind your main army and spawning Frostmites .

Due to his low hitpoints, Frosty can easily be taken out by high-damage defenses such as Ricochet Cannons and the Giga Inferno , as they also have the ability to destroy the summoned Frostmites as well.

Spirit Fox.name: Spirit Fox
notes: When deployed, the Spirit Fox turns both itself and its assigned Hero invisible. The duration of invisibility depends on the level of the Spirit Fox. Once the prescribed duration expires, the invisibility will be reapplied after a 6-second cooldown. The invisibility is only applied whenever the Spirit Fox is on the field. If it is removed from battle by a Recall Spell , the Hero will not be able to turn invisible until the Spirit Fox is brought back onto the field. The Spirit Fox can apply invisibility solely to itself if its Hero is knocked out or recalled by a Recall Spell. Effects that affect attack speed will not affect the cooldown of the invisibility ability.

The invisibility is only applied whenever the Spirit Fox is on the field. If it is removed from battle by a Recall Spell , the Hero will not be able to turn invisible until the Spirit Fox is brought back onto the field. The Spirit Fox can apply invisibility solely to itself if its Hero is knocked out or recalled by a Recall Spell.
Effects that affect attack speed will not affect the cooldown of the invisibility ability.

The Spirit Fox prioritizes a target within 4.5 tiles of the Hero that the Spirit Fox is paired to. If the Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , the Spirit Fox behaves like a troop with no preferential target; they will attack the nearest building to them regardless of type, and will turn and attack enemy units if they become aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.

The Spirit Fox pairs incredibly well with the Royal Champion thanks to its ability which prevents the Royal Champion from being targeted at times, which increases the odds of the Royal Champion surviving. The Spirit Fox is able to jump over Walls , so will not lag behind the Royal Champion.

The Spirit Fox's Spirit Walk ability can be used to push the Hero into compartments with single target Inferno Towers . The ability resets the Inferno Tower's beam every time it activates; giving the Hero or other troops time to destroy it. It should be noted that the 6 second cooldown enables the Inferno Tower to reach its highest damage stage for a split second, which allows it to cause serious damage to your Hero if it was locked on for the entire duration of visibility.

It should not be paired with the Archer Queen or the Grand Warden as the Spirit Fox will run ahead of the two heroes in a lot of cases, and will result in a premature death of the pet, which is a waste of its valuable ability.

While the Barbarian King moves slower, the Spirit Fox will stay behind him because of the King's melee range. Its invisibility increases the tanking potential of the King, thus allowing him to survive longer. If the Barbarian King has the Vampstache equipped, he can use the invisibility periods to safely heal himself, further increasing his survivability. However, this will remove a tank from the battle, potentially exposing troops at the back susceptible to damage, which by the time when the king becomes visible again, could destroy some, if unlucky, most of your backline, which could ruin the attack.

A good way to defend against this is with Inferno Towers and Monolith to take out the Hero directly while it is visible to prevent value. However, the Inferno Tower takes a while to charge up, and if it is not in range when it is visible, it might deal minimal damage. so it is not the most reliable strategy.

Ricochet Cannons and Multi-Archer Towers can target both the Spirit Fox and its paired Hero, due to the ability to bounce its shots to another target and the ability to target three units at a time respectively, unless if there are other units close to its range.

Angry Jelly.name: Angry Jelly
notes: The paired Hero will prioritize defenses , but will also counterattack against defending enemy troops and Heroes that attack them if possible. This targeting manner is identical to the Royal Champion .

The Angry Jelly will stay above the Hero and target defenses in its range. It is untargetable by both defenses and traps while it is brainwashing the Hero. The Angry Jelly will keep up with the Hero even if they move faster than the Angry Jelly can normally move when its brainwash ability is active, similar to an inactive Phoenix. Take note that the cloned Archer Queens are not affected by the brainwash duration after the original Queen has activated her Magic Mirror ability.

Once the brainwash expires, the Angry Jelly loses its invulnerability and detaches from its Hero, and behaves as any other ranged aerial unit, making it vulnerable to Seeking Air Mines. However, if the Hero it is paired to is being damaged by a defense and the Angry Jelly is nearby, it will actually target the defense that is attacking the Hero in order to try and save it.
However, if the Hero it is paired to is being damaged by a defense and the Angry Jelly is nearby, it will actually target the defense that is attacking the Hero in order to try and save it.

The Angry Jelly prioritizes the target that the Hero that the Angry Jelly is paired to is currently targeting, but will counterattack the nearest defense if its Hero is being damaged by them. If its Hero has been knocked out or is removed from battle by a Recall Spell , the Angry Jelly will behave like a troop with no preferred target; it will target the nearest building regardless of type, and will turn and attack against enemy units if it becomes aware of any nearby and can fight back against them.

While it might see some effectiveness to pair alongside a support hero to target defenses, having a hero use the Angry Jelly to funnel will leave behind non-defensive buildings as neither Hero nor Pet will target them for the duration of the brainwash. If you are using it in a Warden Walk for funneling, then some additional cleanup troops will be required to remove the non-defensive buildings for funneling.

Alternatively, you can use the Barbarian King in a Hero Dive, and since it targets defenses, it will make the Hero Dive much more effective, since it will not be distracted by storages or the Clan Castle in the base. It will not also activate the Town Hall by accident just by itself.

While this ability is active, it makes the King behave similar to a Giant , Golem or Ice Golem , so if you are using a Root Rider army, you can use the Angry Jelly with the king to help with such attacks, and the Root Rider also removes walls, of which the Barbarian King will likely get stuck during the ability duration.

It can be paired with a Grand Warden wielding the Fireball equipment. Even though the Angry Jelly will be outranged by the Warden and will rarely be able to attack, this allows one to clearly visualize the defense the Warden will attack with the Fireball. With additional funneling support, the Warden can reach the core during the brainwash duration and use his Fireball to devastate it with the help of Invisibility and/or Overgrowth Spells with Earthquake Spells to destroy major defenses. Take note that he will not be healed from the damage from defenses without the Unicorn, so you will either need Healers or Druids to support him.
Take note that he will not be healed from the damage from defenses without the Unicorn, so you will either need Healers or Druids to support him.

It is not good to pair with the Archer Queen in a Queen Walk since she will not destroy the outside buildings if you are using the Angry Jelly for funneling. You will probably be better off using something like a Unicorn for extra healing instead. However, if the Archer Queen is paired with the Magic Mirror, when her ability is active, the summoned clone(s) will destroy non-defensive buildings on the outer perimeter of the base, while the original will target defenses, thus allowing for successful pseudo-Queen Charges.

However, if the Archer Queen is paired with the Magic Mirror, when her ability is active, the summoned clone(s) will destroy non-defensive buildings on the outer perimeter of the base, while the original will target defenses, thus allowing for successful pseudo-Queen Charges.

In aerial attacks, the Angry Jelly is useful to force the Minion Prince to temporarily target defenses, allowing him to destroy them faster to increase the chance of the army's success. Pairing this with the Noble Iron can turn this into a pseudo Rocket Spear . However, this leaves him very vulnerable to Seeking Air Mines and high-damaging defenses, if he is exposed.

Pairing it with the Dragon Duke also allows him to destroy defenses faster instead of letting him fly around the base. Pairing it with the Electro Fangs and Invisibility Spells can turn it into a Dragon Duke charge, akin to a pseudo Electro Boots charge.

Pairing it with the Royal Champion brings no benefit to her as her targeting will be unchanged by the brainwash effect. Although the Angry Jelly can get guaranteed damage due to its invulnerability, it cannot tank for her and does relatively low DPS compared to other "extra damage" pets, making it a rather poor choice for her, since she does not benefit from the ability, rather than to increase her damage output. Contrary to popular belief, the Angry Jelly does not prevent the Royal Champion from counterattacking against defending Clan Castle Troops, Skeleton Trap Skeletons, Heroes, or Guardians .

The Angry Jelly will not currently change the targeting of the troops summoned by Puppet Equipments such as Barbarian Puppet or Henchmen Puppet. The resulting troops will attack anything. The Hog Rider summoned from the Hog Puppet will target Defenses and ignore defending troops.

Since its defense-targeting mechanism is similar to the Royal Champion, Clan Castle troops and Skeleton Traps will be an effective counter to this, since they will distract the hero and waste the Angry Jelly's ability duration, and allow the defenses to destroy the hero faster, potentially forcing out an ability when it is not effective.

Another good counter to this are Walls . Since the Barbarian King cannot get past Walls, if there is nothing to help him break through, he will spend a majority of its ability duration breaking a Wall (if there are no defenses outside the walls) to reach a defense, which can lead to him taking unnecessary damage and waste the Angry Jelly's brainwash duration. The same issue is also faced by the Archer Queen, since she too cannot get past Walls without help. Although her range allows her to destroy defenses behind Walls, without wall-breaking support she may walk around the outside of a base to continue attacking front line defenses, or may get stuck attacking walls directly.

The same issue is also faced by the Archer Queen, since she too cannot get past Walls without help. Although her range allows her to destroy defenses behind Walls, without wall-breaking support she may walk around the outside of a base to continue attacking front line defenses, or may get stuck attacking walls directly.

Sneezy.name: Sneezy
notes: When deployed, Sneezy flies in the air and maintains distance from the paired Hero. She periodically sneezes to spawn Boogers which damage buildings, usually within 5.5 tiles from them.
Each Booger is spawned from Sneezy every 10 seconds, and there can be a maximum of two at a time. Boogers have moderate damage and hitpoints, and cannot trigger air Traps .

When her paired Hero is knocked out in battle and Sneezy is still active, Sneezy will become enraged, becoming a short-range pet which that targets defenses and attacks by screeching, dealing high damage per second. She will continue to spawn Boogers while in this state but will temporarily stop attacking for a brief period when she does so. Her enraged status grants Sneezy a minuscule 1% damage increase for 30s. This damage increase is barely noticeable, and the effect will be replaced by other damage-increasing effects like Rage Spells , but she will still retain the rage effect until it ends.

Her enraged status grants Sneezy a minuscule 1% damage increase for 30s. This damage increase is barely noticeable, and the effect will be replaced by other damage-increasing effects like Rage Spells , but she will still retain the rage effect until it ends.
Sneezy can be a powerful Pet if used correctly, especially in Warden Charges, as the summoned Boogers will be able to distract defenses or even allow them to create a funnel for your main attack.

Since Sneezy stays well behind her paired Hero, she will not be able to protect Healers from Seeking Air Mines since her range is slightly more than that of the Healer's, so you may need to use Balloons or Baby Dragons to search for Seeking Air Mines.

Since the Boogers will not trigger Seeking Air Mines, it is a good idea to spread them away from each other so that armies like Dragons , Electro Dragons and Dragon Riders will be more likely to be targeted by them.

Greedy Raven.name: Greedy Raven
notes: When deployed, Greedy Raven flies in the air and maintains distance from the paired Hero. He flings his feathers rapidly, targeting Resource Buildings near the Hero first and deals five times the damage to them, usually within 8 tiles from them. If his Hero is knocked out or removed from battle by a Recall Spell , Greedy Raven behaves like a troop that prioritizes Resource Buildings.

The Greedy Raven can be a powerful Pet if used correctly, especially in Queen or Warden Walks or Charges, as the clearing high hitpoints Storages allow him to create a funnel for your main attack and make the walk faster to prevent time fails. He can also act as a Seeking Air Mine absorber, tanking up to 2 Seeking Air Mines if sufficiently leveled, protecting the Healers behind. However, the Greedy Raven has a very long range, and is quite unlikely to go ahead of Healers. It is instead better to use Balloons to protect both Healers and the Greedy Raven.
However, the Greedy Raven has a very long range, and is quite unlikely to go ahead of Healers. It is instead better to use Balloons to protect both Healers and the Greedy Raven.

Air Defenses are one of the defenses that can take the Greedy Raven down, since he only targets resource buildings, the Air Defense will have no problem to easily take him out, provided that he is within the range of said defense. Other anti-air defenses can also work in this regard, as well as aerial Skeletons , as he cannot fight back against them unless all resource buildings are destroyed. All of these can take down the Greedy Raven if defenses are placed correctly. Seeking Air Mines are the worst enemy for the Greedy Raven. Place them in areas where the attacker is most likely to deploy, but in a way that it would target a more important unit, such as a Healer.
