In addition to the ability, the Lavaloon Puppet grants additional hitpoints and damage per second to the Grand Warden.
Every three levels, it increases the level of the Lavaloon summoned by one level except for levels 21 to 27, where it only requires two. At levels 9 and 21, it summons an additional Lavaloon each.

The Lavaloon Puppet, when activated, summons Lavaloons to tank for other aerial units such as Dragons and Electro Dragons from aerial traps like as Air Bombs and Seeking Air Mines , improving their survivability. After the Lavaloons have been summoned, the Grand Warden will follow them, which might lead him to being defeated too early, so deploy your main army before you use the ability, and set your Grand Warden to air for the best effect. Additionally, when Lavaloons attack, they can deal heavy splash damage, in order for other aerial units to finish them off.

After the Lavaloons have been summoned, the Grand Warden will follow them, which might lead him to being defeated too early, so deploy your main army before you use the ability, and set your Grand Warden to air for the best effect.
Additionally, when Lavaloons attack, they can deal heavy splash damage, in order for other aerial units to finish them off.

Clone Spell can be used on the Lavaloons to summon massive amount of Lavaloon Pups, this strategy is only effective at lower Town Halls as more and more splash damage and multi target defenses get introduced.

An important milestone of this equipment is upgrading it to level 9, since it will spawn two Lavaloons to help out in battle, making it the biggest spike in power for this equipment. Similarly, having it upgraded to level 21 will spawn 3 Lavaloons, which also works and provides more tanking.

When used with the Life Gem , it will not have much effect to the summoned Lavaloons and other air units such as Dragons, since their hitpoints are too high. However, it can be useful for the LaLo strategy, since the aura can boost the hitpoints of Balloons. Lavaloon Pups can also gain benefits due to their low hitpoints, although their survivability remains low, especially without the Eternal Tome.

However, it can be useful for the LaLo strategy, since the aura can boost the hitpoints of Balloons. Lavaloon Pups can also gain benefits due to their low hitpoints, although their survivability remains low, especially without the Eternal Tome.

When used with the Rage Gem , it allows the Lavaloons to deal more damage when they attack, and their Lavaloon Pups will also benefit from it. Not only do these things apply, it can also be very helpful to further increase the damage of already-high damage aerial units, thereby increasing the synergy of this Equipment. However, this leaves him vulnerable to Seeking Air Mines, if they somehow manage to target him first.
However, this leaves him vulnerable to Seeking Air Mines, if they somehow manage to target him first.

It can be very useful to help your Battle Blimp to go towards its desired target, so that the attack can be executed successfully, especially in the cases of a Super Archer Blimp or a Blizzard, since after the update that reworked the Eternal Tome, which the Battle Blimp will lose its invincibility when it leaves the aura. To do this, at least two Air Defenses must be destroyed (with each one on both opposite sides of the base). Doing it correctly will increase the chances of a successful attack, otherwise they will be split from the Battle Blimp, leading to the Blimp's premature destruction and may cause a one-star or a loss of an attack.

When used with the Healing Tome , the ability will not be as effective on the summoned Lavaloons, as they will only heal a small portion of their hitpoints and the Lavaloon Pups die easily, and only heals the supporting army.

When used with the Fireball , it is complicated as the Fireball will be summoned first, and then the Lavaloons, on which the Grand Warden might follow them, if the player does not deploy the main army.

Defending against Lavaloons are quite tricky as they can distract Air Defenses to provide cover for other aerial units. The best way to prevent this is to spread them from other important defenses from other Air Defenses, so that the Lavaloons will be split away from the main army. Aerial traps can also help in this regard. However, this does not work if the attacker manages to destroy too many Air Defenses, either by using Lightning Spells , Earthquake Spells , or using ranged Hero Equipment such as the Giant Arrow .
However, this does not work if the attacker manages to destroy too many Air Defenses, either by using Lightning Spells , Earthquake Spells , or using ranged Hero Equipment such as the Giant Arrow .

Single-target Inferno Towers and Monoliths are very effective against Lavaloons, because they will get popped early on, while the multi-target Inferno Towers and Multi-Archer Towers are very useful in warding off Lavaloon Pups, because they can target Lavaloon Pups independently of any shielding Lavaloons.

Useful troops to include in a defending Clan Castle to oppose Lavaloons are Super Dragons and Electro Titans . A Super Dragon can deal strong damage to Lavaloons and his area damage can eliminate nearby Lavaloon Pups, while the Electro Titan will outright wipe out any Lavaloon Pups that come near her due to her electric aura.

Henchmen Puppet.name: Henchmen Puppet
notes: The Henchmen Puppet appears as a light blue keychain with black eyes, horns, and a spiked collar at the end, held by chains connecting to a chibi-styled head of the Henchman. When equipped, it enables the Minion Prince to summon two Henchmen when using his ability. Additionally, upon activation, he turns invisible for a short duration, which, among other things, allows these Henchmen to tank for him, all while distracting defenses from targeting him.
In addition to the ability, the Henchmen Puppet grants additional damage and hitpoints to the Minion Prince, and also increases the amount of health he recovers when using the ability.
It can also be used to stop defenses from targeting him, such as single-target Inferno Towers, as this ability turns him invisible for one second.
It can be paired with Dark Orb , slowing down defenses in a large area and increasing the effectiveness of the tanking by the Henchmen.

Dark Orb.name: Dark Orb
notes: The Dark Orb appears as a black orb with a glowing magenta and cyan crack from top to bottom and glows cyan at the edge. It summons a crystal from a portal behind the Minion Prince which then travels forward for a short while at where he is facing, dealing small amount of damage and slowing defenses and defending troops in a radius around it.
The Dark Orb can slow down a full compartment of defenses, which can be extra effective at the core of the base where most high value defenses reside.

There are different interactions when the Dark Orb is paired with other Hero Equipment for the Minion Prince: It can be paired with Henchmen Puppet , slowing down defenses in a large area increases the effectiveness of the tanking by the Henchmen. When paired with the Metal Pants , it also allows him to take reduced damage after he fires the Dark Orb. When paired with the Noble Iron , this combo may not be as effective due to its long range when he initially attacks from a long range, wasting most of the Dark Orb's range, even if paired with the Angry Jelly . However, as the Noble Iron is a passive ability while the Dark Orb is active, you can choose to use the two separately.
It can be paired with Henchmen Puppet , slowing down defenses in a large area increases the effectiveness of the tanking by the Henchmen.

When paired with the Noble Iron , this combo may not be as effective due to its long range when he initially attacks from a long range, wasting most of the Dark Orb's range, even if paired with the Angry Jelly . However, as the Noble Iron is a passive ability while the Dark Orb is active, you can choose to use the two separately.

Because the Dark Orb deals damage while traveling a significant distance, its use can activate Invisibility Spell Towers , Giga Teslas and Giga Infernos from afar. Activating a Town Hall weapon early can prove to be a liability, so care must be taken when doing this. On the other hand, activating a Town Hall weapon can also be a benefit as it causes defense-targeting troops to start targeting the Town Hall.
Be aware of where the Minion Prince is facing before using the Dark Orb, especially when he is about to change targets, as he may end up wasting it by shooting it to the side or even outwards.

Metal Pants.name: Metal Pants
notes: The Metal Pants appear as a piece of chain mail pants with the inner side and groin cover made with leather, with a tied cincture acting as a belt.
When equipped, it enables the Minion Prince to create an orange shield around him which temporarily reduces the damage from any type.
In addition to the ability, the Metal Pants grants additional hitpoints to the Minion Prince, and also increases the amount of health he recovers when using the ability.

The Metal Pants can be used to let the Minion Prince tank Seeking Air Mines better when he is by himself, and can also reduce damage taken from defenses. However, its weakness is that single-target Inferno Towers at maximum stage and Monolith can take lots of damage if they had locked on to him, eventually getting him knocked out.
However, its weakness is that single-target Inferno Towers at maximum stage and Monolith can take lots of damage if they had locked on to him, eventually getting him knocked out.

Protect your single-target Inferno Towers and the Monolith in a way so that the army will be separated from the Minion Prince, allowing the Inferno Tower and Monolith to lock onto him and possibly defeat him, even with his barrier.

Noble Iron.name: Noble Iron
notes: The Noble Iron is a passive Hero Equipment that appears to be a dumbbell with a brass bar and crown-shaped end, and iron weights bolted on each end. When equipped, it increases the range and damage of the first few shots of the Minion Prince after he is deployed and modify his shots into a big purplish iron fist.

In addition to the above pairing, one can add Air Mode Grand Warden into the charge as he will attack the same target with the Minion Prince and may help provide some passive bonus based on his own Equipment, and both can be recalled after the charge is finished. While Grand Warden have more range than Minion Prince normally and stays safe behind him, it is not true when the Noble Iron ability is active, be careful to not let him be target first.

At level 12 and above, only the Inferno Artillery , Firespitters , Long Range Multi-Gear Tower , and Longshot can match or outrange the Minion Prince with Noble Iron, which renders him vulnerable, especially when exposed. While the Eagle Artillery can also target him when Noble Iron is active, he most likely is deployed at the start of the attack so it will remain inactive. Even when he is deployed later when it is active to help with the back end, the Eagle Artillery will likely target the main army instead.

While the Eagle Artillery can also target him when Noble Iron is active, he most likely is deployed at the start of the attack so it will remain inactive. Even when he is deployed later when it is active to help with the back end, the Eagle Artillery will likely target the main army instead.

Action Figure.name: Action Figure

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Friend or Foe event for 3,100 Buy in Splash Bash event for 3,100 Buy in Equipment Blast event for 3,100 Buy in Wise Warriors event for 3,100 or purchasable from the Trader for 1,500

notes: The Action Figure is a doll of a Giant with a bare chest, brown and orange bands on his arms and legs, and green underpants.
When the ability is used, the Archer Queen will summon a Giant Giant , in addition to turning invisible for 1 second. The level of the Giant Giant depends on the level of the Action Figure.
In addition to the ability, the Action Figure grants additional damage per second, hitpoints, and self-regeneration to the Archer Queen.

This Hero Equipment can be used as a superior version of the Magic Mirror . It pairs well with the Giant Arrow , Healer Puppet , Archer Puppet , and Frozen Arrow . Additionally, it can also be paired with the Magic Mirror for more damage to creating a funnel for the main army, like Dragons .

Since the Giant Giant that spawns has very high amounts of hitpoints, it is a good idea to pair this up with an Apprentice Warden , since his uncapped HP boost can significantly impact the Giant Giant himself, allowing him to tank more.

Be careful of Inferno Towers and Monoliths, as they are able to take down the Giant Giant, so use Freeze , Invisibility , or Overgrowth Spells to stop them from attacking. Skeleton Spells and Bat Spells can also help in this regard.

It functions as an alternative to the Mighty Yak for the Archer Queen, as a bulky meatshield for her that also helps her break through Walls . This is especially useful when another Hero is using it, and allows the Archer Queen to use a different pet .

When the defense he is targeting through a Wall is destroyed, he may target another building, wasting all of the Wall damage. It can be seen in his demonstration clip when the X-Bow is destroyed by the Archer Queen.

When defending against this Equipment, place high-damage defenses away from each other, otherwise the attacker will get a lot of value from these spells mentioned above. Similarly, placing defenses at least 1 tile away from Walls will prevent the Giant Giant from dealing damage to them while he is attacking said Walls.
Inferno Dragons can significantly drain the hitpoints of the summoned Giant Giant because of his high damage.

The summoned Giant Giant cannot jump over Walls, however they can deal massive damage to them, just in case if the Archer Queen wants to destroy a closed compartment. Therefore, place low-tier defenses on the outside to expose the Archer Queen, rendering the tank useless.

Meteor Staff.name: Meteor Staff

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Cosmic Rock event for 3,100 Buy in Wise Warriors event for 3,100 or purchasable from the Trader for 1,500

notes: The Meteor Staff appears to be a golden wand with a large knob on the bottom, has a large meteor shell floating above, and glows cyan. When equipped, the Meteor Staff will periodically summon meteors on the nearest defensive building. These meteors do area damage to both ground and air units. The damage radius is enough to damage adjacent buildings, when targeting a 3x3 building, similar to the damage area of a Lightning Spell .

Buildings can be hit at any distance, but only when the Minion Prince is actively on the map and not knocked out. Buildings must be targetable (i.e. not under Invisibility Spell or Overgrowth Spell ) in order to be hit. In the event there are no defenses to target, meteors will instead attack the nearest building. Meteors do not spawn if there are no targetable buildings.
In the event there are no defenses to target, meteors will instead attack the nearest building. Meteors do not spawn if there are no targetable buildings.

The Meteor Staff allows the Minion Prince to summon Meteors to damage or destroy defenses from a long distance. It can also help with clean up, since its unlimited range allows it to destroy buildings from far away, preventing potential time fails.
Upgrading the Meteor Staff allows the Minion Prince to summon more meteors that deal more damage, as higher levels can exponentially increase the damage output.
Meteors cannot trigger Invisibility Spell Towers since they last too short to activate them, and must be triggered by other means ( Giant Arrow , Log Launcher's logs, Spiky Ball , etc).

Because of the nature of the Meteor Staff being a passive ability, it might not be the worst idea to pair it up with a Revive Spell if the attacking Minion Prince gets knocked out, in order to help with clean up, given by the passive Meteor Strike ability, and its infinite range can be beneficial so long as the Minion Prince is alive. If he is knocked out however, the meteors will not spawn.

Frost Flake.name: Frost Flake

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Meltdown Mayhem event for 3,100 or purchasable from the Trader for 1,500

notes: When activated, the Frost Flake will send a number of ice flakes simultaneously to a number of defenses nearest to the Royal Champion. Each flake does a small amount of damage on impact and freezes the target for a few seconds. If there are not enough defenses to target, non-defensive buildings as well as defending troops can be targeted. The flakes can hit air units. Only one ice flake can hit a given target. If there are insufficient targets, the excess flakes will be wasted.

Because of this, it is not the most effective Equipment for Royal Champion Charge, as the passive Hero Boost does no provide any damage increases to make her deal with defenses faster, and the short freeze time will not provide more value than the ability of the Haste Vial or Rocket Spear during the charge, while both of them also provide passive damage per second increases.

When paired with the Seeking Shield , there are some anti-synergy as the Shield also target the closest defenses, potentially wasting some of the ice flakes freezes. It is outclassed by the pairing with Haste Vial or Rocket Spear as it spreads out the power of Royal Champion's damage boost from the ability over time instead of a burst, while Rocket Spear also allows her to stay back when supporting the main army, keeping her safer with the extra max health provided by Frost Flake.

When paired with the Electro Boots , the role of the Royal Champion is still backend support instead of doing a charge with reasons stated above. The main reason to still use it is the self healing, providing health over the course of the raid while she supports the army, with the passive aura damage being a bonus.

Stick Horse.name: Stick Horse

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Wise Warriors event for 3,100

notes: The Stick Horse appears as a stick consisting of a white horse head on top with a brown strap on its nose and a dark yellow mane with orange tips covering its eyes. When equipped, it creates a yellow aura and leaves behind a trail of its matching color, allowing the Barbarian King to jump over Walls and lets him move and attack faster for a while when deployed.

In general, the Stick Horse is a direct upgrade over the Rage Vial , it provides more than twice the maximum hitpoints compared to the health recovery of the Rage Vial and almost twice the passive damage increase. For the ability, the duration last three times longer, despite only having around half of the movement speed increase and the damage per second multiplier is much smaller (damage increase for Rage Vial, attack speed increase for the Stick Horse), the longer duration and higher passive damage increase make up for it. The only downside being it always activates at the start of the battle and usually is not active in the core of a base.

In addition, using a Rage Spell allows him to deal much more damage because of its longer rage duration, destroying high-hitpoint buildings like Storages and merged defenses with ease. Beware of Monoliths and Single-Target Inferno Towers as they can still do major damage even with the Giant Gauntlet's damage reduction.

Defending against the Barbarian King's Stick Horse ability may be difficult, but it can be countered effectively by opening up a Wall in a compartment. When this happens, the Barbarian King will go to a much longer distance around the walls to reach his target instead of jumping over them. This allows defenses time to quickly deal damage to him before he causes too much destruction.

Monoliths , single-target Inferno Towers and Revenge Towers (in its final stage) can quickly whittle out the hitpoints of the Barbarian King, even when his Giant Gauntlet ability is used. Traps like Spring Traps and Skeleton Traps can also help in this regard, though the former deals reduced damage to the King as he is a Hero and the latter is ineffective if the King is using the Giant Gauntlet.

Clan Castle troops like Witches can overwhelm the King, provided that if he is not equipped with the Giant Gauntlet, they will outrange him while their summoned Skeletons can overwhelm the King with the help of other high-damaging defenses. If the King is equipped with the Giant Gauntlet, the splash damage combined with the increased movement speed and attack speed will easily kill the Witches.

Fire Heart.name: Fire Heart
notes: When equipped, it grants a large amount of health regeneration and a death explosion to the Dragon Duke. The death explosion can only trigger once, for the first time the Dragon Duke falls. If he is revived later, his subsequent defeats will not cause an explosion.
The death explosion can only trigger once, for the first time the Dragon Duke falls. If he is revived later, his subsequent defeats will not cause an explosion.

Rocket Backpack.name: Rocket Backpack

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Sound of Clash event for 3,100 or purchasable from the Trader for 1,500

notes: When activated, the Dragon Duke will fly in a straight line towards the center of the base and across the whole base until the edge while spitting flames, damaging everything along his path. While in the ability, the Dragon Duke is untargetable; he will not trigger traps or Clan Castle troops, but will trigger Hidden Teslas to appear. The Dragon Duke's Pet , if it is present and still alive, will also be transported during the ability. It is temporarily removed while the ability is ongoing, and re-placed next to the Dragon Duke after the ability is over. However, Dragon Duke can still be affected by the Poison effect from the Poison Spell Tower if he passes through its radius.
However, Dragon Duke can still be affected by the Poison effect from the Poison Spell Tower if he passes through its radius.
In addition to the ability, it grants additional damage, max health, and health recovery to the Dragon Duke.

Similiar to Giant Arrow , activating the Rocket Backpack towards the area of coverage of an Invisibility Spell Tower can be used as a means to trigger the spell early, preventing it from messing up the attack once it reaches the vicinity of the tower. However, the Invisibility Spell Tower has a relatively short cooldown, so the ability should not be used too early, lest the tower reload in time.

The Flame Blower's area of effect will be oriented in the direction that the Dragon Duke will fly in during the Rocket Backpack ability. This allows the Duke to deal extra damage against his initial targets but also limits the potential damage zone of the Flame Blower.

Stun Blaster.name: Stun Blaster
notes: https://clashofclans.fandom.com/wiki/Stun_Blaster
The Stun Blaster is a piece of Common Hero Equipment for the Dragon Duke . It is unlocked when the Blacksmith is upgraded to level 9, which requires Town Hall 16.
The Stun Blaster appears as a ray gun, with a gear and antenna on its back, a red trigger, a wooden grip, and a metal dish in front, already shooting shockwaves.
When activated, it creates a shockwave around the Dragon Duke, dealing damage and stunning defending troops and buildings for a while.
In addition, the Stun Blaster grants additional hitpoints and damage per second to the Dragon Duke.

Flame Blower.name: Flame Blower
notes: When activated, it allows the Dragon Duke to create a cone of flame ahead of him, dealing massive damage. It also increases the health recovery.

Electro Fangs.name: Electro Fangs
notes: The first target struck by the chain lightning (and which takes the full damage from the ability) is a target near the Dragon Duke's initial target; the original target takes no extra damage. If there are no targets to chain to, the chain lightning will not occur.

The Electro Fangs' chain lightning property is helpful to assist the Dragon Duke in taking out swarms of enemy troops (such as Skeleton Traps used for stalling), as he is a single-target Hero and would otherwise require support or using his ability to do area damage.

Revenge Deck.name: Revenge Deck

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Awesome Medal Event for 3,100

notes: The Revenge Deck is the second Epic piece of Hero Equipment for the Dragon Duke . It made its debut in the Awesome Medal Event starting August 12, 2026.

Counters are limited to a frequency of once per 0.8 seconds for each unit attacking the Duke; any subsequent attacks by the same attacker in this time window will not be countered. If multiple enemy units attack the Dragon Duke at the same time, each unit is countered independently, i.e. has their own separate cooldown.

Counters do not occur against the following: Traps and defensive Spells; Non-damaging effects (such as Air Sweeper knockback); Attacks occurring more than 25 (?) tiles away (such as Eagle Artillery if far enough away); Attacks from units that are already destroyed, or which get destroyed upon their attack (e.g. Yetimites and Electromites ); Certain other effects such as Electro Dragon 's chain and death damage, Firemites ' area-of-effect damage, or Electro Titan 's aura.

Bomb.name: Bomb
notes: Bombs are traps that remain hidden until they are activated by an attacking troop moving into their trigger radius like other traps. It is the first such trap unlocked.
Once triggered, Bombs must be re-armed, which can be done for free and takes place automatically after logging into the game.

Although they are the weakest of all the traps, Bombs can still have a positive impact on the effectiveness of a village's defense if properly placed, but only if they are always re-armed after triggering.
Even though Bombs are classified as " Defensive Buildings ", they are not buildings and do not need to be triggered/destroyed for your enemy to reach 100% destruction (nor do they count toward it).

The Bomb explodes approximately 1.5 seconds after an enemy comes within 1 tile of it, causing splash damage to every enemy ground troop within 3 tiles. This delay means that you will want to place the Bomb in an area where troops are likely to remain for a period of time like right next to a building they are attacking.

A Bomb can destroy an equivalent-level Wall Breaker in one hit. Since the Wall Breaker A.I. targets wall junctions, place Bombs at outside perimeter intersections and corners for maximum effect. This can be used to ruin pathing for a potential Queen Charge or similar strategy, though it is ineffective against Super Wall Breakers (or if the enemy deploys a sufficient amount of Wall Breakers and they are able to reach the Walls).

This can be used to ruin pathing for a potential Queen Charge or similar strategy, though it is ineffective against Super Wall Breakers (or if the enemy deploys a sufficient amount of Wall Breakers and they are able to reach the Walls).

One defensive strategy commonly used for the placement of Bombs is to position them along the outside Wall , behind external buildings. The external buildings serve to delay the enemy troops until they have grouped up, so that when they attack the Wall, the Bomb hits many troops at once. This is most effective against low-health troops, though grouping enough Bombs together can be a serious hazard for Giants , too.

Be cautious when upgrading a Bomb, as this will reveal its location. Combat this by relocating it during the upgrade period, since it will not trigger during that period anyway. This is useful against players who scout out your base ahead of time for revenge attacks. This does not apply when the player is in Legend League, where the Bomb will always be active while it is upgraded.

Exploiting the way the A.I. targets buildings can dramatically increase the defensive effectiveness of your Bombs. For example, a group of 2 to 3 Bombs placed between a pair of resource collectors is very likely to destroy an entire group of Goblins as they pass from one collector to the next.

A Bomb upgraded to level 4 or higher can instantly kill a group of summoned Skeletons , making Bombs very effective against Witch based attacks. However, note that Skeletons on their own are unable to trigger Bombs, meaning they will not be immediately wiped out until other troops (such as Giants) trigger it.

Bombs are useful against players who use a Battle Blimp filled with Sneaky Goblins who aim to use the Sneaky Goblins to quickly destroy the Town Hall. Since Bombs trigger even if the Sneaky Goblins are invisible, a sufficient amount of Bombs around the Town Hall can quickly kill the Sneaky Goblins and defuse this tactic. This increases in importance at the highest Town Hall levels, where Town Hall sniping strategies become more viable as the Town Hall gains an increasingly devastating weapon.
Bombs can damage Witches fairly, also wiping out her summoned Skeletons. Pair this with a sufficiently-leveled Giant Bomb, and this combo will destroy them.

Bombs do only slight damage to high health troops but will destroy small troops. Try using tanks or high health troops like a Giant to absorb the Bomb. Skeletons spawned by Witches or a Skeleton Spell do not trigger Bombs, so using such troops to trigger the traps may be less beneficial in Witch-based strategies.
Skeletons spawned by Witches or a Skeleton Spell do not trigger Bombs, so using such troops to trigger the traps may be less beneficial in Witch-based strategies.

If you suspect that a particular location has Bombs in it, use a small troop, such as a Barbarian to trigger them. Do not send small troops in mass, or they may all be heavily damaged at best, or completely wiped out at worst. Air troops like Minions do not have to worry about Bombs as Bombs cannot damage them.

Spring Trap.name: Spring Trap
notes: It prioritizes the unit with the highest housing space if there are more than two units that are in its trigger radius.

The Spring Trap has a short activation delay. Units with a movement speed of 32 or above, such as the Goblin , can move across it unaffected unless they stop on top of the trap. Units that are slightly slower, such as an Archer , can also avoid the trap by simply passing over a corner of the Spring Trap's tile.

A sound strategy for Spring Traps is to place them in an intentionally-designed Wall gap. As troops will generally tend to go through the gap rather than fight their way through the Wall, they will be directed right over the Spring Trap and be bounced to their death. Remember, Spring Traps are one-time-use and until being re-armed it will leave an undefended gap in the Wall after an attacker has triggered it. A modified version of this strategy is to place Walls inside your base so that the enemy Troops have to walk over the Spring Trap to attack nearby buildings.
A modified version of this strategy is to place Walls inside your base so that the enemy Troops have to walk over the Spring Trap to attack nearby buildings.

You can also place them in front of commonly-targeted Walls to stop Wall Breakers from breaking them, forcing the attacker to deploy a second wave if they have one or be disadvantaged in the attack. However, this may fail to deter Super Wall Breakers , as the Spring Trap will instead instantly trigger its Mega Bomb ability.
You can place them in between Defensive Buildings to take out a defense-targeting troop with high hitpoints.

Troops with abilities that activate on their destruction can still activate these abilities when getting bounced off a Spring Trap. For example, if an Ice Golem is launched, he still freezes nearby structures and enemy troops since he was technically defeated on the spot.

The Spring Trap can be used to stun Heroes and slightly damage them, especially the Royal Champion , since the short stun time will force the attacker to use more spells than normal in a Champion Charge, thus reducing the value they can get.

If you suspect that a certain location (such as a gap in the Wall ) has a Spring Trap, try to trigger the trap by using a single expendable troop like a Barbarian or a Goblin, as high housing-space units such as ground units like P.E.K.K.As , Root Riders , Electro Titans , Golems , Heroes , Siege Machines , or Pets will take massive amounts of damage from it, although it is limited to one. You can also use a small unit to protect a larger unit with low hitpoints from being flung off the map.

Air Bomb.name: Air Bomb
notes: The Air Bomb is unlocked at Town Hall 5. It is the first trap that targets aerial troops . It triggers when a flying troop comes into proximity, then rises out of the ground and follows the nearest flying troop. The Air Bomb explodes after coming in contact with the flying troop or—if dead—the location of its death.

It is extremely effective against large groups of Minions , Lava Pups and Bats spawned by Bat Spells and does a significant amount of damage to Balloons (especially level 4 and below). It is much less effective against higher health targets such as Baby Dragons , Dragons , and Electro Dragons .

In the early game, placing an Air Bomb next to an Air Defense can be very effective. After a Ground Troop destroys the Air Defense, the enemy might deploy all of their powerful air units at once, and the Air Bomb may be able to damage a vast majority of the troops. However, at higher Town Hall levels, it is not recommended to place Air Bombs in the range of an Air Defense as Lava Hounds will fly directly towards it, which will trigger the trap and absorb the hit, dealing next to no damage to the Hound.

However, at higher Town Hall levels, it is not recommended to place Air Bombs in the range of an Air Defense as Lava Hounds will fly directly towards it, which will trigger the trap and absorb the hit, dealing next to no damage to the Hound.

At lower levels where Balloons have relatively low health, placing two Air Bombs next to each other can easily and swiftly destroy clumps of Balloons, often before the attacker has the chance to react with a Healing Spell (if they have one). You can place your defenses in a way such that you can force enemy Balloons to clump up and then destroy them with the Air Bombs when they are clumped up in such a manner.

At higher levels, Air Bombs will have less of an effect on Balloons but can still have significant effects on Minions , Lava Pups , and Bats (the latter only if another troop triggers the trap first). Nonetheless, multiple Air Bombs can prove problematic to Balloons, especially if a Wizard Tower is nearby and can force the attacker to use a Healing Spell.

Air troops with higher hitpoints, such as Baby Dragons , Dragons , and Electro Dragons , can usually ignore the Air Bomb as its damage is negligible compared to the health of the troop. However, the Lava Hound can be an exception in situational cases; if the Air Bomb explodes just as the Lava Hound splits into Lava Pups , it may wipe out all of the Lava Pups at once before they can do any damage.

At level 9, the Air Bomb's balloons become larger and now are colored crimson, with the exception of the skull. The wooden barrels are colored red with dark gray spikes. The trapdoor's corners are also reinforced. When triggered, a fuse appears to be ignited.

Giant Bomb.name: Giant Bomb
notes: The Giant Bomb is unlocked at Town Hall level 6. Like the Bomb , the Giant Bomb explodes when an enemy comes into proximity. It is essentially a much more powerful (and expensive) version of the Bomb. This deals splash damage to all enemies within a 3 to 4 tile radius, depending on the Giant Bomb's level.
Giant Bombs can do serious damage to moderate-health troops, such as low-level Giants or Hog Riders and usually instantly kill low-health troops such as Barbarians , Archers , Goblins , and Wizards .

A Giant Bomb takes up the same amount of space (2×2) as a Hidden Tesla . If you have multiple places where your Hidden Teslas could spawn, placing Giant Bombs in the others can be an effective strategy. Your enemy may decide that the area is safe once they do not trigger a Hidden Tesla, then spawn additional troops, which will all be blown up by the Giant Bomb.

Be cautious when upgrading the Giant Bomb, as this will reveal its location to future attackers. Combat this by relocating it during the upgrade period. As with any other Trap , Giant Bombs cannot be triggered during an upgrade.

Some players place their Giant Bombs on the outside of their bases, to ensure that troops will trigger them early, helping to prevent 50% destruction. The best place to put outside Giant Bombs is behind external buildings, but in front of external Walls . This ensures that troops will get grouped up while destroying the external building, after which the bomb triggers, destroying many troops at once.

Other players prefer to place the Giant Bomb further into their bases to act as a trap for Hog Rider and Giant groups. Placing them between two Defensive Buildings ensures that the Giants and Hog Riders will be closely grouped before triggering the bomb. This strategy can also be used to counter the Invisibility Spell , Clone Spell , and Super Archers or Super Wizards combo that may come out from Battle Blimp , with the help of other Traps like Bombs.

This strategy can also be used to counter the Invisibility Spell , Clone Spell , and Super Archers or Super Wizards combo that may come out from Battle Blimp , with the help of other Traps like Bombs.

Try to trigger them with a single expendable troop such as a Barbarian (or a Goblin if it is near resource buildings) if you can; drop them one by one near 2×2 spaces in an attempt to trigger them as to prevent further losses in your army.
Use a Healing Spell to heal your remaining troops, especially if you are a lower level using Giant attacking strategy after they trigger a Giant Bomb.
Try using a Hero or a troop with lots of hitpoints such as a P.E.K.K.A or Golem to trigger the Giant Bomb as they will not take much damage compared to their overall health.

Do not use the Barbarian Puppet , Archer Puppet , or Hog Rider Puppet abilities when they trigger a Giant Bomb, as they will blow up the summoned troops. Likewise, it is best to avoid doing the same when approaching a suspicious empty space, lest a Giant Bomb appears.

Seeking Air Mine.name: Seeking Air Mine
notes: The Seeking Air Mine is a single-target air trap . It consists of a spiky metallic bomb attached to three black balloons with white skulls painted onto them.

While the Air Bomb is considered as the aerial counterpart of the Bomb , the Seeking Air Mine is considered the aerial counterpart of the Spring Trap , both dealing huge damage to a single target and has the potential to instantly defeat a troop, though it has a larger trigger radius and lacks a stun.

This trap will target air units with at least 5 housing spaces (including Healers , Siege Machines , Heroes and Pets ). The only air troops with fewer than 5 housing spaces are Minions , Lava Pups (and other Pup variations), Bats , and Boogers , none of which can trigger the Seeking Air Mine, or get affected by it. The Angry Jelly cannot be targeted by the Seeking Air Mine while it is still brainwashing a Hero. Since the Seeking Air Mine can only target a single unit, unlike the Giga Bomb and Spear Trap from Clan Capital , the Seeking Air Mine only counts housing spaces of single troops, rather than summing up.
The Angry Jelly cannot be targeted by the Seeking Air Mine while it is still brainwashing a Hero.

Since the Seeking Air Mine can only target a single unit, unlike the Giga Bomb and Spear Trap from Clan Capital , the Seeking Air Mine only counts housing spaces of single troops, rather than summing up.

The player can place it near the outside of their base to quickly take down any Healers that are deployed. However, more skilled players can deploy Balloons to test for Seeking Air Mines and defuse them. Therefore, it might be more advisable to place them deeper in the base, such as behind a row of defenses.
The same applies to the Minion Prince , although he can tank up to two Seeking Air Mines because of his higher health, given that he is at a higher level.

For the Dragon Duke however, while alone, he can resist Seeking Air Mines, although he can be damaged like normal if nearby aerial units are close enough to him. Even then, because of his extremely high health, it may require multiple Seeking Air Mines to defeat him unless he is already heavily damaged.

If the player has the setting "Automatically use Hero abilities on KO" turned on, the Grand Warden will be able to endure a hit from the Seeking Air Mine regardless of the level provided his ability has not yet been used. If the Seeking Air Mine would defeat him, the Grand Warden will use his ability and survive with barely any health remaining.

It can be used to take down a Battle Blimp that is being used to finish off the Town Hall after a ground or air attack, due to the speed of the Seeking Air Mine being faster. However, this may have adverse effects since the Battle Blimp may spawn the Clan Castle troops in an unfavorable location, such as the P.E.K.K.A right near a Wizard Tower or even the Town Hall itself.

At higher Town Hall levels, Seeking Air Mines can greatly reduce the health of aerial Siege Machines , or even destroy them early. The player can spread out Seeking Air Mines in their base, so that they can cover as many possible Siege Machine directions as possible.

It is usually not recommended to group together multiple Seeking Air Mines since they will all target the same unit, effectively wasting them. However, at Town Hall 9, where Lava Hounds are used often with Balloons, double Seeking Air Mines can be placed near two Air Defenses, to greatly damage Lava Hounds and make them more vulnerable to getting taken out early.

The Balloon is the best choice against this trap, as it occupies only 5 housing space. It gains even more value if too many traps are set off against once since they will all just hit the Balloon for nothing. This is useful in some Single Player maps where a level can contain hundreds of them as a single Balloon will trigger dozens of Seeking Air Mines and waste them all. In the Mashup Mania event, the player could also use the Ice Minion , since it is more housing space-efficient. However, since an update, the Seeking Air Mine requires at least 5 housing space to trigger, which means that the Ice Minion can no longer trigger Seeking Air Mines. [what update?]

When initially constructed, the Seeking Air Mine is a spherical, explosive contact mine made of metal with spikes as triggers and a small red dot at the center, some of which parts are hidden under a trapdoor just like the Air Bomb . Inside the mine, there is an explosive material, most likely trinitrotoluene , and produces red smoke as it flies to the target. Three black balloons with white skulls are attached to the mine via a metal handle. When triggered, the mine leaves a red trail and its red dot blinks repeatedly as it intercepts its target, and explodes with a red vertical cloud will appear once it hits, dealing massive damage.
At level 5, the mine's red dot becomes bigger, and some spikes are replaced in favor of larger ones with metal reinforcements that hold them. When it follows its target, the dot lights up repeatedly.

Skeleton Trap.name: Skeleton Trap
notes: The Skeleton Trap is a trap , which is unlocked at Town Hall 8, that remains hidden until they are activated by an attacking troop moving into their trigger radius. Once triggered, the coffin rises from the ground and multiple Skeletons appear in the area around the coffin to attack nearby troops depending on whether it is set for ground or air troops.
They can be configured to attack either ground troops or air troops, but not both at once. They will remain invisible if set to ground and an air troop passes over (or vice versa).

The Skeletons released have a small skull icon next to them to signify they came from a Skeleton Trap (as opposed to being summoned by a Witch ), similar to the icon displayed next to Clan Castle troops. The reason behind this is that they play an equal role to the Skeletons summoned by a defending Witch in the Clan Castle.

The Skeleton Traps set to defend against air troops have wings instead of a skull on the face of the coffin. Skeletons that arise from being triggered while set to defend against air troops float through the air with the aid of two small red balloons, the same balloons as those on the Air Bomb . If they do not notice any more air troops, they will become idle, but they can still be taken down by any troop that attacks air.

The Skeleton Traps make valuable distractions. Upgrading them would be a good idea, as single-target units would have a hard time taking them down. You can place them near buildings you wish to protect to distract most troops that wish to attack that building, allowing your defenses time to destroy the attacking troops.

They are useful in distracting Heroes and P.E.K.K.As , especially when either are near the Town Hall . They are even better against troops who target defenses, such as Giants and Hog Riders , because they do not stop to attack the Skeletons, in which they slowly get taken out while destroying the defenses. This is the same with any other troop who target a certain building . However, they do not work against Golems , because of their death damage, and the Electro Titan , since her aura will instantly take them out.
However, they do not work against Golems , because of their death damage, and the Electro Titan , since her aura will instantly take them out.

The Skeleton Trap is also particularly effective against Miners , because they will have to burrow and resurface every time they kill a Skeleton (which significantly slows them down compared to other troops).

You can place Skeleton Traps near a Bomb Tower to stall troops there when it explodes. However, this generally does not work for troops that target defensive buildings, such as the Giant or Hog Rider, since they will ignore the Skeletons unless the Bomb Tower is the last defense standing.
In air mode, place the Skeleton Trap near Air Defenses to distract Dragons from targeting them.

The Skeleton Trap's Skeletons can attack defense-targeting troops without retaliation, so when you make a base, try to separate the support unit from the tanks in order to prevent such support units from destroying the Skeletons.

Single Skeleton Traps should only pose a threat if they are distracting slow-attacking troops such as P.E.K.K.As , Miners and Electro Dragons , if your troops have no means of fighting back (such as when using Giants or Hog Riders in groups), or if they prevent troops from attacking a particularly valuable target (such as the Town Hall ). They can be largely ignored otherwise, though Spells may need to be used to keep your troops alive from defensive fire during this time of distraction (e.g., a Freeze Spell against a single-target Inferno Tower ).

Area splash is effective against Skeleton Traps, especially when multiple are placed in close proximity. Valkyries , their Super Form , and Electro Titans are particularly effective at killing the spawned Skeletons, as they are able to take out Skeletons coming from all directions. Other sources of splash damage, such as Wizards , Baby Dragons , Witches , and Bowlers can work best if the Skeletons are first clumped up together.

Some Spells may be used as a substitute for the aforementioned splash damage. Poison Spells , as the most effective against typical Clan Castle troops, can be used to create a kill zone for enemy Skeletons in which they are unable to survive for long; however, Lightning Spells are more effective as they can kill the Skeletons instantly. In the case of Lightning Spells, they must be placed in the correct location so that all the Skeletons will be wiped out, otherwise some of them will survive, which could otherwise mess up your attack. The Electro Boots can easily counter Skeletons spawned from Skeleton Traps, since the aura will instantly destroy them, even if they have newly spawned.
The Electro Boots can easily counter Skeletons spawned from Skeleton Traps, since the aura will instantly destroy them, even if they have newly spawned.

Tornado Trap.name: Tornado Trap
notes: The Tornado Trap is a trap unlocked at Town Hall level 11. When triggered, it pulls in attacking troops, forcibly moving them, and does small damage to them.

The Tornado Trap also deals a small amount of damage per second to all units within its radius (including the aforementioned units unaffected by the Tornado Trap's displacement effect). As the trap lasts longer at higher levels, it deals more damage overall at higher levels.
The Tornado Trap will not prevent units from attacking if they can attack targets still in range.

You can use the Tornado Trap to pull in ranged units and make them lose their range advantage. While they may still be able to attack while trapped in the tornado, you can take advantage of this by placing high-damage buildings to quickly destroy them, you can also place other traps near the Tornado Trap to trigger them on grouped up enemies.
Placing the Tornado Trap in front of Walls that Wall Breakers would target can prevent them from attacking said Walls, which can disrupt plans of the attacker.

Placing a Tornado Trap near the Giga Tesla or Giga Inferno can stall attacking reinforcements deployed near them by a Wall Wrecker or Battle Blimp . The strategy is particularly useful if the reinforcement consists of Balloons , who need to be on top of the Town Hall to do damage to it. However, in some cases, this does not work, as for example, if the Balloons get cloned by a Clone Spell or two to get out of the radius of the Tornado Trap.
However, in some cases, this does not work, as for example, if the Balloons get cloned by a Clone Spell or two to get out of the radius of the Tornado Trap.

Certain sub-troops like Skeletons from Skeleton Spells and Witches, and Bats from Bat Spells will not trigger Tornado Traps, while others can. Skeletons and Bats are weak to Tornado Traps, but will not trigger them. Tornado Traps will only activate if a troop walks into its radius, and any Bats or Skeletons that enter the radius will be severely damaged if not destroy them.

Skeletons and Bats are weak to Tornado Traps, but will not trigger them. Tornado Traps will only activate if a troop walks into its radius, and any Bats or Skeletons that enter the radius will be severely damaged if not destroy them.

If ground troops are pulled into a Wall by a Tornado Trap, they will get stuck on the Wall and be unable to move until the trap's effect ends, even if they are able to bypass Walls innately. This can be used in many different ways, such as trapping units to be hit by splash defenses, or stalling Heroes from attacking.

Tornado Traps can waste most of the Hero ability duration, for example the Royal Champion under the effects of her activated Haste Vial can be stuck on a wall, preventing her from getting the full value.

Use some low health troops like Barbarian , Archer , Goblin , Minion , or Wall Breaker to trigger the Tornado Trap so that the Army at the back can push without the Tornado Trap interrupting and wiping them out.

When initially constructed, the Tornado Trap appears as a metallic spiral tube rotated clockwise that is covered by a wooden hatch on the ground. When activated, the hatch opens, the trap reveals itself and pulls units in its radius in a counter-clockwise motion.

Giga Bomb.name: Giga Bomb
notes: The Giga Bomb is a trap that is unlocked at Town Hall 17. It is separated from the Town Hall 16 Giga Inferno when it had merged into Inferno Artillery which no longer has a death bomb. The explosion damage and radius remains the same but it loses the poison damage and slowing effect on movement and attack speed, but in return, it gains a powerful knockback effect that affects most troops.

Unlike other traps, it is visible to attackers and needs a total amount of housing space (18) within its trigger radius (3.5 tiles) to be triggered. Troops that cannot trigger traps, such as Skeletons and Bats , do not add any housing spaces when determining whether the Giga Bomb is to be triggered.
Troops that cannot trigger traps, such as Skeletons and Bats , do not add any housing spaces when determining whether the Giga Bomb is to be triggered.
Damaging spells like Lightning Spells and the Earthquake Spells cannot trigger this trap, and neither the Freeze Spell nor Overgrowth Spell will prevent the explosion from happening.

Once triggered, it causes a massive explosion which heavily damages all units in its explosion radius. The resulting explosion knocks back or even flings up enemy units. Units like Dragons , Electro Dragons , Heroes , and those with enough hitpoints such as Root Riders and Golems are affected by its knockback. Its area damage can affect both ground and air units at the same time, just like the fully upgraded Giga Tesla's death bomb, in addition to forcing troops to retarget.
If you want to avoid triggering this trap, deploy a few small units such as Barbarians, Archers or Minions to snipe off buildings.

Otherwise, you can trigger it using a unit with 18 or more housing space with or troops that count to a total of 18 housing space, such as the Yeti , to waste the Giga Bomb. However, be wary of any traps and defenses nearby the trigger radius.

Miners , and/or their Super version can avoid triggering the Giga Bomb, unless if they surface too early, and in which case if they do survive, they get knocked back upwards. The same principle applies to Diggy and the Battle Drill .

Pairing the Giga Bomb with the Tornado Trap will make both traps more effective, similar to placing the Tornado Trap near the Town Hall weapon for more troops to be affected by the death bomb. However, just like before, the Town Hall and Giga Bomb being visible to raiders means it telegraphs where the Tornado Trap usually is and the damage can be mitigated with the Eternal Tome, leaving only the secondary effects like poison damage and slow down or knockback to be effective.

If the Giga Bomb is properly placed in a base layout, it can displace ground units into adjacent compartments which can get them stuck for a long time, unless if they have high damage to Walls to shorten the amount of time required to destroy them like Root Riders , or if they can jump over Walls like Hog Riders , Headhunters , and the Royal Champion .

Placing the Giga Bomb on the outside can be a waste, especially if a unit such as Dragon triggers it, the explosion will only damage the Dragon, and not the main army. Thus, it is best used inside the base where the army is most likely to enter from the base, where it will damage the main army if the attacker is not careful, increasing the chances of a successful defense.

The Hook Tower can grab units towards its blind spot, allowing the Giga Bomb to explode and severely damage them, if not wiping it out. However, the unit targeted must be at least 18 housing space, else it will not activate. Therefore, an attacker's Hero can prove to be a great target for the Hook Tower, allowing other defenses and traps to defeat them.

However, the unit targeted must be at least 18 housing space, else it will not activate. Therefore, an attacker's Hero can prove to be a great target for the Hook Tower, allowing other defenses and traps to defeat them.

When initially constructed, the Giga Bomb is a giant, tall vermilion stick of dynamite with a fuse and a skull symbol leaning to the right side. It is placed in a hole of the ground with a iron foundation, surrounded by a raised edge and and arrow-shaped pieces on all four corners, riveted on the sides. When triggered, the fuse ignites, and the dynamite itself flashes twice in a white tint. Once the fuse is fully charred, it lights up once more and causes an orange skull-like explosion, leaving a crater with a skull behind that lasts for a few seconds.

Longshot.name: Longshot
notes: When tapping her, she faces the player and punches her fists together three times, with the first two releasing some blue energy, and the last one generating a small blue shockwave. If she was on the Town Hall, she will then jump down to the bottom right side of the Town Hall.

When the Town Hall is destroyed while she is still standing, the Longshot will forcefully jump down immediately if no attacking troops enter her trigger range beforehand. This is common on attacks where maxed-level Fireballs with triple Earthquake Spells are used to destroy the Town Hall, paired with the Giant Arrow .

The Longshot has a very long range, allowing her to outrange every attacking unit in the game. One of the strategies used is to place the Town Hall at the core, especially paired with Invisibility and Rage Spell Towers , so that when the main army enters the base, she will be in action.

Since the Longshot deals splash damage, she can take out swarms easily, but her attack speed is too slow, which she would be overwhelmed by them. Protect her with splash defenses to keep them at bay. However, her death damage can also take them out, and damage higher-hitpoint units, including Heroes like the Grand Warden . In addition, the Longshot can even snipe the Royal Champion in a Champion Charge, as her arrow deals damage to both her and the Spirit Fox , dealing heavy damage to if not defeat either or both of them.
However, her death damage can also take them out, and damage higher-hitpoint units, including Heroes like the Grand Warden .

The Longshot has a slow attack speed, but she can defeat swarms with ease because of her high splash damage. Overwhelming her with medium to high-hitpoint units can defeat her, but the damage when destroyed may take them out, especially when there are traps like the Giga Bomb and Spring Traps , unless if the attacker uses the Grand Warden 's ability beforehand.

To prevent her from wreaking havoc from afar, the attacker can either use a Totem Spell to redirect her attacks away from the army, a Freeze Spell to stop her from attacking, an Invisibility Spell to protect units from being damaged. Avoid using Headhunters however, as they will not target her, unless if there are no more Heroes remaining in the base. Poison Spell can be used, albeit less effective as it will decrease her attack speed and movement speed by 30% of their usual effects.

Avoid using Flame Flingers to target an area of the base where the Longshot can attack from her attack radius, else they will be severely damaged, or even get destroyed prematurely, unless if it is tanked by a high-hitpoint unit like a Totem from the Totem Spell.

Do not use the Totem Spell while she is jumping over a wall, otherwise she will still lock onto her current target if it had not taken out already, especially important units like the Grand Warden in Warden Charges.

Smasher.name: Smasher
notes: When tapped, the Smasher twirls his club from his right hand, puts it down and bumps his left fist twice onto his armor. If he was already on top of the Town Hall, he will also jump down from the bottom right side of the Town Hall.

He has a violent temper and is fiercely protective of the Town Hall, and will become enraged, boosting his damage and movement speed by 60% if the Town Hall is destroyed. This enraged status persists until he is defeated.

Upon death, the Smasher falls backwards to the ground and a burst of purple energy from the cracks is released, creating a defensive Rage Spell which buffs defensive buildings and units identically to Rage Spells from the Spell Tower . He will drop this Rage Spell regardless of whether he had enraged previously.

The Smasher is one of the most durable of the Guardians currently in the game, and his health and damage per hit exceeds that of the Barbarian King , while the damage is more than that of the Archer Queen when it comes to damage per second. However, his main drawback is his very slow attack speed, which can overwhelm him, especially when dealing with medium-hitpoint units like Valkyries , but is compensated for his wide damage radius, similar to the Giant Gauntlet , just slower but permanent.

However, his main drawback is his very slow attack speed, which can overwhelm him, especially when dealing with medium-hitpoint units like Valkyries , but is compensated for his wide damage radius, similar to the Giant Gauntlet , just slower but permanent.

When placed near the outside of the base, protected by a compartment of Walls , he can prove to be effective against armies and at the backend, can be very tough to deal with. Pair this up with sufficiently-spaced defenses and the correct Clan Castle troops like Ice Golems and the Smasher will wipe out attacking units in seconds.

The Smasher can easily deal with swarms due to his massive damage, but his attack is slow that eventually he would get taken out. To prevent this, place splash-damaging or multi-targeting defenses like Scattershots and Bomb Towers to counter them. Traps and defending Heroes can also work in this regard.
The Smasher can outrange Flame Flingers, even if he is not considered a defense, as he will approach the Siege Machine and destroy it prematurely.

To prevent the Smasher from wreaking havoc to the player's army, the attacker can either use a Totem Spell to redirect his attacks away from the army, a Freeze Spell to stop him from attacking, an Invisibility Spell to protect units from being damaged, or an Ice Block Spell to tank for other units. Avoid using Poison Spells or Headhunters however, as the former will be ineffective and the latter will not target him, unless if there are no more Heroes remaining in the base.
Avoid using Poison Spells or Headhunters however, as the former will be ineffective and the latter will not target him, unless if there are no more Heroes remaining in the base.

Logger.name: Logger
notes: The Logger is a male royal blue anthropomorphic entity with glowing blue eyes and four pastel blue patches on each of his arms, and has a golden wristband on each of his wrists. Unlike the Longshot and the Smasher , he wears a stone brick armor in a running bond pattern. He also has burnt orange wooden eyebrows, beard and a mohawk, which holds brown wooden planks to make it look like a roof-shaped hat. He holds a very large log with two metal rings on each end and numerous spikes. Because to his large size, he can attack both ground and air units.

When tapped, the Logger throws his log in the air before catching it using one of his hands then juggling it into another, after which he lifts the log using both hands in the air. If he was already on top of the Town Hall, he will also jump down from the bottom right side of the Town Hall.

The Logger attacks by throwing a log at the closest target, damaging and knocking back all units, ground and air at the same time by one tile. After this, he gathers a log from inside his hat, and the cycle repeats until he is defeated or no units are in range.

The Logger is a formidable Guardian to deal with, with higher hitpoints than the Longshot but less than the Smasher, and has the least damage and range of all the Guardians in the game, although the projectile lasts much longer. His main drawback is his very slow attack speed, which can overwhelm him, especially when dealing with medium-hitpoint units like Valkyries or Hog Riders , but is compensated for his wide damage radius, knockback and maximum range of his Logs while also damaging both ground and air at the same time, making him much more dangerous when units are very close to him, similar to the Log Trap , rolling from 7 tiles initially to 8 tiles at max level.

His main drawback is his very slow attack speed, which can overwhelm him, especially when dealing with medium-hitpoint units like Valkyries or Hog Riders , but is compensated for his wide damage radius, knockback and maximum range of his Logs while also damaging both ground and air at the same time, making him much more dangerous when units are very close to him, similar to the Log Trap , rolling from 7 tiles initially to 8 tiles at max level.

To prevent the Logger from wreaking havoc to the player's army, the attacker can either use a Totem Spell to redirect his attacks away from the army, a Freeze Spell to stop him from attacking, an Invisibility Spell to protect units from being damaged, or an Ice Block Spell to tank for other units, especially when protecting Healers from being taken out by his Logs. Avoid using Poison Spells or Headhunters however, as the former will be not be as effective and the latter will not target him, unless if there are no more Heroes remaining in the base. The Logger's logs can still hit targets behind the initial target, especially Healers, even when invisible, so be careful.
Avoid using Poison Spells or Headhunters however, as the former will be not be as effective and the latter will not target him, unless if there are no more Heroes remaining in the base.
The Logger's logs can still hit targets behind the initial target, especially Healers, even when invisible, so be careful.
Guardians like the Logger are immune to Poison Spells only when they are on top of the Town Hall and are not yet triggered.

Army Camp.name: Army Camp
notes: You should not surround your Army Camps with Walls , as they do not need protection. Army Camps also occupy a lot of space (4x4). More Walls are needed to contain them when the extra Walls can be used to surround Defensive Buildings that are already inside the Walls, strengthening the defense.
At level 11, the fire pit becomes larger and the edges become more "flat". The sides have metal support, the corners gain golden chains, and the corners are no longer diagonal shaped pieces.

At level 12, the fire pit becomes slightly smaller and is darker in color. The corner chains are replaced with flames. The base gains another layer, and the steps on the sides of the Army Camp are now triangular.

Town Hall.name: Town Hall
notes: "This is the heart of your village . Upgrading the Town Hall unlocks new defenses , buildings , traps and much more. Destroying an opponent's Town Hall earns you one star in battle. Protect your Town Hall from attacks by placing it in the middle of your village and surrounding it with walls, traps, and defenses."

The Town Hall also serves as a resource storage of Gold, Elixir, and Dark Elixir (the latter only when the Town Hall is level 7 or above). Unlike other resource storages, the loot stored in the Town Hall can only be looted if it is destroyed. As a resource storage, it is immune to damage from Lightning Spells , but not from Earthquake Spells , unlike other storages.
As a resource storage, it is immune to damage from Lightning Spells , but not from Earthquake Spells , unlike other storages.

When upgraded to level 12 through 17, the Town Hall becomes weaponized, and gains the ability to defend itself, doubling as a potent defensive building capable of dealing high damage to multiple targets at once and quickly. At Town Hall 18, the Town Hall's weapon is removed in favor of defending them with Guardians .

Since the change that players no longer gain a shield if the opponent destroyed their Town Hall, placing it outside a farming base serves no purpose anymore, other than to rapidly drop trophies . Players should aim to protect their Town Hall at all costs, as it contains 20% of all 3 different resources.

Town Halls have the highest hitpoints of any relative level building, with the exception of Walls , which means they take a long time to destroy. Placing your Town Hall within the range of your most powerful defenses can give them the most shots to destroy enemy troops.

If maximizing builder time is a priority, as it is inefficient to wait until all of the building upgrades are finished before beginning to upgrade the Town Hall, as all but one of the builders will be idle for the duration of your Town Hall upgrade. In order to keep all builders occupied (but ensure they are all available when the Town Hall upgrade finishes), plan for the Town Hall upgrade to finish just as the remaining builders are finishing their final projects. For example, if you are currently at Town Hall level 9 and have five builders, you should upgrade your Town Hall (which takes 2 days and 12 hours) when the total remaining upgrading time of other buildings approaches 10 days.
Do not place the Town Hall in a corner surrounded by Walls, as troops can still be placed next to the Town Hall in the darker grass.
Unlocked at Town Hall 12, the Giga Tesla is an addition to the Town Hall that allows it to defend itself when attacked. It can target multiple enemies and explode with high damage when destroyed.

Unlocked at Town Hall 13, the Giga Inferno is a direct upgrade that replaces the Giga Tesla with a continuously-firing Inferno Tower while adding a slowdown effect to the death bomb. The Giga Inferno remains as the weapon of Town Halls 14 through 16 but with a different appearance. At Town Hall 14, the death bomb's slowdown effect is replaced with a poison effect, doing damage over time on top of the slowdown. Town Halls 15 and 16 improve the Giga Inferno's hitpoints, damage per second, and potency of the death bomb.

The Giga Weapons will be activated once damaged by a troop or spell, or when the village has reached 51% destruction. It is not deployed by a troop moving into its range.
Troops that target defenses ( Giants , Balloons , Hog Riders etc.) will not prioritize the Town Hall as a target until the Giga Weapons are activated.

Instead of damaging multiple targets continuously, it now deals splash damage by shooting fireballs that create fiery pools on impact with the ground, which damages all enemies that stay within these areas. This allows the Inferno Artillery to affect more than four enemies it directly targets. It automatically triggers at the start of the battle unlike previous Town Hall weapons.
Unlike previous levels, the Inferno Artillery does not have a death bomb, which separated from the Town Hall as a Giga Bomb that knocks back troops.
