When being rotated, the entire furnace changes to the direction, indicated by the claws. The Firespitter aims by turning its head alone the groove of the furnace, and attacks by firing a maximum of twenty molten balls which pierce through units, ground and air alike. These molten balls spread by a small angle, which means that the Firespitter is more accurate when troops are close to it and may damage troops behind its original target.

*These damage per second values are seen in-game and are approximations; it does not necessarily do this much DPS if it cannot utilize the full potential of its bursts. **In-game, damage per hit values display with decimals truncated.

Crafting Station.name: Crafting Station
notes: The Crafting Station is a defensive building unlocked at the highest Town Hall level (currently level 18), which can be toggled between three different modes, each with their advantages and disadvantages. It is free and covers a 3x3 area of the base. Even if the Crafting Station has not chosen its defense yet, it is still treated as a "defensive building". This means that defense-targeting units like Giants , Balloons , and Golems can attack it as their priority, and it can also soak up Seeking Shields and Fireballs . Once the Crafting Station's crafted defense has been selected, it can no longer be switched back to its non-damaging building form.

Even if the Crafting Station has not chosen its defense yet, it is still treated as a "defensive building". This means that defense-targeting units like Giants , Balloons , and Golems can attack it as their priority, and it can also soak up Seeking Shields and Fireballs .

The following defenses are the currently available Crafted Defenses: The Hot Candle flings flame spurts at surrounding units and splits its attacks among nearby units similiar to Multi-Archer Tower , however its number of targets drops as it melts over time. The Hero Hunter targets all ground and air units with a range of 9.5 tiles while effecting them down with a Poison Spell effect, it deals extra damage against Heroes. The Cake-A-Pult launches destructive cakes at ground and air units within a range of 3-12 tiles, it leaves a explosive surprise behind after dropping.
The Hot Candle flings flame spurts at surrounding units and splits its attacks among nearby units similiar to Multi-Archer Tower , however its number of targets drops as it melts over time.
The Hero Hunter targets all ground and air units with a range of 9.5 tiles while effecting them down with a Poison Spell effect, it deals extra damage against Heroes.
The Cake-A-Pult launches destructive cakes at ground and air units within a range of 3-12 tiles, it leaves a explosive surprise behind after dropping.
The Hook Tower grabs a unit into its blind spot with a range of 4-15 tiles, ground or air, but does not deal any damage and stuns them temporarily.
The Flame Spinner is always active and deals area damage, with a range of 8 tiles. When attacking, it attacks in a spiral motion, releasing a large number of fireballs.

The Crusher Mortar can deal heavy damage to ground units with splash damage with a range of 2.5-9 tiles. When attacking, it launches spiky, heavy stones rapidly at the opponent, and each bounces up to two times before disintegrating, similar to a Super Bowler .
The Light Beam is a single-target defense with very long range, however its shots diminish in power the further away its target is.
The Roaster fires bursts of plasma, dealing rapid splash damage against ground and air troops at medium range.
The Air Bombs launches aerial bomb balloons, dealing high splash damage against air units.
The Lava Launcher launches fiery projectiles at long range, dealing high splash damage against ground units. The projectiles leave lava pools on impact, further damaging ground units that enter them.

Super Wizard Tower.name: Super Wizard Tower

raw.Damage Type: Single Target (Chain Lightning; up to 15 other targets)

attrs.attack_type: Single Target (Chain Lightning; up to 15 other targets)

notes: The Wizard Tower received Supercharges at level 17, which would have made the difference smaller, but the bonus stats are dissipated when the Super Wizard Tower is introduced, so they cannot be directly compared as only normal Wizard Tower can merged. When compared to two Supercharged Wizard Towers, the Super Wizard Tower starts off with 11.1% less health but each bolt deals 27.2% more damage than the two combined.

With this ability, the range of the Super Wizard Tower can be up to 12 tiles situationally. Despite the cap on the chain lightning targets, its radius is much larger than the 1 tile splash radius of the Wizard Tower and likely can hit more troops, while each chain lightning deals 5.5% more damage than an arcane bolt from a Wizard Tower (or 1.75% more from a Supercharged Wizard Tower).

The Super Wizard Tower is a formidable defense when it comes to swarm-based attacks, but since it has lost the splash damage from its unmerged version, theoretically the Super Wizard Tower is vulnerable by overswarming. In reality, it is unlikely that there are more than 16 troops stacking within the 1 tile splash radius of the Wizard Tower; with the 4 tile chain radius, it can likely damage more enemies at once and be more effective at clearing swarms, while still being more effective at high hitpoint target because of the extra range and damage.

The Super Wizard Tower can easily damage high-hitpoint units like Dragons and Electro Dragons and can chain to supporting enemy units, eventually leading to being taken out by other defenses, combined with its attack speed that allows it to handle groups of units effectively.

Super Wizard Towers are powerful merged defenses with high damage that can heavily damage swarms in mere seconds, chaining up to 15 targets and eventually taking them out by itself or supported by other defenses. To prevent it from wreaking havoc, use Freeze Spells and Overgrowth Spells to disable this defense, Invisibility Spells to turn attacking units invisible, or Totem Spells to redirect the attacks to the summoned Totem.
If the attacker is not careful, any unit in front of the Flame Flinger within its range can damage the Siege Machine in certain cases.

At level 2, the floating crystal becomes darker and has a proper floor with a small platform in the middle and walls on the edge, connected at the corners. It also gains beige stone battlements all around the crystal walls, with golden plates at the corners that has a gold spike on top.

Lava Pup.name: Lava Pup
notes: Lava Pups are fast, weak air troops. They are spawned in a circular spread when the Lava Hound has been defeated.

Lava Pups have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Lava Pups will proceed to attack the nearest structure.
Like the Minion, it cannot trigger Seeking Air Mines , but can trigger Air Bombs .

A group of Lava Pups can be easily wiped out by a single Air Bomb or other AOE/Multi-Target defenses , but can easily distract the Air Defense for some time. Try using more durable aerial units to distract them and buy valuable seconds. If they are adequately protected, they can even help to finish off buildings in the corners in a similar fashion to Minions .
Lava Pups can easily stall single-target defenses. Consider using one with Balloons , Dragons , or Electro Dragons to help with these slower units.

The Lava Hound can be placed inside the Clan Castle, but Lava Pups cannot. Nonetheless, when a Lava Hound explodes, the Lava Pups are able to overwhelm enemies with their large numbers. This makes them useful to stall slower troops like Electro Dragons and the Royal Champion , but they are weaker if multiple troops engage them at the same time.
If the Lava Hound dies while being burned by the Inferno Artillery 's fire pools, then the Lava Pups that spawn on it will quickly get taken out as well.

Golemite.name: Golemite
notes: Golemites are basically a smaller and less powerful version of the Golem . A Golemite has one-fifth of the Golem's damage per second, damage upon death, and hitpoints.
Both Golems and Golemites do splash damage when destroyed.
At level 5, the Golemite gains purple, crystal-like spikes on his back, similar to those on the level 7 Wall . His entire body also gains a grayish purple color.
At level 13, the Golemite's purple spikes turn dark red, while his white ones now give off an orange glow. His body changes to a red wine while his eyes become yellow.
At level 14, the Golemite's red spikes turn gunmetal, while the glowing orange ones become golden yellow. His body color changes into deep cobalt and his eyes are slightly dimmer.

Yetimite.name: Yetimite

raw.Attack Type: Area Splash (0.8 Tile Radius; Air & Ground)

attrs.attack_type: Area Splash (0.8 Tile Radius; Air & Ground)

notes: Yetimites are small creatures spawned by the Yeti . They attack by approaching a target building before jumping into it after a brief pause. This jump attack makes it invulnerable and untargetable, can hit ground and air target, deals a small amount of damage and destroys the Yetimite on impact.
Yetimites spawn as the Yeti takes damage (specifically each time the Yeti takes 600 damage). When the Yeti is destroyed, he releases any remaining Yetimites he has.

Yetimites can jump over Walls and do four times the damage to Defenses , but half to Resource Buildings . In particular, these factors both apply to Town Hall at level 12 and above if its weapon is active, because it is classed as both a defense and a resource storage, dealing double damage to it.
Yetimites can be useful for distracting single-targeting defenses, as they have relatively high health and can deal good damage.
While the Yeti that spawns them is still alive, the Yeti will serve as a good tank for the Yetimites to deal damage underneath.

Yetimites are hard to stop largely due to the fact that they have a good amount of hitpoints and generally will not have to travel far to reach a defense it can damage; oftentimes they will spawn right in front of a defense, and damage is almost unavoidable in that scenario. To combat this, it is best to make sure Yetis cannot reach your defenses easily so that the Yetimites will have to travel for longer to reach your defenses.

High-damage defenses focused on Yetimites will be able to destroy them in time, but often these same defenses will be distracted by the Yetis that spawn them. Multi-targeting defenses, such as Inferno Towers , Giga Tesla , Giga Inferno , or Multi-Archer Tower are a great counter to Yetimites. Scattershots and raged up Ricochet Cannons are also able to one-shot the Yetimite if it manages a direct hit.
At level 7, the Yetimites are now prussian, and their eyes are glowing orange.

Electromite.name: Electromite
notes: Electromites are small creatures spawned by the Super Yeti . They attack by approaching a target building before turning into a burst of lightning after a brief pause. It can hit ground and air targets, deals a small amount of damage, dissipating the Electromite in the process. The subsequent chain lightning hits up to three targets, with each successive chain doing 20% less damage than the previous one.
Electromites spawn as Super Yeti takes damage (specifically each time the Super Yeti takes 400 damage).
Electromites can jump over Walls and do four times the damage to Buildings (including resource buildings and the Town Hall , which standard Yetimites have a lesser multiplier against).

Electromites prioritize buildings above all other targets, and will bypass defending troops and Heroes while any buildings remain on the battlefield, even if they are being attacked by these units. If there are no targetable buildings (which is possible if the only remaining buildings are covered by Invisibility Spells or Overgrowth Spells ), Electromites become like any other troop with no preferred target; they will attack the nearest target to them regardless of type. However, if buildings become targetable again when Electromites are targeting troops, they will not switch targets back to buildings unless their original target is destroyed.
Electromites can be useful for distracting single-targeting defenses, as they have relatively high health and can deal good damage.

Because of the high damage multiplier and chaining its damage up to three buildings, Electromites can output a crazy amount of damage against them, especially if buffed by a Rage Spell . A weaker version of that uses the Rage Gem, but is always active while the Grand Warden is in the battlefield.
While Super Yeti that spawns them is still alive, he will serve as a good tank for the Electromites to deal damage underneath.

Electromites are hard to stop largely due to the fact that they have a good amount of hitpoints and generally will not have to travel far to reach a building it can damage; oftentimes they will spawn right in front of a building, and damage is almost unavoidable in that scenario. To combat this, it is best to make sure Super Yetis cannot reach your core defenses easily so that the Electromites will have to travel for longer to reach them.

High damage defenses focused on Electromites will be able to destroy them in time, but often these same defenses will be distracted by the Super Yetis that spawn them. Multi-targeting defenses, such as Inferno Towers , Giga Tesla , Giga Inferno , Multi-Archer Tower , or Firespitters are a great counter to Electromites. Scattershots , raged up Ricochet Cannons , and/or the Fast Attack Multi-Gear Tower are also able to one-shot the Electromite if it manages a direct hit.

Tornado Traps can be a viable option, because it can catch multiple Electromites, allowing defenses to quickly take them out, protecting major defenses, unless if they are too close to them or when Clone Spells and/or Totem Spells are involved. Poison Spell Towers can also work in this regard, but slowing them down instead of stalling them.

Big Boy.name: Big Boy
notes: The Big Boy is a giant Skeleton spawned by a Super Witch . He has very high damage and hitpoints.
Compared to regular Skeletons , the Big Boy is much less vulnerable to splash damage but is more susceptible to single target damage instead.

Big Boys have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Big Boys will proceed to attack the nearest structure.

The Big Boy is quite similar to a P.E.K.K.A : both have high health, high damage, slow attack speed, and can only attack ground. His stats are comparable to level 3-4 P.E.K.K.As; he is generally much weaker than a high-level P.E.K.K.A, but will be backed up by the Super Witch.

Compared to ordinary Skeletons , Big Boys are much better at taking fire from splash and multi-target defenses that would otherwise counter ordinary Witches , such as Wizard Towers and multi-target Inferno Towers .

Big Boys tend to fare poorly against swarms, due to their slow attack speed, which makes them poor against defending Clan Castle troops (if present in large numbers) and Skeleton Traps . They may be assisted by Super Witches in this regard as the latter deals splash damage, though this is generally not reliable as the two may target different things. Consider supporting them with fast-attacking units like the Archer Queen and Dragon Rider or splash-attacking units like Wizards , Baby Dragons , and Valkyries .

Ruin Knight.name: Ruin Knight
notes: The Ruin Knight is a unit summoned by the Ruin Witch when she clears rubble from destroyed buildings. It is a single-target melee troop with moderately high damage and hitpoints.

Ruin Knights have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Ruin Knights will proceed to attack the nearest structure.

Firemite.name: Firemite

raw.Attack Type: Area Splash (0.8 Tile Radius; Ground & Air)

attrs.attack_type: Area Splash (0.8 Tile Radius; Ground & Air)

notes: Firemites are small creatures spawned by the Furnace every few seconds. They attack by approaching a target Building before jumping into it after a brief pause. This jump attack makes them invulnerable and untargetable, can hit ground and air target, deals a small amount of damage and upon impact, leaves a burning pool that damages them over time, burning itself upon the process.
Just like the Yetimites and Frostmites , Firemites can jump over Walls .

Furnaces have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Furnaces will proceed to attack the nearest structure.

Bear.name: Bear
notes: The Bear is a sub-troop that is a transformation of a Druid. This transformation occurs when the Druid has remained in his human form for 25 seconds or after the Druid's health bar is depleted. The Bear cannot be trained directly.
The Bear is a defense-targeting troop with moderate damage and somewhat high hitpoints. Unlike the Druid, he cannot bypass Walls .

Bears are weak to Spring Trap , so you may need to place small troops to waste them, or use ground troops with a spring weight higher than 18 or a Hero to trigger them in order to prevent the Bears from being bounced off the village .

Bears are vulnerable to single-targeting defenses such as Ricochet Cannons , Monoliths , and single-targeting Inferno Towers . You can either use a Freeze Spell , which stops them from firing, an Invisibility Spell , which turns your Bears invisible, or use the Overgrowth Spell to disable the defenses completely, so that they will attack that part of the base later.
Walls at higher levels are a very effective way to defend against Bears, as due to their massive hitpoints, the Bears will have a hard time destroying them.

Ice Pup.name: Ice Pup
notes: Ice Pups are spawned when an Ice Hound dies in battle. Although they vaguely resemble their parent, the Ice Hound, in appearance, they are significantly stronger offensively but have only have a minuscule fraction of the Ice Hound's health.
They are similar to Lava Pups , except they are able to slow down targets they hit just like the Ice Hound does - affected targets will have reduced movement and attack speed.
Even though less Ice Pups spawn from the Ice Hound than Lava Pups spawn from a Lava Hound of equal level, they are generally more effective due to their freezing effect.

Ice Pups have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Ice Pups will proceed to attack the nearest structure.
It cannot trigger Seeking Air Mines , but can trigger Air Bombs .
During the freeze of the death of Ice Hound, the Ice Pups can help clear surrounding defenses. This freeze enables them to stand more of a chance against the immediate surroundings.

It is advisable to distract the nearby defenses with other units, such as Balloons , so that Ice Pups will be able to survive longer and possibly slow down the attack speeds of nearby defenses as well (which synergizes with the rest of the attack).

Keep crowd control defenses like the X-Bow , Multi-Archer Tower , and Multi-Target Inferno Tower away from Air Defenses , so that they are less likely to be frozen when an Ice Hound dies and the Ice Pups get released; they will be able to quickly make short work of them.

Air Bombs are as effective of a threat to Ice Pups as they are with Lava Pups. Try to place them in locations such that the Ice Hound will not trigger them, but the Ice Pups do when they are scattered out from the Ice Hound.

Meteormite.name: Meteormite
notes: The Meteormite is a ground troop that deal melee damage. They move a bit faster than Meteor Golem but attack slower. However, when not attacking, they can combine with another nearby Meteormite to form a Meteor Golem. To this end, Meteormites can jump over Walls to reach Meteormites thrown ahead. When combining, the resulting Meteor Golem's health will equal the sum of the health of its constituent Meteormites, rounded down to 0.5% of the Meteor Golem's hitpoints (to a minimum of 1 hitpoints). The Meteor Golem is briefly invincible after being formed.

When combining, the resulting Meteor Golem's health will equal the sum of the health of its constituent Meteormites, rounded down to 0.5% of the Meteor Golem's hitpoints (to a minimum of 1 hitpoints). The Meteor Golem is briefly invincible after being formed.

Meteormites have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Meteormites will proceed to attack the nearest structure.

Meteormites are very powerful units in attacking, especially with the ability to jump over Walls that Meteor Golems cannot. Since they only target one unit at a time and having a slow attack speed, splash-damage units like Valkyries and Hero Equipment like the Electro Boots can deal with Skeletons from Skeleton Traps .
Having the Meteor Golems seperated allows the Healers to be more effective in healing the resulting Meteormites, and when they merge, they will have more hitpoints than if healed alone.

Meteor Golems and Meteormites are prone to single-target damage, because of their high health pool and slow attack speed. To prevent this, spells can be used to disable it, like Freeze Spells , Invisibility Spells , Totem Spells , or Overgrowth Spells . The Grand Warden 's Eternal Tome can also be used to negate the damage done to them, especially in the most-damaging part of the base.
At level 2, its body becomes orange and gains five yellow spikes on its head, with the center spike being larger. The eyes and cracks on its body are changed from blue to white.

Frostmite.name: Frostmite
notes: Frostmites are small creatures spawned by Frosty . Similar to Yetimites , they will move quickly to attack the nearest defense, jumping over Walls if needed. They inflict very low damage, but anything it hits will be chilled, slowing them down for a short period.

In the artwork, a Frostmite appears to be a clump of snow molded together, with hollow blue eyes, and has two small arms. In battle, they are periwinkle and their eyes are white in color, and they appear identical to Yetimites . When it attacks, it jumps into the targeted defense (or unit), melting itself in the process.
Frostmites can be useful for distracting single-targeting defenses, as they have relatively high health and can stall the defense with their frost effect.

Frostmites are hard to stop largely due to the fact that they have a good amount of hitpoints and generally will not have to travel far to reach a defense it can damage; oftentimes they will spawn right in front of a defense, and damage is almost unavoidable in that scenario. To combat this, it is best to make sure Frosty and his Hero cannot reach your defenses easily so that the Frostmites will have to travel for longer to reach your defenses.

High-damage defenses focused on Frostmites will be able to destroy them in time, but often these same defenses will be distracted by the Frosty, his Hero or your opponent's main army. Multi-targeting defenses, such as Inferno Towers , Giga Teslas , or Giga Infernos are a great counter to Frostmites. Scattershots are also able to one-shot the Frostmite if it manages a direct hit.

Skeleton.name: Skeleton
notes: Skeletons are sub-troops spawned by the Witch . They are similar to Barbarians in attack damage, but have lower health and move faster.

Skeletons have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Skeletons will proceed to attack the nearest structure.
They can be a good tank for single damage defense buildings in large numbers, but are vulnerable to splash damage.

Skeletons are unable to trigger Traps , nor can they cause the Clan Castle to activate and deploy its troops (if any). However, they can be harmed by traps if another troop triggers them. Skeletons are able to trigger Hidden Teslas even though they are undetectable by traps.
Try to avoid splash damaging defenses (like Wizard Towers and Mortars ) and other multi-targeting defenses (like Inferno Towers set to multi-target) to keep your Skeletons alive.

Skeletons can act as a "bone shield" to Witches , protecting them from other defenses. However, due to having a melee range, they can enter the Mortar's or Scattershot 's blind spot, rendering the Witches vulnerable to those defenses. They also do not trigger traps, rendering the Witch(es) vulnerable as well.
However, due to having a melee range, they can enter the Mortar's or Scattershot 's blind spot, rendering the Witches vulnerable to those defenses.
They also do not trigger traps, rendering the Witch(es) vulnerable as well.
Witches in your Clan Castle spawns Skeletons to assist in defense. In large numbers (spawned by multiple Witches), Skeletons can prove to be overwhelming to attackers.

Single-target defenses like Cannons and Archer Towers can be overwhelmed by Skeletons (especially if the single-target defense cannot one-shot the Skeleton), which means splash-damaging defenses like the Mortar , Wizard Tower and the Bomb Tower are your defense's best chance of eliminating hordes of these sub-troops. Have Mortars, Wizard Towers and Bomb Towers as high-leveled as possible; they can be able to one-shot Skeletons, leaving the Witch vulnerable to the defenses. Inferno Towers set to multi-target mode, Firespitters and the Revenge Tower are also good at eliminating a few Skeletons at a time and able to target the Witch.
Skeletons cannot target air troops, so an army of Minions , a Dragon , or a Baby Dragon inside the Clan Castle can easily clear them.

Spell Skeleton.name: Spell Skeleton

wiki.Description: When the Skeleton's succesfully hit a unit or building

notes: Skeletons are sub-troops spawned by the Skeleton Spell . They are similar to Skeletons spawned by the Witch , but carry armor that gives them an extra layer of hitpoints. When the armor layer is destroyed, the Skeleton simply loses its armor and becomes a regular Skeleton; any excess damage dealt to the armor layer is lost.
They are similar to Barbarians in attack damage, but have lower health and move faster.

Skeletons have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Skeletons will proceed to attack the nearest structure.
They can be a good tank for single damage defense buildings in large numbers, but are vulnerable to splash damage.

Skeletons are unable to trigger Traps , nor can they cause the Clan Castle to activate and deploy its troops (if any). However, they can still trigger Hidden Teslas , and be harmed by traps if another troop triggers them.

Skeletons spawned by the Skeleton Spell do only 15% of its regular damage to resource storages and the Town Hall , which makes them ineffective choices for stealing loot or for quickly destroying the Town Hall.

Try to avoid splash damaging defenses (like Wizard Towers , Bomb Towers , Scattershots , and Mortars ) to keep your Skeletons alive. Even though their armor allows them to survive a single hit, most splash defenses are able to remove the armor in one hit anyway, so they should be avoided.

When combined with a Poison Spell , the Skeletons can be used to distract and/or take down the defending Archer Queen which can be helpful during air attacks. At higher levels, Headhunters generally do the job better, but Skeleton Spells can still be helpful in cases where the Queen is heavily defended by single-target ground defenses (which can kill Headhunters quickly).
Add multiple Skeleton Spells on top of another to create more damage since Skeleton Spells spawn Skeletons quite slowly.

Single-target defenses like Cannons and Archer Towers can be overwhelmed by Skeletons (especially if the single-target defense cannot one-shot the Skeleton), which means splash-damaging defenses like the Wizard Tower and the Bomb Tower are your defense's best chance of eliminating hordes of these sub-troops. Unlike with regular Skeletons, slow-firing splash defenses such as Mortars (and to a lesser extent Scattershots) are less helpful, as the Skeletons' armor allows them to survive a single hit.

Fast-firing defenses like X-Bows , Revenge Tower , Multi-Gear Tower , and multi-target Inferno Towers are useful against the armored Skeletons despite their armor layer. The armor will not be able to carry out its intended purpose of tanking excess damage, since these defenses have low damage per shot and they thus really only give a small amount of extra hitpoints to the Skeleton.

Bat.name: Bat
notes: Bats are summoned by Bat Spells . Unlike their Builder Base counterpart, they target defenses.
Like Skeletons, Bats do not trigger traps or Clan Castle troops .

Bats do 15% of their regular damage to resource buildings. In particular, this affects their interaction with the Town Hall's Giga Tesla and Giga Inferno , as they are considered both a defense and a resource building.

They can be used to cover your troops by distracting and clearing defenses in an area, but due to their low hitpoints they often need cover themselves. Freeze Spells must be used to stop splash or multi-targeting defenses, otherwise the Bats will be killed quickly.

Consider taking out threats to Bats with your other troops before attacking with Bat Spells. Ideally you will want to destroy any Wizard Towers in the planned area of attack (or distract/freeze that tower when the Bats reach it), as well as any multi-target Inferno Towers or Scattershots .

They are also good as a distraction, but the Skeleton Spell is better for this purpose, as the Skeleton Spell spawn Skeletons with shields, which helps them to take more damage, and spawns more Skeletons, thus distracting defenses for longer.

Any defense that deals splash damage will take out Bats easily: Wizard Towers , the Eagle Artillery , Inferno Towers (multi-target), Scattershots , the Giga Tesla , the Giga Inferno , and Air Bombs , as well as anything with fast hitspeeds: Archer Towers (when set to fast attack mode), X-Bow (ground and air), and Hidden Teslas .

Snake.name: Snake
notes: Snakes are that are summoned by the Barbarian King wielding the Snake Bracelet .
In the artwork, the Snake appears to be similar to that of a rattlesnake with a long orange tongue and rattle at the end of its tail, except its skin is green, and have yellow sclerae.

Snake Bracelets have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Snake Bracelets will proceed to attack the nearest structure.
A Snake is summoned every 300 damage the Barbarian King takes, which can distract defenses and help deal damage for him.
Compared to Snakes spawned by the temporary Snake Barrel , Snakes summoned by the Snake Bracelet have more hitpoints, but lower damage per second except at max level (where they are equal).

Snakes are similar in nature to Hog Riders , Headhunters , and Royal Champion , as they can slither over walls by jumping over them. They can come individually or in swarms, and have much less hitpoints than them, making them much more vulnerable to splash. However, they cannot be summoned without the King taking sufficient amounts of damage. However, the Snakes' health can be boosted by the Life Gem from the Grand Warden , increasing their survivability.
However, the Snakes' health can be boosted by the Life Gem from the Grand Warden , increasing their survivability.

If the Barbarian King takes too much damage in a short time (which most likely is under fire from a Monolith or a single-target Inferno Tower, much like the Flying Fortress, he will summon more Snakes than normal.

The summoned Snakes prove to be very valuable when facing against single-target defenses. Not only do they distract them, but they can help damage and can also give time for other units to eventually destroy these defenses, especially the Monoliths .

Against fast-firing and multi-targeting defenses like Inferno Towers , Multi-Archer Towers , Firespitters , and X-Bows , a Healing Spell may be required to keep them alive. Alternatively, the Healing Tome can also do the same thing, as it can heal them back up to full health.
Alternatively, the Healing Tome can also do the same thing, as it can heal them back up to full health.
Against splash defenses such as Wizard Towers , Mortars , Eagle Artillery , and Scattershots , they may easily be taken out due to their high damage.

Keep your splash defenses protected at all costs, as the Snakes will destroy them, especially if they are exposed. High-hitpoint buildings like storages and the Hero Hall can be useful in this matter, as they can soak up the damage, allowing more defenses time to destroy them. However, the Inferno Artillery is able to tank and deal splash damage itself, requiring little to no support.
However, the Inferno Artillery is able to tank and deal splash damage itself, requiring little to no support.

Trap placement is also important, as when placed near defenses in a base, the horde of Snakes will be wiped out, which can usually be a Giant Bomb (sometimes paired with Bombs ), protecting said defense. However, Snakes cannot trigger traps, so make sure a unit comes across the trap to trigger it.

The Poison Bomb at Town Hall 14 is able to wipe out the summoned Snakes, and its poison can deal enough damage to destroy them. Poison Spell Towers can also be used, which make them an effective countermeasure to Snake hordes. At Town Hall 17, the Giga Bomb can do the same, blowing up the Snakes, except without the poison effect.

Super Rider.name: Super Rider
notes: The Super Rider is a subtroop spawned by the Super Hog Rider upon its defeat. When the Super Hog Rider is defeated, the Super Rider is bucked off the Super Hog , and launched several tiles backwards from where the pair was.

The Super Rider, without his hog, can no longer bypass Walls . He instead targets buildings and ground troops indiscriminately. The Super Rider is capable of doing 2x damage to Walls, though this is not marked as his favorite target.
The Super Rider is capable of doing 2x damage to Walls, though this is not marked as his favorite target.

Super Riders have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Super Riders will proceed to attack the nearest structure.
The Super Rider is very useful for cleaning up a base as he can target non-defensive buildings. This reduces the amount of cleanup troops needed after the defenses have been wiped out.
The Super Rider also deals double damage to walls, which, if there are enough of them, can break walls easily.

Because of the mechanics of the Super Hog Rider, it is easy for Super Riders to be stranded inside a compartment, requiring them to break the Walls to continue participation in the attack. As mentioned, a large group can break the Wall quickly, but if only one is present, it may take a long time for him to rejoin the attack. If he is dropped outside the base, the Super Rider may require the assistance of funneling to re-enter the base, though enabling this to happen may not necessarily be a high priority.
If he is dropped outside the base, the Super Rider may require the assistance of funneling to re-enter the base, though enabling this to happen may not necessarily be a high priority.

Super Hog.name: Super Hog
notes: The Super Hog is a subtroop spawned from the Super Hog Rider upon its defeat. When the Super Hog Rider is defeated, the Super Hog stays where it is, while the corresponding Super Rider is launched several tiles backwards.

The Super Hog maintains the traits of the Super Hog Rider, being a defense-targeting troop that is capable of jumping over Walls . However, it does so with a much lower DPS but higher movement speed compared to the Super Hog Rider.

Consider the Super Hog as a mini-tank, as you can drop damage dealers behind the Hogs, as the Super Hogs will tank for them. Think it as a Royal Hog from Clash Royale: Both have a decent amount of HP, low damage, Fast Movement speed, Targets Defenses(Or in the Royal Hog's case, Buildings and Towers),and both Has the Ability to Jump over Walls (In the Royal Hog's case, the River).

Think it as a Royal Hog from Clash Royale: Both have a decent amount of HP, low damage, Fast Movement speed, Targets Defenses(Or in the Royal Hog's case, Buildings and Towers),and both Has the Ability to Jump over Walls (In the Royal Hog's case, the River).

Henchman.name: Henchman
notes: Henchmen are not directly trainable in the Barracks or Dark Barracks . They can only be summoned through the Henchmen Puppet , a Hero Equipment of the Minion Prince .
The Henchmen attack their targets from a short distance, and have relatively low damage per second. They have moderate hitpoints, exceeding that of low-level Minion Princes.

Henchmen have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Henchmen will proceed to attack the nearest structure.

They are a medium-sized tank, and is useful when paired with the invisibility to allow the minion prince to recover some health. However, they have quite low damage, so consider reinforcing them with high-damage air cards to assist them.

Booger.name: Booger
notes: The Booger is a subtroop spawned by Sneezy . It appears to be an off-white, round ghost and booger with a wide, fang-shaped mouth, a single eye with plum iris, an aqua sclera and a black oval-shaped pupil, and dark pink bat wings. It front flips then sneezes on the building to attack.
The Booger is spawned by Sneezy every 10 seconds and a maximum of two can be available at once.

Boogers are unable to trigger Traps, nor can they cause the Clan Castle to activate and deploy its troops (if any). However, they can be harmed by traps if another troop triggers them. Boogers are able to trigger Hidden Teslas even though they are undetectable by traps.

Boogers have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Boogers will proceed to attack the nearest structure.

While Boogers have mediocre damage, they have a rather large amount of health that can provide tanking, especially useful for aerial Heroes like the Minion Prince and the Air Mode Grand Warden , but will fail to trigger Seeking Air Mines and Air Bombs , which could be dangerous for them. Therefore, Balloons are commonly used to provide protection.

Boogers are able to trigger the Clan Castle, which can be a disadvantage, especially if the Clan Castle is filled with Headhunters that would quickly shut down Warden Walks and Charges, so be careful when entering towards the Clan Castle, mostly used with the Fireball .

Since Boogers do not trigger Seeking Air Mines and Air Bombs, it is a good idea to spread them away from each other so that armies like Dragons , Electro Dragons , and Dragon Riders , or even aerial Heroes like the Minion Prince and the Grand Warden will be more vulnerable to them.

Air Bombs.name: Air Bombs
notes: The Air Bombs exclusively targets aerial enemies. It continuously launches explosive barrels, resembling the Air Bomb , at air troops that deal heavy damage in a small area.

Bomb Hive.name: Bomb Hive
notes: The Bomb Hive is always active in battle. It continually attacks even when no units are in range.
The Bomb Hive's modules upgrade its hitpoints, damage, and range. Only one module can be upgraded at a time.

The Bomb Hive is considered to be one of the most dangerous defenses, especially when it comes to damage, exploding both ground and air units at the same time. However, its main weakness is that it cannot attack in other direction rather than diagonally in a straight line, but can easily take out units of not taken care of when they are in range. To prevent this, use Freeze Spells and/or Overgrowth Spells to stop it from attacking, a Totem Spell to tank for the bomblets, or an Ice Block Spell to protect attacking units.

Because the Bomb Hive is always active and the bombs explode on contact even if the enemy is invisible under Invisibility Spell or Spirit Fox , a well placed one can counter Royal Champion Charge as it deals massive amount of damage to both her and the Fox with the splash damage.

Crusher Mortar.name: Crusher Mortar
notes: The Crusher Mortar is a Crafted Defense that can be chosen from the Crafting Station . It combines aspects of the Mortar and Super Bowler , with each projectile being able to bounce up to three targets with splash damage like the latter, and also fires much faster than the former. Like the former defense, the Crusher Mortar has a blind spot, but smaller.
When attacking, the Crusher Mortar rapidly launches large boulders that bounce up to three times, dealing massive splash damage to all ground units in a line. It cannot attack aerial units.

If any troop goes near towards its range when a group attacks it from its blind spot, the splash damage (if sufficiently upgraded) can deal damage to all of them from its blind spot, but does not work if the troops have range differences (i.e. the Wizard , Archer , and Apprentice Warden ).
The Crusher Mortar's modules upgrade its hitpoints, damage, and area splash. Only one module can be upgraded at a time.

Aerial units such as Dragons , Electro Dragons , Dragon Riders , Baby Dragons , and Minion Prince cannot be targeted by the Crusher Mortar, so they can easily destroy it without the risk of receiving significant damage. Be careful of air traps and defenses that target air, though.
The Crusher Mortar can heavily damage ground units, especially when paired with splash defenses and the Rage Spell Tower , which may force the usage of the Eternal Tome .
The Crusher Mortar is unable to target aerial units, which makes it an easy target for them. Protect it by placing single-target and splash anti-air defenses and traps to maximize its protection.

Against ground armies like Root Riders and Valkyries , the Crusher Mortar is able to deal massive damage, especially when supported by the Rage Spell Tower. Use Inferno Towers and Monolith to destroy tanks, and other splash defenses like Scattershots to help the Crusher Mortar destroy any swarms nearby it.
If the troops are big enough, like Root Riders and Heroes , sometimes they can be hit by the same boulder twice with high level splash radius module, dealing even more damage to them.

Flame Spinner.name: Flame Spinner
notes: When attacking, the Flame Spinner constantly shoots out flames in a spiral, clockwise motion that deal heavy area damage to nearby targets and have the ability to fling small troops off the map.

The Flame Spinner is always active in battle. It continually attacks even when no units are in range. However, there is a 4-second cooldown between the end of each burst and the start of the next burst. This cooldown applies at the start of the battle as well.
The Flame Spinner's modules upgrade its hitpoints, damage, and number of projectiles per burst. Only one module can be upgraded at a time.

The angle between successive projectiles is constant at about 16 degrees, provided that the Flame Spinner is not slowed or interrupted mid-burst. Slowing the Flame Spinner increases the angle between the projectiles, whereas freezing the Flame Spinner mid-burst can have it resume its burst at a different angle than normal. If frozen by a max-level Freeze Spell mid-burst, the Flame Spinner will continue its burst at the same angle as it was before it was frozen. This interaction is specific to this Freeze Spell level and lower-level Freeze Spells will not reproduce this result.

If frozen by a max-level Freeze Spell mid-burst, the Flame Spinner will continue its burst at the same angle as it was before it was frozen. This interaction is specific to this Freeze Spell level and lower-level Freeze Spells will not reproduce this result.
The Flame Spinner is considered to be one of the most dangerous defenses, owing to its splash damage. However, you can use Freeze Spells or Overgrowth Spells to stop it from attacking.

The Flame Spinner can be a very dangerous defense, being able to deal with hordes of swarms around it with ease. It is also an effective counter to Super Archer Blimps and other similar strategies, especially if it is placed in the core alongside the Town Hall to prevent a two-star, as Invisibility Spells cannot prevent troops from being hit.
Like the Inferno Artillery , the Flame Spinner is always active while shooting out flame projectiles around it and protects nearby buildings within its range.

The Flame Spinner is weak to longer-ranged units like Flame Flingers and Rocket Spears from the Royal Champion , so protect it with defenses that match or outrange them like Mortars , X-Bows , and Monolith . Traps like Giant Bombs and Skeleton Traps can also help in this regard.

At levels 12, the base gains a taller, second layer of solid stone, connecting the shorter stone bricks. The bricks at the of the dome are now replaced with a metal band, and the cover of the suction compressor is now made out of wood, also encased with a metal band. There are four exhaust pipes, and each one now grows thinner to the end and has an upside-down trapezoidal shape, with an opening of its respective shape, facing more upwards.

At level 30, the cover becomes crown-shaped and becomes a metal grate where excess heat from the lava is released. The exhaust pipes grow larger, become square-shaped and now have metal grates as well. The metal plates of the dome become orange. In addition, the reinforcements of each side of the dome are now doubled and are spaced away from each other.

Hero Bell.name: Hero Bell
notes: The Hero Bell boosts defending Heroes that are in range, increasing their damage and hitpoints.

The boost is activated within a few seconds of the battle loading and rings a few times to notify the attacker, and lasts indefinitely until the Hero Bell is destroyed. The Hero Bell's boost is also lost if a Hero leaves the range of the Hero Bell, although this is unlikely due to the extremely large range of the Bell (50 tiles).
Freezing the Hero Bell with a Freeze Spell or otherwise has no effect on the Hero Bell or the Heroes.

The Hero Bell's modules upgrade its hitpoints, its boosts to hero damage, and its boosts to hero hitpoints. Only one module can be upgraded at a time. The more upgraded the Hero Bell is, the stronger the defending Heroes are, via the damage and health boost modules. Upgrading the hitpoint module will also allow it to increase its durability, boosting Heroes for longer.

The more upgraded the Hero Bell is, the stronger the defending Heroes are, via the damage and health boost modules. Upgrading the hitpoint module will also allow it to increase its durability, boosting Heroes for longer.

To prevent the Hero Bell from being taken out early on by the Giant Arrow, upgrade its health module to level 5. Even if the Hero Bell was taken out by the Fireball and Earthquake Spells, they will retain some health, at the cost of losing the boost.

If it is at the core, use the main army to deal with it, and if the main army was paired with aerial units and/or the Grand Warden's Eternal Tome , Battle Blimps filled with troops like the Super Yeti paired with Clone Spells will easily deal with main defenses and the Hero Bell at the core, provided if the Electromites do not get taken out too early or slowed down.

Even if trapped , frozen , slowed by the Frozen Arrow and/or Frosty , or stunned by a Lightning Spell or Diggy , it will still boost defending Heroes, rendering the status effects useless. The only way for it to disable its ability is to destroy the Hero Bell itself. However, defending Heroes themselves can be affected by most status effects.

Hero Hunter.name: Hero Hunter
notes: The Hero Hunter launches poisonous cards from a cannon, dealing single-target damage against ground and air units . Units that are hit are poisoned and will be slowed down and take extra poison damage, as if they were afflicted by a Poison Spell . Like poison from a Headhunter , the poison damage wears off quickly over time, making it negligible as compared to card damage.

Heroes take double damage from the cards, and they will be prioritised if possible (though they will not be targeted immediately if the Hero Hunter is attacking another troop when a Hero enters its range).

Hook Tower.name: Hook Tower
notes: The Hook Tower grabs a single unit into its blind spot from a long range. The targeted unit takes minimal damage (1 damage per attack; displayed as having 0 damage per second) and is stunned for a period of time. When this attack is done, it retargets to the closest troop. This is evident when it comes to long-range Siege Machines, as after a troop such as a Barbarian is deployed in front of the Flame Flinger for example, the Hook Tower will first target the Flinger and then the Barbarian, so long as the Barbarian does not reach its blind spot.

When this attack is done, it retargets to the closest troop. This is evident when it comes to long-range Siege Machines, as after a troop such as a Barbarian is deployed in front of the Flame Flinger for example, the Hook Tower will first target the Flinger and then the Barbarian, so long as the Barbarian does not reach its blind spot.
Heroes and Pets can be affected as normal. Siege Machines cannot be pulled by the Hook Tower but will still take damage and be stunned.
When the Hook Tower launches its anchor on the target when it is destroyed, it only stuns the target, without reeling it towards its blind spot, and the anchor disappears afterwards.
The Hook Tower's modules upgrade its hitpoints, attack frequency and stun duration. Only one module can be upgraded at a time.

The Hook Tower has a very long range, so make sure to place it near high-damage defenses such as Ricochet Cannons , Multi-Archer Towers , single-target Inferno Towers and the Monolith to deal significant damage to the target, especially a Hero. Traps like Giant Bombs , Seeking Air Mines , and the Giga Bomb can also work in this regard.

The Hook Tower can pick off strong units one by one, which will get stunned and defeated by high-damage defenses. This makes it particularly effective against tanky units, increasing the chances of a successful defense.

The Hook Tower has a disadvantage if the attacker uses Balloons . When it grabs the Balloon, the unit will trigger any air traps along the way, wasting them, so keep that in mind. Another weakness of the Hook Tower is that it can only target one unit, and would be wasted on fragile units like Barbarians , Minions and Archers . Place splash damage defenses near it to allow the Hook Tower to target units with higher hitpoints.

Another weakness of the Hook Tower is that it can only target one unit, and would be wasted on fragile units like Barbarians , Minions and Archers . Place splash damage defenses near it to allow the Hook Tower to target units with higher hitpoints.

If the Grand Warden is somehow targeted by the Hook Tower and displaces him away from the army after he has activated his Eternal Tome , the army will lose their invincibility, putting the attacker at a significant disadvantage.

The Hook Tower can be especially dangerous, especially if the reeled unit is a Hero , and can lure them into dangerous areas of the base with high damage. It also stuns that unit, which allows defenses time to defeat them. To prevent this, use a Freeze or Overgrowth Spells to disable this defense, Invisibility Spells to turn them invisible. Skeleton Spells and Bat Spells can also work in this regard, so long as they are not placed inside its blind spot. However, freezing, stunning or trapping the Hook Tower will not stop it from reeling the targeted unit if it has already fired its anchor, as said unit will be displaced into its blind spot as usual.
However, freezing, stunning or trapping the Hook Tower will not stop it from reeling the targeted unit if it has already fired its anchor, as said unit will be displaced into its blind spot as usual.

The Hook Thrower cannot target invisible units, such as a Royal Champion concealed by the Spirit Fox or troops covered by Invisibility Spells. However, for the Royal Champion Charge, make sure to time the Invisibility Spells and the invisibility from the Spirit Fox at the correct time, otherwise she will be reeled in towards the Hook Tower and stun her as major defenses will take her out prematurely.

However, for the Royal Champion Charge, make sure to time the Invisibility Spells and the invisibility from the Spirit Fox at the correct time, otherwise she will be reeled in towards the Hook Tower and stun her as major defenses will take her out prematurely.

Miners , their super version , Diggy and the Battle Drill cannot be targeted by the Hook Tower while underground, making them great counters. However, the downside to this is that when they surface, they will get reeled in towards its blind spot when they do so, except for the Battle Drill, which can only be stunned instead. The latter two of the aforementioned units above can stun the Hook Tower, giving more time for other troops to destroy it quickly.
However, the downside to this is that when they surface, they will get reeled in towards its blind spot when they do so, except for the Battle Drill, which can only be stunned instead.
The latter two of the aforementioned units above can stun the Hook Tower, giving more time for other troops to destroy it quickly.

At level 30, the metal parts that were retained from its previous appearance, including the anchor, as well as the bronze supports, become golden. The golden supports of the platform gain two small golden spikes each, and the bottom brass line gains a small semi-oval plate on each side with pentagonal rivets holding it in place. The rope is now orange.

Hot Candle.name: Hot Candle
notes: It is a multi-target defense that fires spurts of flames at multiple ground and air troops, similar to a Multi-Archer Tower . Initially, it can target up to 6 different targets, however after two set intervals of time, it melts slightly, decreasing its damage potential each time. The number of fired spurts decreases to four after its first melt, then to three after its second. Each spurt still does the same amount of damage, however. The Hot Candle starts melting as soon as any building is destroyed.
Like the Multi-Archer Tower, the Hot Candle can hit the same target with multiple shots, stacking its damage on that target.
If there are six or more units in range, each flame targets the six nearest ones.
If there are five units in range, two flames hit the nearest unit, while the others will be hit by one.
If there are four units in range, two flames will target the two closest ones, while the rest will be shot by one.
If there are three units in its range, two flames will each target three units, spreading the damage equally. The same applies to two units in its range, except three flames will target each one.
The same applies to two units in its range, except three flames will target each one.
If there is only one unit in its range, all six flames will hit that unit.

The Hot Candle is one of the most effective defenses against swarms because of its multi-targeting capability and high attack speed similar to an Archer Tower . Because of this, it can be placed in a compartment of the base filled with Traps and other major defenses.

The Hot Candle is weak to longer-ranged units like Flame Flingers and Rocket Spears from the Royal Champion , so protect it with defenses that match or outrange them like Mortars , X-Bows , and the Monolith . Traps like Giant Bombs and Skeleton Traps can also help in this regard.

Keep the Hot Candle separated from other main defenses such as Scattershots and Inferno Towers , otherwise the attacker will get a lot of value by disabling them all using the Overgrowth Spell or Freeze Spell .

When attacking a Hot Candle with a large number of troops, the resulting interaction will play out similar to attacking a multi-targeting Inferno Tower initially, though it decreases as time passes. However, against single units such as a lone Royal Champion or Archer Queen , the Hot Candle will prove to be very potent, with damage per second exceeding that of most other single-target defenses like the X-Bow or a fast-attack Archer Tower.

To prevent the Hot Candle from targeting all important units at once, one can prevent them from being targeted by using an Invisibility Spell . Freeze Spells and Overgrowth Spells are a staple to disable the defense, if it should be required. Totem Spells are also effective, as it can reduce the damage output.

Lava Launcher.name: Lava Launcher
notes: Like its Builder Base counterpart, the Lava Launcher launches powerful molten balls of lava that do a small amount of damage on impact and leaves the ground scorched, which inflicts damage-over-time effect called burn damage on ground troops. The effect of the lava remains for 20 seconds after impact. Unlike the effects of defensive Poison Spell , the burn damage ticks at a flat rate and multiple lava pools can stack their damage without penalty. The burn damage can be boosted by defensive Rage Spell like Rage Spell Tower and Smasher or Super Valkyrie's death rage, unlike defensive Poison effects.
The burn damage can be boosted by defensive Rage Spell like Rage Spell Tower and Smasher or Super Valkyrie's death rage, unlike defensive Poison effects.
The Lava Launcher's modules upgrade its hitpoints, damage, and range. Only one module can be upgraded at a time.

The Lava Launcher is a very powerful defense that must not be underestimated. Because of its extremely long range, it can outrange Royal Champions with active Rocket Spears and Flame Flingers . To prevent this, use Freeze or Overgrowth Spells to stop it from attacking, Totem Spells to redirect its attacks away from the main army, Ice Block Spells to protect units, or Rage Spells and Haste Spells to help units reach its blind spot and destroy it. Hero abilities like the Stun Blaster and Pets like Diggy can also help in this regard.

To prevent this, use Freeze or Overgrowth Spells to stop it from attacking, Totem Spells to redirect its attacks away from the main army, Ice Block Spells to protect units, or Rage Spells and Haste Spells to help units reach its blind spot and destroy it. Hero abilities like the Stun Blaster and Pets like Diggy can also help in this regard.

The Lava Launcher can heavily damage ground units, especially when paired with splash defenses and the Rage Spell Tower, which may force the usage of the Eternal Tome if not taken care of. If the attacker's option of attacking is by ground, usually in Legend League Tournaments , then the best way to proceed would be to distract the Lava Launcher with expendable units such as a Totem from the Totem Spell, and ensure it fires away from the line of attack until the main attacking force has safely entered the Lava Launcher's blind spot. If done correctly, the lava will not impede the attack's progress.
Tanks like Golems are also useful as their very high health means that they can survive for much longer in the lava compared to other troops.
Ground Heroes like the Barbarian King are minimally affected by the fire damage over time effect, so having the King be targeted will minimize the damage of the Lava Launcher.

Aerial units such as Dragons , Electro Dragons , Dragon Riders , Baby Dragons , the Minion Prince and Dragon Duke cannot be targeted by the Lava Launcher, so they can easily destroy it without the risk of receiving significant damage. Be careful of air traps and defenses that target air, though.

The Lava Launcher can prove to be a very powerful defense because of its extremely long range. Because of this, most players would place it behind the Town Hall to deal with Warden Charges with the help of the Longshot and defenses, even when the Grand Warden and the Healers are boosted with Rage Spells due to the high damage over time, provided it has enough range. It can also be placed in the core to maximize its potential, in a way that it can mess up troop pathing and therefore may not reach it. In addition, separate it from other major defenses to prevent high value in ZapQuake attacks or the Fireball with Earthquake Spells .

Often it is not the damage of the lava shot itself that is devastating, but rather the massive damage from the damage over time effect of the resulting lava. The lava can easily make short work of many smaller troops, such as Barbarians , Archers , Witches , and other similar units. To increase the chances of this happening, it is often advantageous to stall attacking troops behind Walls so that they will stay in the lava for as long as possible, racking up damage, but make sure that the Walls can cover the Lava Launcher's blind spot. It is also useful to protect these Walls as Super Wall Breakers can easily clear them, allowing for other troops to rush into the blind spot.
It is also useful to protect these Walls as Super Wall Breakers can easily clear them, allowing for other troops to rush into the blind spot.

The biggest weakness of the Lava Launcher is its blind spot. Cover it with other major defenses to protect it and try to use traps to keep troops in the range of the Launcher, as many troops, especially melee units, can easily reach the blind spot if there is no protection and to deal with aerial units, as it cannot target them.

Light Beam.name: Light Beam
notes: The Light Beam is a Crafted Defense that can be chosen from the Crafting Station . It is a single-target long-range defense that shoots balls of light to attack.

The Light Beam does full damage to targets within 5 tiles of it (damage is calculated at the point of impact, not where the target was when the light ball was fired). However, beyond that distance, the light balls will have reduced damage, down to a minimum of 30% of the original damage at the edge of the range. If a target moves out of range, the light ball will miss entirely.

Against swarms of medium to high-health troops like Dragons , Hog Riders , and Valkyries , if sufficiently-leveled, the Light Beam can rival the power of the Monolith . However, it may be less effective on higher-hitpoint units like Meteor Golems , Lava Hounds , and P.E.K.K.As , as they will be able to tank them, as the latter defense is more effective in taking them out regardless of hitpoints.

Not only can the Light Beam be dangerous for long-range units, including Flame Flingers, but it also deals increased damage when attacking units are close enough. Pair this with high-enough attack speed and damage module levels and this defense can snipe them off more effectively. It can also be placed in areas of the base where Flame Flingers are most likely to be deployed from.

To prevent this defense from wreaking havoc onto the attacking army, use Freeze and Overgrowth Spells to stop it from attacking, Ice Block Spells to protect attacking units in its range, Rage Spells to destroy this defense quickly before it deals too much damage, and Totem Spells to redirect its attacks away from the army.

Portal Pendant.name: Portal Pendant

raw.Unlock Requirement: Buy in Portal Panic event for 3,100

notes: When activated, the Minion Prince pulls the nearby ally Troops , Heroes , and Pets in its area of effect back onto the Minion Prince deployment bar, allowing them to be re-deployed elsewhere (subject to the deployment zones of the village). Upon being redeployed, units gain extra health and a haste effect. Siege Machines cannot be recalled.
Note that the Hero priority does not extend to Pets, which may be separated from their Hero if other high-housing space troops are recalled.

Units that are recalled will retain their current status effects that were afflicted on them when they are recalled, but prior spell effects will generally wear off since they may be redeployed outside the spell radius, and most status timers will count down while the unit is pending redeployment. Exceptions to this rule include clone lifetimes (for clones from the Clone Spell ), the Angry effect from the Angry Jelly and Angry Spell , active Hero Equipment effect timers (such as Rage Vial and Eternal Tome ), and revival timers (for Heroes being temporarily revived by Phoenix), all of which are paused while pending redeployment.
In addition to the ability, it grants health recovery to the Minion Prince.

Roaster.name: Roaster
notes: The Roaster launches a rapid burst of damaging flames that deal splash damage, with a short delay between each burst. The splash damage can only target either ground or air, based on the initial target.
The Roaster's modules upgrade its hitpoints, damage, and number of projectiles per burst. Only one module can be upgraded at a time.
At level 21, the stone base's second layer is replaced by a golden band, the ladder becomes gold, and the muzzle grows wider.

At level 30, the stone box is replaced with a bellows surrounded by a thin metal frame with several bolts fitted in. The bellows will repeatedly blow air into the Roaster approximately every half second. A shorter pipe has been added above the longer one that connects to the timer.
* These damage per second values are seen in-game and are approximations; it does not necessarily do this much DPS if it cannot utilize the full potential of its bursts.
